**`CatSitOnBlockGoal(cat, speed)`** (CatSitOnBlockGoal.txt 1–197):
`MoveToBlockGoal(cat, speed, 8)`; `canUse` needs tame and not ordered to sit; `start` and
`stop` clear the sitting pose; `tick` sets it to `isReachedTarget()`; `isValidTarget`
(68–116): the block above empty, the block `#cats_can_sit_on`, then the first matching
rule of three: a chest with `ChestBlockEntity.getOpenCount(level, pos) < 1`; a furnace
that is lit; a bed whose part is not the head (so the foot); anything else of the tag:
true.

**`FleeSunGoal(mob, speed)`** (FleeSunGoal.txt 1–181), the fox's shelter seeking (its
`SeekShelterGoal` extends it). Flags MOVE. `canUse` (35–75): no target;
`level.isBrightOutside()`; on fire; `level.canSeeSky(blockPosition())`; nothing on the
head; `setWantedPos()` (`getHidePos()` not null). `getHidePos` (129–180): up to ten
tries, each `p = blockPosition().offset(nextInt(20) − 10, nextInt(6) − 3, nextInt(20) −
10)` (three draws, in that order); the first with `!canSeeSky(p)` and
`getWalkTargetValue(p) < 0` is returned as `atBottomCenterOf` (an early exit: draws stop).
`start`: `moveTo(wanted, speed)`; continues while the navigation is not done.
`Level.isBrightOutside()` (Level.txt 656–669) is `!dimensionType().hasFixedTime() &&
skyDarken < 4`, with `skyDarken = (int)(15f − the dimension's value of the environment
attribute sky_light_level)` (`updateSkyBrightness`, 1185–1198), a function of the time of
day, not of light at a position. `canSeeSky(pos)` is `BlockAndTintGetter`'s (not dumped:
12.2; it needs the sky light, N8).

**`ClimbOnTopOfPowderSnowGoal(mob, level)`** (ClimbOnTopOfPowderSnowGoal.txt 1–84). Flags
JUMP; every tick. `canUse` (23–71): (`wasInPowderSnow || isInPowderSnow`) and the type
is `#powder_snow_walkable_mobs` (rabbit, endermite, silverfish, fox in 26.3); the block
above the mob's is powder snow or has the empty collision shape (`== Shapes.empty()`, an
identity test). `tick`: `jumpControl.jump()`.

**`JumpGoal`** (JumpGoal.txt 1–13): abstract, flags MOVE, JUMP. **`DolphinJumpGoal(dolphin,
interval)`** (DolphinJumpGoal.txt 1–348): `interval = reducedTickDelay(interval)`; not
interruptable. `canUse` (24–83): one `nextInt(interval)` must be 0; `d =
getMotionDirection()` (`Entity`'s is `getDirection()`, the horizontal facing of
its yaw, Entity.txt 9955–9959, unless the dolphin overrides it); for each step `n` of `{0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7}`: the block at `pos +
(d.x·n, 0, d.z·n)` is water and not `#blocks_dolphin_jump`, and the blocks one and two
above it are air. `start` (198–227): motion += `(d.x·0.6, 0.7, d.z·0.6)`;
`navigation.stop()`. `canContinueToUse` (154–192): false when `motion.y² <
0.029999999329447746`, `xRot != 0`, `|xRot| < 10` and in water; else `!onGround()`.
`stop`: `xRot = 0`. `tick` (236–347): if not yet `breached`, `breached` = the fluid at its
block is water; on the first `breached`, `playSound(DOLPHIN_JUMP, 1, 1)`; then if
`motion.y² < 0.0299…` and `xRot != 0`: `xRot = Mth.rotLerp(0.2f, xRot, 0)`; else if
`motion.length() > 9.999999747378752E-6`: `xRot = (float)(Math.atan2(−motion.y,
horizontalDistance) × 57.2957763671875)` (finding 7). `breached` is never cleared
(finding 14).

### 2.8 Goals that look

**`LookAtPlayerGoal(mob, type, lookDistance[, probability = 0.02f[, onlyHorizontal =
false]])`** (LookAtPlayerGoal.txt 1–280). Flags LOOK. The conditions (42–88):
`forNonCombat().range(lookDistance)`, and for `type == Player.class` also the selector
`EntitySelector.notRiding(mob)` (a player whose chain of vehicles contains the mob is not
looked at; EntitySelector.txt (n5) 63–84). Line of sight and invisibility are tested
(the defaults).

- `canUse` (89–177): one `nextFloat()`; false if `>= probability`. (If the mob has a
  target it is assigned to `lookAt` and at once overwritten: finding 14.) For players:
  `lookAt = level.getNearestPlayer(conditions, mob, x, getEyeY(), z)`; for another type:
  `getNearestEntity(level.getEntitiesOfClass(type, getBoundingBox().inflate(lookDistance,
  3.0, lookDistance), always), conditions, mob, x, getEyeY(), z)`. True when found.
- `canContinueToUse` (179–208): `lookAt` alive, `distanceToSqr(lookAt) <= (double)
  (lookDistance × lookDistance)` (a `float` product), and `lookTime > 0`. (Conditions are
  not tested again: a player who turns invisible is still looked at.)
- `start` (210–224): `lookTime = adjustedTickDelay(40 + nextInt(40))` (20 to 40 selector
  ticks: 40 to 80 ticks).
- `stop`: `lookAt = null`. `tick` (232–268): if `lookAt` is alive,
  `lookControl.setLookAt(lookAt.x, onlyHorizontal ? mob.getEyeY() : lookAt.getEyeY(),
  lookAt.z)` (the default speeds 10 and 40), `lookTime −= 1`.
- Draws: a `nextFloat` in every selector tick it is asked (not running and LOOK free or
  held by a higher number); `nextInt(40)` at start.

The search's distance is from the mob's eyes (`getNearestPlayer(…, x, eyeY, z)`), the
range test of the conditions from its feet.

**`InteractGoal(mob, type, lookDistance[, probability])`** (InteractGoal.txt 1–31): a
`LookAtPlayerGoal` with flags LOOK and MOVE (it holds the mob still while it looks; the
wandering trader's, N10).

**`RandomLookAroundGoal(mob)`** (RandomLookAroundGoal.txt 1–110). Flags MOVE, LOOK
(it stops walking while it runs); every tick. `canUse` (25–38): one `nextFloat() <
0.02f`. `canContinueToUse`: `lookTime >= 0`. `start` (49–76): `a = 6.283185307179586 ×
nextDouble()`; `relX = Math.cos(a)`, `relZ = Math.sin(a)` (HotSpot's, finding 7);
`lookTime = 20 + nextInt(20)`. `tick` (82–109): `lookTime −= 1`;
`lookControl.setLookAt(x + relX, getEyeY(), z + relZ)`. Draws: a `nextFloat` per asked
selector tick, `nextDouble` and `nextInt(20)` at start. Lasts 21 to 40 ticks.

**`BegGoal(wolf, lookDistance)`** (BegGoal.txt 1–192). Flags LOOK. Conditions
`forNonCombat().range(lookDistance)` (line of sight and invisibility tested). `canUse`
(41–62): `player = level.getNearestPlayer(conditions, wolf)` (from its feet) and
`playerHoldingInteresting(player)` (157–191: in the main hand or the off hand, in that
order, a bone or an item the wolf `isFood`; no tame test). `canContinueToUse` (63–98):
the player alive, within `lookDistance²` (float product), `lookTime > 0`, still holding
it. `start`: `wolf.setIsInterested(true)` (synched data, the wolf's section), `lookTime =
adjustedTickDelay(40 + nextInt(40))`. `stop`: not interested, `player = null`. `tick`:
`setLookAt(player.x, player.getEyeY(), player.z, 10, maxHeadXRot)`, `lookTime −= 1`.

### 2.9 Goals between animals, and with players

**`BreedGoal(animal, speed[, partnerClass = animal.getClass()])`** (BreedGoal.txt
1–225). Flags MOVE, LOOK. `PARTNER_TARGETING = forNonCombat().range(8).ignoreLineOfSight()`
(217–224).

- `canUse` (51–70): `animal.isInLove()`; `partner = getFreePartner()` not null.
- `getFreePartner` (150–205): `level.getNearbyEntities(partnerClass, PARTNER_TARGETING,
  animal, getBoundingBox().inflate(8))`; of those that `animal.canMate(other)` (the
  animal section: same type, both in love, not itself) and are not panicking, the
  nearest by `distanceToSqr` (strictly closer from `Double.MAX_VALUE`: ties to the
  earlier).
- `canContinueToUse` (71–93): partner alive, in love, `loveTime < 60`, not panicking.
- `tick` (104–149): `lookControl.setLookAt(partner, 10, maxHeadXRot)`;
  `navigation.moveTo(partner, speed)` (in every selector tick); `loveTime += 1`; if
  `loveTime >= adjustedTickDelay(60)` (30) and `distanceToSqr(partner) < 9`: `breed()`
  (`animal.spawnChildFromBreeding(level, partner)`, 206–215, the animal section).
- `stop`: `partner = null`, `loveTime = 0`.
- Both animals run the goal; whichever breeds first resets both lovers (the animal
  section), which ends the other's goal at its next `canContinueToUse`. No draws in the
  goal.

**`TemptGoal(mob, speed, items, canScare[, stopDistance = 2.5])`** (TemptGoal.txt 1–349).
Flags MOVE, LOOK. Conditions: `TEMPT_TARGETING` = `forNonCombat().ignoreLineOfSight()`
(343–348), copied per goal with the selector `shouldFollow` (126–144: the item in the
main hand or the off hand matches `items`).

- `canUse` (90–125): if `calmDown > 0`: `calmDown −= 1`, false. `player =
  level.getNearestPlayer(conditions.range(tempt_range), mob)` (the attribute, 10 by
  default, re-read each time; from the mob's feet); true when found.
- `canContinueToUse` (145–226): if `canScare()`: within 6 blocks (`distanceToSqr(player)
  < 36`), false if the player moved since it was last noted (`player.distanceToSqr(px,
  py, pz) > 0.010000000000000002`) or turned (`|xRot − pRotX| > 5` or `|yRot − pRotY| >
  5`, in double); farther than 6, `px, py, pz` are noted afresh; `pRotX`, `pRotY` are
  noted afresh in both cases. Then `canUse()` (the nearest tempting player, which may be
  another player now).
- `start` (233–254): notes `px, py, pz`, `isRunning = true`. (`pRotX`/`pRotY` are not
  noted at start: the first scared check compares with what an earlier run left, 0 at
  first.)
- `tick` (271–309): `lookControl.setLookAt(player, maxHeadYRot + 20, maxHeadXRot)`; if
  `distanceToSqr(player) < stopDistance²` (6.25): `stopNavigation()` (`navigation.stop()`),
  else `navigateTowards(player)` (`navigation.moveTo(player, speed)`, 318–329), in every
  selector tick.
- `stop` (255–270): `player = null`, `stopNavigation()`, `calmDown =
  reducedTickDelay(100)` (50 asked selector ticks), `isRunning = false`.
- `TemptGoal$ForNonPathfinders` (TemptGoal$ForNonPathfinders.txt 1–53): stops by
  `moveControl.setWait()` and moves by `moveControl.setWantedPosition(mob.position() +
  (player.getEyePosition() − mob.position()) × nextDouble(), speed)` (a draw per
  selector tick; the happy ghast's and others', sections 5 and 6).
- No draws in `TemptGoal` itself.

**`FollowParentGoal(animal, speed)`** (FollowParentGoal.txt 1–174). No flags (0: the
constructor sets none). Constants 8, 4, 3. `canUse` (29–100): the animal is a baby
(`getAge() < 0`); among `level.getEntitiesOfClass(animal.getClass(), getBoundingBox()
.inflate(8, 4, 8))` the adults (`getAge() >= 0`), the nearest by `distanceToSqr`, taking
a candidate when `d <= best` (**ties to the later**); none, or nearest closer than 3
(`d < 9`): false. `canContinueToUse` (101–133): still a baby, parent alive, `9 <= d <=
256`. `start`: `timeToRecalcPath = 0`. `tick` (148–173): `timeToRecalcPath −= 1`; when it
reaches 0 or below: `timeToRecalcPath = adjustedTickDelay(10)` (5) and
`navigation.moveTo(parent, speed)`. `stop`: `parent = null`. No draws.

Note that `FollowParentGoal` has no flags at all: it runs beside whatever holds MOVE, and
its `moveTo` every 10 ticks competes with a stroll's path (the later `moveTo` wins until
the next).

**`FollowOwnerGoal(tamable, speed, startDistance, stopDistance)`** (FollowOwnerGoal.txt
1–209). Flags MOVE, LOOK. The constructor throws unless the navigation is ground or
flying (44–57). `canUse` (59–94): owner not null; not `unableToMoveToOwner()`
(TamableAnimal.txt 673–694: ordered to sit, a passenger, leashed (`mayBeLeashed`), or the
owner a spectator); `distanceToSqr(owner) >= startDistance²` (float product). Continues
(95–126) while the navigation is not done, not unable, and `distanceToSqr(owner) >
stopDistance²`. `start` (127–144): `timeToRecalcPath = 0`; the WATER malus noted and set
to 0. `stop`: `owner = null`, `navigation.stop()`, the WATER malus put back. `tick`
(161–208): `teleport = shouldTryTeleportToOwner()` (TamableAnimal.txt 524–541: owner within
`distanceToSqr >= 144`, 12 blocks or more); unless teleporting, `setLookAt(owner, 10,
maxHeadXRot)`; `timeToRecalcPath −= 1`, and at 0 or below `= adjustedTickDelay(10)` (5)
then `tryToTeleportToOwner()` if teleporting, else `navigation.moveTo(owner, speed)`.
`tryToTeleportToOwner` (511–522) → `teleportToAroundBlockPos(owner.blockPosition())`
(543–595): up to ten tries of `dx = nextIntBetweenInclusive(−3, 3)`, `dz =
nextIntBetweenInclusive(−3, 3)` (two draws); if both `|dx| < 2` and `|dz| < 2` the try is
skipped (no third draw); else `dy = nextIntBetweenInclusive(−1, 1)` and
`maybeTeleportTo(x + dx, y + dy, z + dz)` (597–630: if `canTeleportTo` (632–671: the
static path type is WALKABLE, the block below is not leaves unless the type can fly to
its owner, and the mob's box moved there has no collision), `snapTo(x + 0.5, y, z + 0.5,
yRot, xRot)` and `navigation.stop()`; the first success ends it).
`nextIntBetweenInclusive(a, b)` is `nextInt(b − a + 1) + a` (RandomSource.txt 54–65).

**`SitWhenOrderedToGoal(tamable)`** (SitWhenOrderedToGoal.txt 1–100). Flags JUMP, MOVE.
`canUse` (26–80): `ordered = isOrderedToSit()`; false if neither ordered nor tame (an
untamed animal never sits); false in water or off the ground; owner null or in another
level: `true`; owner within 12 blocks (`distanceToSqr < 144`) and hurt by a mob
(`owner.getLastHurtByMob() != null`): false; else `ordered`. Continues while ordered to
sit. `start`: `navigation.stop()`, `setInSittingPose(true)`; `stop`: pose false.

**`FollowMobGoal(mob, speed, stopDistance, areaSize)`** (FollowMobGoal.txt 1–339), the
parrot's. Flags MOVE, LOOK; ground or flying navigation only. The predicate (328–338): a
mob of another class than this one. `canUse` (65–106): of
`level.getEntitiesOfClass(Mob, getBoundingBox().inflate(areaSize), predicate)` the first
that is not invisible (list order; no distance test). Continues (107–133) while it is
there, the navigation is not done and `distanceToSqr > stopDistance²` (float product).
`start`/`stop` as `FollowOwnerGoal`'s water malus. `tick` (168–327): nothing if
following none or leashed; `setLookAt(following, 10, maxHeadXRot)`; every 5 selector
ticks (`adjustedTickDelay(10)`): `d² = (mob − following)²`; if `d² > stopDistance²`:
`moveTo(following, speed)`; else `navigation.stop()` and, if `d² <= stopDistance` (not
squared) or the followed mob's look control wants exactly the follower's position (x, y
and z equal), step away: `moveTo(x − (fx − x), y, z − (fz − z), speed)`. No draws.

**`FollowFlockLeaderGoal(fish)`** (FollowFlockLeaderGoal.txt 1–180), schooling fish
(section 6). No flags. The constructor draws: `nextStartTick = nextStartTick(fish)`
(11–37: `reducedTickDelay(200 + nextInt(200) % 20)`, 100 to 110) — **a draw when the
goals are built**, that is when the entity is made or loaded. `canUse` (38–107): false if
the fish has followers; true if it follows; while `nextStartTick > 0`: `−1`, false; else
draw `nextStartTick` again, and among `getEntitiesOfClass(fish.getClass(),
getBoundingBox().inflate(8))` the leader is the first (`findAny` of a sequential stream,
**Inferred** first) that `canBeFollowed() || !isFollower()`, else the fish itself;
`leader.addFollowers(the stream of those that are not followers)`; returns
`isFollower()`. Continues (108–122) while following and `inRangeOfLeader()`. `start`:
`timeToRecalcPath = 0`; `stop`: `stopFollowing()`; `tick` (137–157): every 5 selector
ticks `pathToLeader()` (the fish's section).

**`LlamaFollowCaravanGoal(llama, speed)`** (LlamaFollowCaravanGoal.txt 1–353). Flags
MOVE; caravan limit 8. `canUse` (27–157): not leashed, not in a caravan; `list =
level.getEntities(llama, getBoundingBox().inflate(9, 4, 9), llama or trader llama)`
(339–352); first pass, the nearest that is in a caravan and has no tail; if none, second
pass, the nearest leashed one with no tail (both passes: `d > best` skips, so ties to the
later); none → false; `d < 4` → false; the chosen must be leashed or `firstIsLeashed(it,
1)` (313–338: walks up the caravan heads, at most 8 deep, true at the first leashed);
then `llama.joinCaravan(chosen)`, true. `canContinueToUse` (158–221): in a caravan, the
head alive, `firstIsLeashed(llama, 0)`; `d = distanceToSqr(head)`; if `d > 676` (26
blocks): with `speedModifier <= 3`, `speedModifier ×= 1.2`, `distCheckCounter =
reducedTickDelay(40)` (20) and true; else false if `distCheckCounter == 0`; then
`distCheckCounter −= 1` if positive, true. `stop`: `leaveCaravan()`, `speedModifier = 2.1`.
`tick` (232–312): nothing unless in a caravan and not held by a fence knot; `v = (head −
llama).normalize() × max(distanceTo(head) − 2, 0)` (the float distance widened);
`navigation.moveTo(llama + v, speedModifier)` in every selector tick. No draws.

**`LandOnOwnersShoulderGoal(parrot)`** (LandOnOwnersShoulderGoal.txt 1–117). No flags;
interruptable only while not on the shoulder (62–71). `canUse` (16–61): the owner is a
`ServerPlayer` that is not a spectator, not flying (`abilities.flying`), not in water,
not in powder snow; the parrot is not ordered to sit and `canSitOnShoulder()` (the
parrot's section). `start`: `isSittingOnShoulder = false`. `tick` (79–116): unless on
the shoulder, in the sitting pose or leashed: if the owner is a `ServerPlayer` whose box
meets the parrot's, `isSittingOnShoulder = parrot.setEntityOnShoulder(owner)` (the
parrot is removed and kept as data on the player). Continues as `canUse` (the default).
A creative player who flies never gets a parrot.

**`FollowPlayerRiddenEntityGoal(mob, type)`** (FollowPlayerRiddenEntityGoal.txt 1–298),
the dolphin's (`AbstractBoat`, the dolphin's section). No flags; interruptable. `canUse`
(25–75): the player followed has moved horizontally recently (`hasMovedHorizontallyRecently`,
the player's), or any entity of the type within `getBoundingBox().inflate(5)` whose
controlling passenger is a player that has. `start` (99–144): the first such entity's
controlling player is followed (in list order; note it does not test movement here);
`timeToRecalcPath = 0`; state `GO_TO_ENTITY`. Continues while the player is a passenger
and has moved recently. `tick` (152–297): `moveRelative(GO_IN_ENTITY_DIRECTION ? 0.01f :
0.015f, (xxa, yya, zza))`, `move(SELF, motion)` (a second move, as `BreathAirGoal`'s);
every 5 selector ticks: `GO_TO_ENTITY`: `moveTo(the block behind the player
(blockPosition().relative(getDirection().getOpposite())) one down, 1.0)`, and when
`distanceTo(player) < 4` switch to `GO_IN_ENTITY_DIRECTION` with the timer at 0;
`GO_IN_ENTITY_DIRECTION`: `moveTo(the block 10 ahead in the player's motion direction,
one down, 1.0)`, and when farther than 12, back to `GO_TO_ENTITY` with the timer at 0.

### 2.10 Goals of one kind of animal

**`EatBlockGoal(mob)`** (EatBlockGoal.txt 1–217), the sheep's. Flags MOVE, LOOK, JUMP.
`IS_EDIBLE` is `#minecraft:edible_for_sheep` (205–216). `canUse` (32–75): one
`nextInt(adjustedTickDelay(isBaby() ? 50 : 1000))` (25 or 500) must be 0; then true if the
block at `blockPosition()` is edible, or the block below is a grass block. `start`
(76–94): `eatAnimationTick = adjustedTickDelay(40)` (20); `level.broadcastEntityEvent(mob,
10)` (the client's eating animation); `navigation.stop()`. `canContinueToUse`:
`eatAnimationTick > 0`. `stop`: 0. `tick` (118–204), every selector tick:
`eatAnimationTick = max(0, eatAnimationTick − 1)`; when it equals `adjustedTickDelay(4)`
(2): if the block at the mob's position is edible: with `mobGriefing`,
`level.destroyBlock(pos, false)` (no drops); `mob.ate()` in either case; else if the
block below is a grass block: with `mobGriefing`, `levelEvent(2001, below,
Block.getId(GRASS_BLOCK default))` and `setBlock(below, DIRT default, 2)`; `ate()` in
either case. Timing: started at selector tick 0 and ticked in it (20 → 19), it eats at
the selector tick that takes it to 2, the 18th, 34 ticks after the start, and ends two
selector ticks later. Draws: the `nextInt` per asked selector tick.

**`RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal(horse, speed)`** (RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal.txt 1–176). Flags
MOVE. `canUse` (29–69): not mob controlled, not tamed, ridden (`isVehicle()`);
`DefaultRandomPos.getPos(horse, 5, 4)` not null. `start`: `moveTo(pos, speed)`.
Continues while untamed, the navigation not done and ridden. `tick` (107–175): if
untamed, one `nextInt(adjustedTickDelay(50))` (25); when 0: the first passenger; none →
nothing; a player: `t = getTemper()`, `m = getMaxTemper()`; if `m > 0` and `nextInt(m) <
t`: `tameWithName(player)` and done; else `modifyTemper(5)`; then for any passenger,
`ejectPassengers()`, `makeMad()`, `broadcastEntityEvent(horse, 6)`. (The horse's section
has the temper.)

**`RandomStandGoal(horse)`** (RandomStandGoal.txt 1–100). No flags; every tick. The
constructor sets `nextStand = −getAmbientStandInterval()` (7–18, 87–95). `canUse`
(47–86): `nextStand += 1` (in every asked selector tick); if `nextStand > 0` and
`nextInt(1000) < nextStand`: reset to `−getAmbientStandInterval()`, then true when not
immobile and `nextInt(10) == 0`; else false. `canContinueToUse` false (it stops at the
next clean-up). `start`: `standIfPossible()`, and the stand sound
(`getAmbientStandSound()`, at the horse's volume and pitch) if any. Draws: `nextInt(1000)`
once `nextStand` is positive, `nextInt(10)` after a reset.

**`UseItemGoal(mob, item, finishSound, predicate)`** (UseItemGoal.txt 1–85), the
wandering trader's (N10). No flags. `canUse`: the predicate; continues while
`isUsingItem()`. `start`: the main hand gets `item.copy()`, `startUsingItem(MAIN_HAND)`.
`stop`: the main hand emptied; if a sound: `playSound(sound, 1.0f, nextFloat()·0.2f +
0.9f)` (one draw).

### 2.11 Goals of fleeing and fighting

**`AvoidEntityGoal(mob, class, [avoidPredicate,] maxDist, walkSpeed, sprintSpeed[,
predicateOnAvoidEntity])`** (AvoidEntityGoal.txt 1–275). Flags MOVE. The conditions
(38–82): **`forCombat()`**`.range(maxDist).selector(e -> predicateOnAvoidEntity(e) &&
avoidPredicate(e))` (256–270); the defaults are `NO_CREATIVE_OR_SPECTATOR` and "any". So
a creative player is never avoided (finding 1), and line of sight and invisibility are
tested.

- `canUse` (96–190): `toAvoid = level.getNearestEntity(level.getEntitiesOfClass(class,
  getBoundingBox().inflate(maxDist, 3.0, maxDist), always), conditions, mob, x, y, z)`
  (from the feet); none → false; `pos = DefaultRandomPos.getPosAway(mob, 16, 7,
  toAvoid.position())`; null → false; if `toAvoid.distanceToSqr(pos) <
  toAvoid.distanceToSqr(mob)` (the place is nearer the threat) → false; `path =
  navigation.createPath(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z, 0)`; true when a path.
- `canContinueToUse`: the navigation is not done. `start`: `navigation.moveTo(path,
  walkSpeed)`. `stop`: `toAvoid = null`.
- `tick` (221–245), every selector tick: `navigation.setSpeedModifier(distanceToSqr
  (toAvoid) < 49 ? sprintSpeed : walkSpeed)`.
- Draws: `getPosAway`'s, only when something to avoid is found.

**`MeleeAttackGoal(mob, speed, followingTargetEvenIfNotSeen)`** (MeleeAttackGoal.txt
1–433). Flags MOVE, LOOK; every tick. Constants: attack interval 20, a `canUse` at most
every 20 game ticks.

- `canUse` (50–104): `now = level.getGameTime()`; if `now − lastCanUseCheck < 20`: false;
  `lastCanUseCheck = now`; target (`getTarget()`) not null and alive; `path =
  navigation.createPath(target, 0)`: a path → true; else `isWithinMeleeAttackRange
  (target)`.
- `canContinueToUse` (105–156): target not null and alive; if not following when unseen:
  `!navigation.isDone()`; else the target's block within the home and the target not a
  spectator or creative player.
- `start` (157–179): `navigation.moveTo(path, speed)`, `setAggressive(true)` (the mob's
  flags, data 15 bit 4), both counters 0.
- `stop` (180–203): if the target fails `NO_CREATIVE_OR_SPECTATOR`, `setTarget(null)`;
  `setAggressive(false)`; `navigation.stop()`.
- `tick` (209–358):

```
t = getTarget(); if t == null: return
lookControl.setLookAt(t, 30f, 30f)
recalc = max(recalc - 1, 0)
if (followingEvenIfNotSeen || sensing.hasLineOfSight(t)) && recalc <= 0
   && ((pathedX == 0 && pathedY == 0 && pathedZ == 0)
       || t.distanceToSqr(pathedX, pathedY, pathedZ) >= 1.0
       || nextFloat() < 0.05f):                 // drawn only when the first two fail
    pathed = (t.x, t.y, t.z)
    recalc = 4 + nextInt(7)
    d = distanceToSqr(t)
    if d > 1024: recalc += 10 else if d > 256: recalc += 5
    if !navigation.moveTo(t, speed): recalc += 15
    recalc = adjustedTickDelay(recalc)          // every tick: unchanged
attackCooldown = max(attackCooldown - 1, 0)
checkAndPerformAttack(t)
```

- `checkAndPerformAttack(t)` (359–380): if `canPerformAttack(t)` (400–420: cooldown 0,
  `isWithinMeleeAttackRange(t)`, line of sight): `resetAttackCooldown()` (cooldown =
  `adjustedTickDelay(20)` = 20), `swingForAttack(MAIN_HAND)` (Mob.txt 3570–3583: the
  item's attack animation; `swing(hand, animation, false)`, the living body's section),
  `doHurtTarget(level, t)`.

**`LeapAtTargetGoal(mob, yd)`** (LeapAtTargetGoal.txt 1–139). Flags JUMP, MOVE. `canUse`
(26–77): no controlling passenger; a target; `4 <= distanceToSqr(target) <= 16`; on the
ground; one `nextInt(reducedTickDelay(5))` (3) == 0. Continues while off the ground.
`start` (89–138): `v = (tx − x, 0, tz − z)`; if `v.lengthSqr() > 1.0E-7`: `v =
v.normalize() × 0.4 + motion × 0.2`; motion = `(v.x, (double)yd, v.z)`.

**`OcelotAttackGoal(mob)`** (OcelotAttackGoal.txt 1–179), cats and ocelots. Flags MOVE,
LOOK; every tick. `canUse`: a target (stored). Continues (39–69) while it is alive,
`distanceToSqr <= 225`, and the navigation is not done or `canUse()`. `stop`: target
null, `navigation.stop()`. `tick` (86–178): `setLookAt(target, 30, 30)`; `reach =
(double)((bbWidth·2)·(bbWidth·2))` (float product); `d = distanceToSqr(target.x, y, z)`;
speed 0.8, or 1.33 when `reach < d < 16`, or 0.6 when `d < 225` (and not the 1.33 case);
`navigation.moveTo(target, speed)` (every tick); `attackTime = max(attackTime − 1, 0)`;
if `d <= reach` and `attackTime <= 0`: `attackTime = 20`, `doHurtTarget`. No draws.

**`RangedAttackGoal(rangedMob, speed, intervalMin[, intervalMax], radius)`**
(RangedAttackGoal.txt 1–267), the llama's spit and the snow golem's snowballs (and the
witch's, N9). Flags MOVE, LOOK; every tick; `attackTime = −1` at first; `radiusSqr =
radius·radius` (float). `canUse`: a live target (stored). Continues (99–117) while
`canUse()`, or the stored target lives and the navigation is not done. `stop`: target
null, `seeTime = 0`, `attackTime = −1`. `tick` (136–266):

```
d = distanceToSqr(t.x, t.y, t.z); see = sensing.hasLineOfSight(t)
seeTime = see ? seeTime + 1 : 0
if d <= (double)radiusSqr && seeTime >= 5: navigation.stop() else navigation.moveTo(t, speed)
lookControl.setLookAt(t, 30f, 30f)
attackTime -= 1
if attackTime == 0:
    if !see: return
    f = (float)Math.sqrt(d) / radius
    performRangedAttack(t, clamp(f, 0.1f, 1.0f))      // the type's (sections 4 and 5)
    attackTime = Mth.floor(f * (float)(max - min) + (float)min)
else if attackTime < 0:
    attackTime = Mth.floor(Mth.lerp(Math.sqrt(d) / (double)radius, (double)min, (double)max))
```

**`MoveTowardsTargetGoal(mob, speed, within)`** (MoveTowardsTargetGoal.txt 1–144), the
iron golem's. Flags MOVE. `canUse` (36–91): a target within `within²` (float product);
`DefaultRandomPos.getPosTowards(mob, 16, 7, target.position(), π/2)` not null.
Continues (92–120) while the navigation is not done, the target lives and is within
`within²`. `start`: `moveTo(wanted, speed)`; `stop`: target null.

### 2.12 Target goals (`ai.goal.target`)

**`TargetGoal(mob, mustSee[, mustReach = false])`** (target/TargetGoal.txt 1–292),
abstract; `unseenMemoryTicks` 60.

- `canContinueToUse` (52–134): `t = getTarget()`, or `targetMob` when null; null →
  false; `!mob.canAttack(t)` → false; both on the same team (the mob's team not null and
  the same object) → false; `distanceToSqr(t) > follow²` (`follow` = the `follow_range`
  attribute, 135–142) → false; if `mustSee`: seen → `unseenTicks = 0`; unseen →
  `unseenTicks += 1`, false once above `reducedTickDelay(unseenMemoryTicks)` (30);
  `mob.setTarget(t)`; true.
- `start` (143–155): `reachCache = 0`, `reachCacheTime = 0`, `unseenTicks = 0`. `stop`
  (156–166): `mob.setTarget(null)`, `targetMob = null`.
- `canAttack(t, conditions)` (167–226): null → false; `conditions.test(level, mob, t)`;
  `mob.isWithinHome(t.blockPosition())`; if `mustReach`: `reachCacheTime −= 1`, and at 0
  or below `reachCache = 0`; if `reachCache == 0`: `reachCache = canReach(t) ? 1 : 2`;
  false when 2.
- `canReach(t)` (227–284): `reachCacheTime = reducedTickDelay(10 + nextInt(5))` (5 to 7,
  one draw); `path = navigation.createPath(t, 0)`; no path or no end node → false; `dx =
  end.x − t.getBlockX()`, `dz = end.z − t.getBlockZ()`; `dx² + dz² <= 2.25`.

**`HurtByTargetGoal(mob, ignoreDamageFrom...)`** (target/HurtByTargetGoal.txt 1–255).
Flags TARGET; `mustSee` true. `HURT_BY_TARGETING = forCombat().ignoreLineOfSight()
.ignoreInvisibilityTesting()` (248–254; no range).

- `canUse` (30–92): `ts = getLastHurtByMobTimestamp()`, `a = getLastHurtByMob()`; false if
  `ts == timestamp` (already answered) or `a` is null; false if `a` is a player and the
  game rule `universalAnger` is on; false if any ignored class `isAssignableFrom(a's
  class)`; then `canAttack(a, HURT_BY_TARGETING)` (so a creative player who hit it: false).
  `getLastHurtByMob` is forgotten 100 ticks after the hit (the living body's section).
- `start` (104–133): `setTarget(a)`; `targetMob = getTarget()`; `timestamp = ts`;
  `unseenMemoryTicks = 300`; if `setAlertOthers` was called, `alertOthers()`; then
  `TargetGoal.start`.
- `alertOthers()` (134–240): `d = follow range`; `box = AABB.unitCubeFromLowerCorner(
  position()).inflate(d, 10, d)`; for each of `level.getEntitiesOfClass(mob.getClass(),
  box, NO_SPECTATORS)` in order: skip itself; skip one with a target; when this mob is a
  `TamableAnimal`, skip one with another owner (identity); skip one allied to the
  attacker; skip one whose class is exactly one of `toIgnoreAlert`; else `alertOther(o,
  a)` (`o.setTarget(a)`, 241–254).

**`NearestAttackableTargetGoal(mob, class, [interval = 10,] mustSee[, mustReach],
[selector])`** (target/NearestAttackableTargetGoal.txt 1–205). Flags TARGET;
`randomInterval = reducedTickDelay(interval)` (5 for 10); conditions
`forCombat().range(follow).selector(selector)` (49–76).

- `canUse` (77–100): if `randomInterval > 0` and `nextInt(randomInterval) != 0`: false;
  `findTarget()`; true when found.
- `findTarget()` (112–173): the range is set to the current follow range
  (`getTargetConditions`, 192–199); for `Player` or `ServerPlayer`:
  `level.getNearestPlayer(conditions, mob, x, getEyeY(), z)`; else
  `getNearestEntity(getEntitiesOfClass(class, getBoundingBox().inflate(follow, follow,
  follow), always), conditions, mob, x, getEyeY(), z)` (`getTargetSearchArea`, 101–111).
- `start`: `setTarget(target)`, `TargetGoal.start`. `setTarget(t)` sets the field only.
- Draws: `nextInt(5)` per asked selector tick.

**`NonTameRandomTargetGoal(tamable, class, mustSee, selector)`**
(target/NonTameRandomTargetGoal.txt 1–53): as the above (interval 10), `canUse` only when
not tame (20–33); `canContinueToUse` is `targetConditions.test(level, mob, target)` (the
conditions, with the range last set), not `TargetGoal`'s (34–52).

**`OwnerHurtByTargetGoal(tamable)`** (target/OwnerHurtByTargetGoal.txt 1–105). Flags
TARGET; `mustSee` false. `canUse` (24–84): tame, not ordered to sit; an owner; the owner's
`getLastDamageSource(100)` not null and not `#no_wolf_retaliation`; `a =
owner.getLastHurtByMob()`, `ts = owner.getLastHurtByMobTimestamp()`; `ts != timestamp`,
`canAttack(a, DEFAULT)`, `tamable.wantsToAttack(a, owner)`. `start`: `setTarget(a)`,
`timestamp = ts`. A creative owner takes no damage, so this never fires for one.

**`OwnerHurtTargetGoal(tamable)`** (target/OwnerHurtTargetGoal.txt 1–93): the same with
the owner's `getLastHurtMob()` and `getLastHurtMobTimestamp()` (what the owner hit), and
no damage-source test. A creative player who hits a mob makes their wolf attack it (the
`DEFAULT` conditions test the mob, not the player).

**`ResetUniversalAngerTargetGoal(neutralMob, alertOthersOfSameType)`**
(target/ResetUniversalAngerTargetGoal.txt 1–136). No flags. `canUse` (23–41): game rule
`universalAnger` on and `wasHurtByPlayer()` (42–64: last hurt by a player, with a
timestamp newer than the noted one). `start` (65–92): notes the timestamp;
`forgetCurrentTargetAndRefreshUniversalAnger()` (the `NeutralMob`'s); if alerting, the
same for every other mob of the same class in `unitCubeFromLowerCorner(position())
.inflate(follow, 10, follow)` (`NO_SPECTATORS`, list order).

**`DefendVillageTargetGoal(golem)`** (target/DefendVillageTargetGoal.txt 1–131). Flags
TARGET; `mustSee` false, `mustReach` true; conditions `forCombat().range(64)`. `canUse`
(30–120): `box = golem.getBoundingBox().inflate(10, 8, 10)`; villagers =
`getNearbyEntities(Villager, conditions, golem, box)`; players =
`getNearbyPlayers(conditions, golem, box)`; for each villager, each player: if
`villager.getPlayerReputation(player) <= −100`, `potentialTarget = player` (the last such
pair wins); then false if `potentialTarget` is null, false if it is a spectator or
creative player, else true. `potentialTarget` is never cleared (finding 14). `start`:
`setTarget(potentialTarget)`. Reputation is N10's; in a creative world this never fires.

### 2.13 The village and raid goals

`GolemRandomStrollInVillageGoal(golem, speed)` (GolemRandomStrollInVillageGoal.txt
1–243) is the iron golem's wander: a `RandomStrollGoal` with interval 240 and
`checkNoActionTime` false. `getPosition` (21–65) draws from **the level's random**: `r1
= nextFloat()`; if `r1 < 0.3f`: `LandRandomPos.getPos(golem, 10, 7)` (the golem's
random); else `r2 = nextFloat()`: if `r2 < 0.7f`, towards a villager who wants a golem,
else towards a point of interest, each falling back on the other, then on the plain land
position. Towards a villager (75–119): `level.getEntities(VILLAGER,
getBoundingBox().inflate(32), wantsGolem)` (the predicate is `doesVillagerWantGolem`,
`villager.wantsToSpawnGolem(gameTime)`, 218–227; **Inferred** method reference); one by
`level.nextInt(size)`; `LandRandomPos.getPosTowards(golem, 10, 7, its position)`. Towards
a point of interest (120–216): the sections of `SectionPos.cube(SectionPos.of(golem), 2)`
with `level.sectionsToVillage(s) == 0` (`SectionPos.cube(c, r)` is
`betweenClosedStream(c − r … c + r)` on each axis, SectionPos.txt 578–608, 635–667, its
order the spliterator `SectionPos$1`'s, not dumped; `PoiManager.sectionsToVillage` is
its distance tracker's level, PoiManager.txt 350–360); one by `level.nextInt(size)`; the
occupied points of interest of any type within 8 of its centre (`PoiManager.getInRange`,
109–125: `getInSquare` filtered by `pos.distSqr(centre) <= 8·8`, λ 782–795); one by
`level.nextInt(size)`; `LandRandomPos.getPosTowards(golem, 10, 7, atBottomCenterOf(it))`.
Without points of interest (N10) the sections list is empty and that branch gives null;
with villagers placed by structures (N7) but no brain, `wantsToSpawnGolem` (a memory) is
false, so in N7 the golem strolls on plain land positions, with the level's draws still
made.

`OfferFlowerGoal(golem)` (OfferFlowerGoal.txt 1–185). Flags MOVE, LOOK. `canUse`
(29–74): `level.isBrightOutside()`; one `nextInt(8000) == 0`; `entity =
level.getNearestEntity(#candidate_for_iron_golem_gift, forNonCombat().range(6), golem, x,
y, z, getBoundingBox().inflate(6, 2, 6))` (villagers and copper golems). `start`: `tick =
adjustedTickDelay(400)` (200), `golem.offerFlower(true)` (the golem's: an entity event,
the golem's section). `tick`: `setLookAt(entity, 30, 30)`, `tick −= 1`. Continues while
`tick > 0`. `stop` (98–143): `offerFlower(false)`; if it ran to the end (`tick == 0`) and
the entity is a mob of `#accepts_iron_golem_gift` (the copper golem) whose antenna slot
(`CopperGolem.EQUIPMENT_SLOT_ANTENNA`) is empty and whose box meets the golem's inflated
box: a poppy put there and `setGuaranteedDrop` on that slot.

`MoveBackToVillageGoal(golem, speed, checkNoActionTime)` (MoveBackToVillageGoal.txt 1–72):
a stroll (interval 10) that runs only when `!level.isVillage(blockPosition())`, toward
the centre of `BehaviorUtils.findSectionClosestToVillage(level, section, 2)` when that is
another section, by `DefaultRandomPos.getPosTowards(golem, 10, 7, …, π/2)`. Needs points
of interest (N10). `StrollThroughVillageGoal(mob, interval)`
(StrollThroughVillageGoal.txt 1–243), the fox's at night near villages
(`isCloseToVillage(pos, 6)`), likewise N10.

By name only (not animals' or golems'): `MoveThroughVillageGoal`, `OpenDoorGoal`,
`DoorInteractGoal`, `BreakDoorGoal`, `RemoveBlockGoal`, `ZombieAttackGoal`, `SpearUseGoal`,
`RangedBowAttackGoal`, `RangedCrossbowAttackGoal` (and `$CrossbowState`), `SwellGoal`,
`RestrictSunGoal` (N9, monsters); `PathfindToRaidGoal`, `NearestAttackableWitchTargetGoal`,
`NearestHealableRaiderTargetGoal` (N10, raids); `LookAtTradingPlayerGoal`,
`TradeWithPlayerGoal`, `InteractGoal`, `UseItemGoal` (N10, the wandering trader; the last
two are read above).

### 2.14 Who builds which goal

From the references in the dump (a class that names the goal: builds it or extends it).
Priorities and arguments are the types' own (sections 4 to 6).

| Goal | Animals, golems and others that build or extend it |
|---|---|
| `FloatGoal` | cat, cow (`AbstractCow`), rabbit, zombie horse, happy ghast (`$HappyGhastFloatGoal`), llama, panda, ocelot, polar bear, sheep, bee, chicken, horse (`AbstractHorse`), fox (`$FoxFloatGoal`), wolf, pig, parrot; monsters and traders |

### 2.15 What exists in Clustine to reuse, and what is missing

**To reuse:**

- The living body without a mind (`crates/clustine-sim/src/living.rs`, `living/travel.rs`,
  `living/inside.rs`): `LivingEntity.baseTick` and `aiStep` as an armour stand meets them,
  `travel` in air, water and lava with the attributes' gravity, friction and drag. N7's
  mobs need what it leaves out: input (`xxa`, `yya`, `zza`, `speed`), `serverAiStep`,
  jumping (`jumping`, `noJumpDelay`, `jumpFromGround`, `jumpInLiquid`), head and body
  yaw (`yHeadRot`, `yBodyRot`) with `tickHeadTurn`, and the attributes `movement_speed`,
  `flying_speed`, `follow_range`, `tempt_range`, `step_height`, `jump_strength`.
- `Mth.atan2` (`clustine-sim/src/physics/minecart.rs:196–230`), the sine table
  (`clustine-noise/src/trig.rs`), `wrap_degrees` (`clustine-noise/src/angle.rs:29`;
  copies in `region/riding.rs:1067` and `physics/vehicle_move.rs:35`), `Mth.floor`
  (`physics::floor`).
- Entity lookups in the game's order by chunk, section and key
  (`region/items.rs:619` `entities_in`, the region's own chunks only); the region's
  copies of chunks across a line (`region/entities.rs`, `copies`), which a lookup must
  also read.
- The entity's stream without state (`region/items.rs:180` `entity_stream`,
  `region/random_ticks.rs:64` `Random::of_entity`, with `next_int`, `next_float`,
  `next_double`).
- `BlockPos.betweenClosed` (`physics/walk.rs:31`), a block ray (`physics::walk::traverse`
  with collision shapes: `region/explosions.rs:882` `clips_collider`,
  `region/falling.rs:123`), on which `hasLineOfSight`'s `clip` can be built.
- Tags by registry, including entity types, fluids and damage types
  (`crates/clustine-data/src/generated/tags.rs`), and the entity types' sizes and
  categories (`generated/entity_types.rs`).
- The edge's tracker (`services/edge/src/tracking.rs`): positions, rotations (`yaw`,
  `pitch`), motion, entity data and equipment, with the game's periodic sync.

**Missing:**

- The goal machinery: `Goal`, `WrappedGoal`, `GoalSelector` (2.2) as a vector in
  `registerGoals` order with the locks and the disabled flags, the every-other-tick rule,
  `adjustedTickDelay`, and a representation of each goal's state that a commit can carry
  (or the decision of finding 5).
- The controls (2.3), `Sensing`, `TargetingConditions` (2.4), the random positions (2.5)
  and every goal of 2.7 to 2.12 that N7's animals use.
- `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` through `libm` for `RandomLookAroundGoal` and
  `generateRandomDirectionWithinRadians`; `libm::atan2` for `DolphinJumpGoal`.
- A stream for the level's random (finding 8).
- Players in copies, or a reading of the players of other regions (finding 9), and the
  nearest player's distance across lines for `noActionTime` (finding 10); a defined order
  of players for the queries.
- The iteration orders of `BlockPos$3` (Manhattan order: panic's water),
  `BlockPos$5` (`neighborColumn`: the dolphin's air) and `SectionPos$1` (the golem's
  sections), whose iterators are not dumped; the parameters are read (2.5, 2.7, 2.13).
- The edge's head rotation: `ClientboundRotateHeadPacket` when the packed head yaw
  changes by at least 1 (N4 brief section 9, line 1194); `tracking.rs` keeps no head
  rotation for its entities now (a stand's head follows its yaw). The mob flags (data
  15), entity events 10, 6 and the swing (9.2).
- The default attributes per type (`DefaultAttributes`), not extracted.

## 3. Navigation and path finding

Read from `reference/n7-javap/` (26.3): `net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.navigation.*`
(`PathNavigation`, `GroundPathNavigation`, `AmphibiousPathNavigation`,
`WaterBoundPathNavigation`, `FlyingPathNavigation`, `WallClimberNavigation`) and
`net.minecraft.world.level.pathfinder.*` (`PathFinder`, `NodeEvaluator`,
`WalkNodeEvaluator` and `$1`, `SwimNodeEvaluator`, `AmphibiousNodeEvaluator`,
`FlyNodeEvaluator`, `Node`, `Target`, `Path`, `BinaryHeap`, `PathType`, `PathTypeCache`,
`PathfindingContext`, `PathComputationType`); the mobs' own navigations
(`Frog$FrogPathNavigation`, `Frog$FrogNodeEvaluator`, `Turtle$TurtlePathNavigation`,
`Bee$1`, `HappyGhast$BabyFlyingPathNavigation`); and where they meet the rest:
`Mob` (malus, fall distance, `serverAiStep`, `createNavigation`), `LivingEntity`
(`maxUpStep`, `getSpeed`, `canStandOnFluid`, `getComfortableFallDistance`),
`PathfinderMob`, `ServerLevel.sendBlockUpdated` and `$EntityCallbacks`, `FloatGoal`,
`FollowOwnerGoal`, `FollowMobGoal`, `Attributes`, `BlockSetType`, and from the earlier
dumps `Level.setBlock` (n5), `BlockBehaviour.isPathfindable` and `$BlockStateBase` (n6),
`Direction$Plane` (n6), `AABB` (n5), `CollisionGetter` (n5). Line numbers are of the
`javap` file named. A second dump (see the head of this brief) added
`PathNavigationRegion`, `BlockPos` and `$MutableBlockPos`, `Vec3i`, `Vec3`, `ClipContext`,
`BlockGetter`, `ServerChunkCache`, `Level`, `LevelReader`, `Entity`, `BlockBehaviour` and
`$BlockStateBase`, and the blocks `DoorBlock`, `TrapDoorBlock`, `FenceGateBlock`,
`SlabBlock`, `StairBlock`, `WallBlock`, `SnowLayerBlock`, `LiquidBlock`, `CampfireBlock`
and others; the rules that rested on them are now the bytecode's, with their lines, and
3.22 says what an extraction must write so that no per-block code is needed.

Everything in this section is deterministic and draws nothing, except one place: a
flying mob whose own block it cannot start in draws start candidates from its own random
(3.17.3, 10.3). The goals that call navigation are section 2's; 3.18 says only what each
navigation method gives them.

### 3.0 Findings of this section

1. **A path search draws nothing and reads only blocks.** Walking, swimming and
   amphibious searches are a pure function of the mob's position, box, flags, malus map,
   attributes and the blocks (with their fluids and collision shapes) in a bounded box
   around it. So paths can be ported **exactly**, not by distribution, and judged
   exactly: the official server never shows a path (only a debug subscription a vanilla
   client cannot make, 9.3), but the jar's `PathFinder` can be run headless on fixed
   block layouts, as `Extract.java` runs the jar for block data, and its node lists
   compared with the port's (12.3 proposes it). This is the strongest test this section
   allows; the mobs' wandering itself is not comparable (their randoms are seeded from
   the clock, ADR-0028 section 4).

2. **Navigation keeps state the game never saves, and ADR-0028's two rules do not
   cover it.** `PathNavigation` holds the current `Path` (a list of nodes, each with its
   position and `PathType`, and the index of the next), its target and reach, the speed,
   the stuck check's tick and position, the timeout's cached node, timer and limit, the
   delayed recomputation, and the evaluator's flags; `Mob` holds a malus map that goals
   change for as long as they run (`FollowOwnerGoal`, `FollowMobGoal`,
   `AmphibiousNodeEvaluator`). The game saves none of it (`Mob.addAdditionalSaveData`
   writes `CanPickUpLoot`, `PersistenceRequired`, `drop`, `LeftHanded`, `NoAI`, `home`,
   loot table and seed): a reload drops every path. In the game that happens at a chunk
   unload; in Clustine every crossing, merge, split, lend and restore would do it, in
   ordinary play: a cow walking across a line would stop dead and stand until its next
   wander. The plan needs a decision: **carry navigation state with the entity**
   (proposed: it is small, and changes only when a path is made, advanced, stopped or
   timed out; 3.20 lists every field and how each can be held at rest), or name the
   stop as a difference. The path cannot be recomputed on arrival to the same result:
   it was planned from where the mob was, against the blocks then.

3. **A walking mob's search reaches about 17 blocks, a bee's or a villager's about 49.**
   The search range is `max(FOLLOW_RANGE, requiredPathLength)`, 16 for almost every
   animal; nodes are kept only while their walked distance is below it, and blocks are
   read up to one step and one neighbour cell beyond the last node, and `entityWidth −
   1` further in +x and +z. A region's copy one chunk wide therefore answers every read
   of a 16-range mob except when the mob stands within about two blocks of the line
   (11.3 gives the exact reach). It does **not** answer the 32 to 48 ranges of foxes
   (32), llamas (40), bees, allays, copper golems, baby happy ghasts and villagers (48),
   whose searches read up to three chunks across. The game reads land outside its
   `FULL` chunks, and outside the search's box, through an `EmptyLevelChunk`
   (`PathNavigationRegion.getChunk` 160–228): no block, no fluid, no collision.
   Clustine's `World::block` returning `None` there can be read as air with the same
   effect.

4. **A block change re-plans paths inside `setBlock`, in the same tick, mid-phase.**
   `ServerLevel.sendBlockUpdated` (2382–2470), reached from `Level.setBlock` only with
   `UPDATE_CLIENTS` (flag 2) in a chunk at least `BLOCK_TICKING`, first invalidates the
   level's path type cache at that position, then, if the old and new collision shapes
   differ, asks every navigating mob of the level whether its path passes near and
   recomputes those paths there and then (at most once in 20 game ticks per mob; a
   refused recompute is retried at each of its navigation ticks). Across a line this can
   only happen when the copy update arrives, a tick or more late (11.3).

5. **The level's path type cache can be stale, and its staleness is history.**
   `PathTypeCache` (4,096 slots, direct mapped by `HashCommon.mix(pos.asLong())`) holds
   the static type of a block state at a position; only `sendBlockUpdated` invalidates
   it. A block set without flag 2, or in a chunk below `BLOCK_TICKING` (the outer loaded
   ring), leaves the old type until another position evicts the slot. Which paths that
   changes depends on what was computed before, on any region's history: a region cannot
   reproduce it across merges, splits or restores. Proposed: compute types fresh (or
   cache with exact invalidation, including on copy updates), a named difference that
   shows only where the game itself is stale.

6. **The node limit is `maxVisitedNodes − 1` pops**, 255 for the default range of 16
   (`floor(16 × 16)` = 256, `PathNavigation.<init>` 76–85, `PathFinder` 146–160: the
   counter is raised before it is compared with `>=`). Range 48 gives 767.

7. **Porter's traps found in the bytecode** (each detailed below):
   - `walkedDistance` of a neighbour is overwritten by every visit, before the test of
     whether the visit improves it (`PathFinder` 226–236); SteelMC-26.3 writes it only on
     an improvement (`steel-core/src/entity/ai/pathfinder.rs:106-125`), which changes
     which nodes later count as out of range.
   - When a target is reached the path is built to that **target's best node** (the
     node seen nearest to it, by Euclidean distance, first seen wins), not to the node
     whose pop reached it (`PathFinder` 300–311, `Target.updateBest`).
   - The start node's `h` is the plain best distance; every other node's is that times
     `1.5f` (`PathFinder` 107–119 against 385–398).
   - The heap breaks a tie between two children towards the right one and never moves a
     node past an equal one (3.11).
   - `SwimNodeEvaluator` adds 8 to a node's malus, `FlyNodeEvaluator` 1, and the frog's
     shallow-swimming rule 1, **each time** the node is evaluated or listed, so the extra
     cost accumulates on a node seen from several neighbours (3.17).
   - A diagonal neighbour's jump test is made from the centre of the *orthogonal*
     neighbour in the direction iterated, not from the current node (3.15.6).
   - `getPathTypeOfMob` computes the origin cell's type twice, the second time outside
     the box loop (3.16.4); harmless but it is the cost.
   - `GroundPathNavigation.createPath(Entity, int)` throws away the base class's region
     offset of 16 and its start one block up: a walking mob following an entity searches
     the same box as for a block (3.7.4).
   - `recomputePath` makes a new path without resetting the stuck check (3.4.3); the
     timeout's timer is not reset when the next node changes (3.6.2); `moveTo` of a path
     equal node for node to the current one keeps the current one and its progress
     (3.4.1).
   - `AmphibiousNodeEvaluator.prepare` sets the mob's `WATER` malus to 0 and never
     restores it (3.17.2).
   - A fence is entered as a *closed* node only so that a small mob may slip diagonally
     between two fence posts (3.15.4, 3.15.5).
   - Node identity is by `Node.createHash`, which keeps only 8 bits of y and folds the
     signs of x and z into other coordinates' bits; no two cells of one search collide
     unless they are 128 blocks apart in x or z or 256 in y (3.12.2).

8. **Almost every land animal has `canFloat` set** by its `FloatGoal` (`FloatGoal.<init>`
   24–29 calls `setCanFloat(true)`), which changes where a search starts in water, the
   floor of a water cell (y + 0.5) and lets water cells be crossed at malus 8 instead of
   sinking to the bottom (3.15.7). A port that forgets the goal's side effect plans
   different paths around water.

9. **The cost is small and bursty.** A cow's wander on open grass pops about as many
   nodes as the path is long (10 to 15) and evaluates 60 to 120 neighbours, about 40 to
   70 distinct cells and 300 to 400 distinct block states; an unreachable target makes
   it pop the full 255 and evaluate about 2,000 neighbours over 400 to 500 cells
   (3.19, **Inferred** from the rules, to be measured). Following a path costs a few
   comparisons a tick.

10. **The rules about blocks are a per-state table.** `WalkNodeEvaluator.getPathTypeFromState`
    (1670–1814), the base of every type, reads nothing but the block state (its tags, its
    class, its fluid, two properties and `isPathfindable(LAND)`). `isPathfindable` is
    overridden by many block classes (those of both dumps are tabled in 3.16.1).
    Proposed: extract, per state, `getPathTypeFromState` and `isPathfindable` for
    `LAND`, `WATER` and `AIR` with `Extract.java`, exactly as collision shapes are now;
    the evaluators then need only that table, flags, fluids and shapes already
    extracted, and three tags (3.22 lists every field).

### 3.1 The classes and which mob has which

| Navigation (class) | Evaluator | Used by (from `createNavigation`) |
|---|---|---|
| `GroundPathNavigation` | `WalkNodeEvaluator` | `Mob`'s default (`Mob` 183–190): every land animal (cow, pig, sheep, chicken, horse kinds, llama, goat, fox, rabbit, cat, wolf, sniffer, camel, armadillo, panda, polar bear, ocelot, mooshroom), iron and snow golems, villagers, monsters |
| `WallClimberNavigation` (extends Ground) | `WalkNodeEvaluator` | spiders (N9) |
| `FlyingPathNavigation` | `FlyNodeEvaluator` | parrot (`setCanOpenDoors(false)`, `setCanFloat(true)`), allay (same, and `setRequiredPathLength(48)`), bee (`Bee$1`: `setCanOpenDoors(false)`, `setCanFloat(false)`, `setRequiredPathLength(48)`), baby happy ghast (`HappyGhast$BabyFlyingPathNavigation`: no doors, floats, 48) |
| `WaterBoundPathNavigation` | `SwimNodeEvaluator(allowBreaching)` | fish (`AbstractFish`), tadpole, nautilus, guardian, dolphin (breaching: `allowBreaching = mob.is(DOLPHIN)`, `WaterBoundPathNavigation` 13–49) |
| `AmphibiousPathNavigation` | `AmphibiousNodeEvaluator(false)` | axolotl; turtle (`Turtle$TurtlePathNavigation`, own `isStableDestination`) |
| `Frog$FrogPathNavigation` (extends Amphibious) | `Frog$FrogNodeEvaluator(true)` | frog |

Other settings made at construction or by goals (callers found by grep; their
conditions are section 2's): `setCanOpenDoors` by `Zombie`, `Vindicator`, `Villager`,
`CopperGolem`, `MoveThroughVillageGoal`; `setCanWalkOverFences` by `Camel`;
`setAvoidSun` by `RestrictSunGoal`; `setCanPathToTargetsBelowSurface` by
`TransportItemsBetweenContainers` (copper golem); `setMaxVisitedNodesMultiplier` by the
bee's `BeeGoToHiveGoal` and `BeeGoToKnownFlowerGoal`; `setRequiredPathLength` by
`Llama` (40), `Fox` (32), `CopperGolem` (48), `Villager` (48) besides those in the table;
`setCanPassDoors(false)` only by `WaterBoundPathNavigation`.

`Mob.getNavigation()` (288–303) returns the navigation of the mob's controlled vehicle
when that vehicle is a `Mob`, else its own; `Mob.serverAiStep` ticks its own field
`navigation` directly (1776–1777), after sensing and both goal selectors and before
`customServerAiStep` and the move, look and jump controls (`serverAiStep` 1705–1830):
a path made by a goal in a tick is followed, and the move control aimed, in that same
tick.

### 3.2 `PathNavigation`: state, construction and the range

Fields (`PathNavigation` 3–49), with their initial values (`<init>` 51–101):

| Field | Type | Initial | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mob`, `level` | | | |
| `path` | `Path` | null | the path followed |
| `speedModifier` | `double` | 0 | passed to the move control with each wanted position |
| `tick` | `int` | 0 | navigation ticks so far (`tick()` raises it first thing) |
| `lastStuckCheck` | `int` | 0 | `tick` at the last stuck check or `moveTo` |
| `lastStuckCheckPos` | `Vec3` | `Vec3.ZERO` | the mob's temp position then |
| `timeoutCachedNode` | `Vec3i` | `Vec3i.ZERO` | the next node's position when the timeout last saw it change |
| `timeoutTimer` | `long` | 0 | game ticks spent with an unchanged next node, summed since the last reset |
| `lastTimeoutCheck` | `long` | 0 | game time of the last timeout check |
| `timeoutLimit` | `double` | 0 | ticks the current node should take |
| `maxDistanceToWaypoint` | `float` | 0.5 | how close counts as at a node horizontally; set from the width at every `followThePath` |
| `hasDelayedRecomputation` | `boolean` | false | a recompute was refused and is to be retried |
| `timeLastRecompute` | `long` | 0 | game time of the last recompute |
| `nodeEvaluator` | | set by `createPathFinder` | |
| `targetPos` | `BlockPos` | null | the target of the last path made |
| `reachRange` | `int` | 0 | its reach |
| `maxVisitedNodesMultiplier` | `float` | 1.0 | scales the node limit for one search |
| `pathFinder` | `PathFinder` | | |
| `isStuck` | `boolean` | false | the last stuck check found the mob had not moved |
| `requiredPathLength` | `float` | 16.0 | a floor under the follow range |

**Construction** (`<init>` 51–101): `pathFinder = createPathFinder(floor(mob.getAttributeBaseValue(FOLLOW_RANGE) × 16.0))`,
the *base* value in `double` (`Mth.floor(double)`). Each subclass's `createPathFinder`
makes its evaluator, stores it in `nodeEvaluator`, and returns `new PathFinder(evaluator,
maxVisitedNodes)`. The debug capture is wired to `ServerDebugSubscribers.hasAnySubscriberFor(ENTITY_PATHS)`
(lambda 1300–1305); it only adds debug data to the path (9.3).

**The range.** `getMaxPathLength()` (126–136) = `max((float) mob.getAttributeValue(FOLLOW_RANGE), requiredPathLength)`
(`d2f`, then `Math.max(float, float)`). `updatePathfinderMaxVisitedNodes()` (103–115) sets
the finder's limit to `Mth.floor(getMaxPathLength() × 16f)` (float). It runs from
`setRequiredPathLength` (117–124) and from `Mob.onAttributeUpdated` when `FOLLOW_RANGE`
**or `TEMPT_RANGE`** changes (`Mob` ~3520–3540). So the limit is first from the base
value and later from the modified value with the floor of `requiredPathLength`.

`FOLLOW_RANGE` defaults (`Attributes` 430–451: 32, range 0 to 2048), but
`Mob.createMobAttributes` (175–181) adds 16, which every animal inherits unless it sets
its own: polar bear 20, fox 32, ravager 32, pillager 32, zombie 35, vindicator and evoker
12, illusioner 18, happy ghast 16 (grep of the `createAttributes` methods). For a cow:
range 16, 256 nodes, 255 pops.

`setMaxVisitedNodesMultiplier(f)` / `resetMaxVisitedNodesMultiplier()` (138–150) set the
multiplier the next searches use; `setSpeedModifier` (160–165) sets the speed.

### 3.3 `createPath` in its forms, and the box it reads

The public forms and what they pass (`regionOffset`, `offsetUpward`, `reach`, range):

| Form (lines) | Targets | regionOffset | offsetUpward | reach | range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `createPath(double x, y, z, int reach)` (209–218, final) | `BlockPos.containing(x, y, z)` through the virtual `createPath(BlockPos, int)` | | | | |
| `createPath(Stream<BlockPos>, int reach)` (220–231) | `Collectors.toSet()`: a `HashSet` | 8 | false | reach | `getMaxPathLength()` |
| `createPath(Set<BlockPos>, int reach)` (233–241) | the set | 8 | false | reach | `getMaxPathLength()` |
| `createPath(BlockPos, int reach)` (243–252) | `ImmutableSet.of(pos)` | 8 | false | reach | `getMaxPathLength()` |
| `createPath(BlockPos, int reach, int maxPathLength)` (254–265) | `ImmutableSet.of(pos)` | 8 | false | reach | `(float) maxPathLength` |
| `createPath(Entity, int reach)` (267–277) | `ImmutableSet.of(entity.blockPosition())` | **16** | **true** | reach | `getMaxPathLength()` |

`GroundPathNavigation` and `FlyingPathNavigation` override `createPath(Entity, int)` to
`createPath(entity.blockPosition(), reach)` (Ground 191–198, Flying 61–68), so the last
row holds only for the amphibious and water navigations. `LongJumpToRandomPos` is the
only caller of the three-argument form; `AcquirePoi` (villagers) the only caller with
several targets; no caller of the stream form was found.

**The common body**, `createPath(Set targets, int regionOffset, boolean offsetUpward, int reach, float range)` (291–399):

```
if targets.isEmpty() → null
if mob.getY() < level.getMinY() → null
if !canUpdatePath() → null
if path != null && !path.isDone() && targets.contains(targetPos) → return path   // no search
start = offsetUpward ? mob.blockPosition().above() : mob.blockPosition()
i = (int)(range + (float) regionOffset)            // f2i of a float sum
region = new PathNavigationRegion(level, start.offset(−i, −i, −i), start.offset(i, i, i))
result = pathFinder.findPath(region, mob, targets, range, reach, maxVisitedNodesMultiplier)
if result != null && result.getTarget() != null:
    targetPos = result.getTarget(); reachRange = reach; resetStuckTimeout()
return result
```

So a repeated call to the same block while a path is under way costs nothing, and
returns the path in progress. `start` here only centres the box: the search's own start
node is the evaluator's `getStart()` (3.15.2). For a cow, `i = 24`: a cube of 49 blocks
centred on the mob's block, that is four chunks by four horizontally.

**The box (`PathNavigationRegion`, 320 lines, a `CollisionGetter`).**
- `<init>(level, min, max)` (15–146): `centerX = min.x >> 4`, `centerZ = min.z >> 4` (the
  *lowest* chunk, despite the names); `chunks = new ChunkAccess[(max.x >> 4) − centerX + 1][(max.z >> 4) − centerZ + 1]`,
  filled for each chunk column `(cx, cz)` from `level.getChunkSource().getChunkNow(cx, cz)`
  (null where none); then `allEmpty` is cleared at the first non-null chunk whose
  `isYSpaceEmpty(min.y, max.y)` is false. `allEmpty` is never read by the search.
- `getChunk(cx, cz)` (160–228): the array's chunk if the column is inside the array and
  non-null; otherwise a **new `EmptyLevelChunk(level, ChunkPos(cx, cz), plains)`** (the
  plains biome holder, memoised, `lambda$new$0` 311–319). So a column outside the box,
  or a chunk not loaded at `FULL`, reads as an empty chunk.
- `getBlockState(pos)` (261–277): `Blocks.AIR` if `isOutsideBuildHeight(pos)`, else the
  chunk's; `getFluidState(pos)` (279–295): `Fluids.EMPTY` outside the height, else the
  chunk's. `EmptyLevelChunk`'s own answers are not dumped: it is read as giving air (or
  void air, which is also `isAir()`, with an empty collision shape) and no fluid, as its
  name says; for every rule of this section the two are the same.
- `getChunkForCollisions(cx, cz)` (237–243) = `getChunk(cx, cz)`, so block collisions
  outside are empty; `getEntityCollisions` (245–248) = `List.of()`: **the search's
  collision tests ignore entities**; `getWorldBorder` (230–235) is the level's;
  `getBlockEntity` the chunk's; `getMinY`/`getHeight` the level's (297–309).

`ServerChunkCache.getChunkNow(cx, cz)` (`ServerChunkCache` 325–405): null off the main
thread; else the chunk from the four-entry cache when its status there is `FULL` and it
is a `LevelChunk`, or the visible `ChunkHolder`'s `getChunkIfPresent(FULL)` if that is a
`LevelChunk`, else null. So only chunks loaded at `FULL` count, entity-ticking or not;
in Clustine, "loaded or copied".

The search reads through the box, but four reads of the navigation go to the level
directly: the target's surface (`findSurfacePosition`, through `getChunkNow` of
the target's chunk), the ground under the next node (`getGroundY`), the cauldron and sky
checks of `trimPath`, and `isStableDestination`.

### 3.4 `moveTo`, `stop`, recomputing, and block changes

#### 3.4.1 `moveTo`

- `moveTo(x, y, z, speed)` (401–412) = `moveTo(createPath(x, y, z, 1), speed)`: reach 1.
- `moveTo(x, y, z, reach, speed)` (414–425): the same with the reach given.
- `moveTo(Entity, speed)` (427–434) = `moveTo(entity, 1, speed)`; `moveTo(Entity, reach, speed)`
  (436–453): `createPath(entity, reach)`, false if null, else `moveTo(path, speed)`.
- `moveTo(Path p, double speed)` (455–499):

```
if p == null: this.path = null; return false
if !p.sameAs(this.path): this.path = p        // same nodes → the old path and its index stay
if isDone() → false                            // path null or its index at the end
trimPath()
if path.getNodeCount() <= 0 → false
speedModifier = speed
lastStuckCheck = tick; lastStuckCheckPos = getTempMobPos()
return true
```

`Path.sameAs` compares the node lists by `Node.equals` (x, y, z only; `Path` 262–275). A
path of one node (the start, when nothing better was found) is accepted: the mob walks
to its own node's centre and is done.

`stop()` (1007–1012) sets `path = null` and nothing else. `isDone()` (983–995) is `path ==
null || path.isDone()`; `isInProgress()` its negation.

#### 3.4.2 `recomputePath` (167–207)

```
if level.getGameTime() − timeLastRecompute > 20 && canUpdatePath():
    if targetPos != null:
        path = null
        path = createPath(targetPos, reachRange)     // the virtual one: Ground's surface search runs
        timeLastRecompute = level.getGameTime()
        hasDelayedRecomputation = false
    // targetPos null: nothing at all
else:
    hasDelayedRecomputation = true
```

`timeLastRecompute` is set only here; a fresh navigation (0) may recompute at once.
`MAX_TIME_RECOMPUTE = 20` names the constant; the code uses the literal `20L` with a
strict `>`.

#### 3.4.3 What a recompute does not do

It neither calls `moveTo` (so no `trimPath`, no reset of `lastStuckCheck`, the speed
kept) nor checks the new path's length: a null result stops the mob. `createPath`'s
`resetStuckTimeout` does run when the new path is non-null.

#### 3.4.4 `shouldRecomputePath(BlockPos changed)` (1205–1271) and the level's loop

```
if hasDelayedRecomputation → false
if path == null || path.isDone() || path.getNodeCount() == 0 → false
end = path.getEndNode()
mid = ((end.x + mob.getX()) / 2.0, (end.y + mob.getY()) / 2.0, (end.z + mob.getZ()) / 2.0)   // i2d then dadd, ddiv
return changed.closerToCenterThan(mid, (double)(path.getNodeCount() − path.getNextNodeIndex()))
```

`Vec3i.closerToCenterThan(pos, d)` (`Vec3i` 492–) is `distToCenterSqr(pos) < Mth.square(d)`,
and `distToCenterSqr(x, y, z)` (521–, and its `double` form) sums the squares of
`(getX() + 0.5) − x`, `(getY() + 0.5) − y`, `(getZ() + 0.5) − z`, in that order, in
`double`. A sphere around the midpoint of mob and goal, whose
radius is the number of nodes still to go.

`ServerLevel.sendBlockUpdated(pos, oldState, newState, flags)` (`ServerLevel` 2382–2470):
1. `getChunkSource().blockChanged(pos)`;
2. `pathTypesByPosCache.invalidate(pos)`, always;
3. if `Shapes.joinIsNotEmpty(old.getCollisionShape(this, pos), new.getCollisionShape(this, pos), NOT_SAME)`
   is false (the collision shape did not change), stop;
4. for every mob in `navigatingMobs`, collect those whose `getNavigation().shouldRecomputePath(pos)`;
5. with `isUpdatingNavigations` set (a recursive `sendBlockUpdated`, or an entity starting
   or ending tracking meanwhile, is reported as an error), call `recomputePath()` on each
   collected navigation in turn.

`navigatingMobs` is an `ObjectOpenHashSet<Mob>` (identity order, `ServerLevel` ~120–127),
filled by `$EntityCallbacks.onTrackingStart` with every `Mob` that starts *tracking* (not
only ticking) and emptied by `onTrackingEnd` (`$EntityCallbacks` 73–146, ~224). The
order does not matter: each recompute reads blocks and the cache, both already as after
the change, and writes only its own navigation. It does matter **when**: inside the
`setBlock` that made the change, so a path recomputed in the block tick phase sees the
blocks as they are at that moment of the tick.

`Level.setBlock(pos, state, flags, recursionLeft)` (`n5 Level` 298–) calls
`sendBlockUpdated` only when `flags & 2` and, on the server, the chunk's full status is
at least `BLOCK_TICKING` (offsets 83–137).

### 3.5 The tick, and following a path

#### 3.5.1 `tick()` (507–596)

```
tick += 1
if hasDelayedRecomputation: recomputePath()
if isDone() → return
if canUpdatePath():
    followThePath()
else if path != null && !path.isDone():
    pos = getTempMobPos(); next = path.getNextEntityPos(mob)
    if pos.y > next.y && !mob.onGround() && floor(pos.x) == floor(next.x) && floor(pos.z) == floor(next.z):
        path.advance()                                   // dropping onto the node counts
if isDone() → return
next = path.getNextEntityPos(mob)
mob.getMoveControl().setWantedPosition(next.x, getGroundY(next), next.z, speedModifier)
```

`getGroundY(Vec3 v)` (598–617): `p = BlockPos.containing(v)`; if `level.getBlockState(p.below()).isAir()`
then `v.y`, else `WalkNodeEvaluator.getFloorLevel(level, p)` (3.15.8). Amphibious and
water navigations return `v.y` (Amphibious 49–53, WaterBound 71–75). `Mob.getMoveControl()`
is the controlled vehicle's when it is a mob.

#### 3.5.2 `followThePath()` (619–721)

```
pos = getTempMobPos()
maxDistanceToWaypoint = mob.getBbWidth() > 0.75f ? mob.getBbWidth() / 2f : 0.75f − mob.getBbWidth() / 2f
n = path.getNextNodePos()
dx = |mob.getX() − (n.x + 0.5)|; dy = |mob.getY() − n.y|; dz = |mob.getZ() − (n.z + 0.5)|
close = dx < (double) maxDistanceToWaypoint && dz < (double) maxDistanceToWaypoint
        && dy < (double) getMaxVerticalDistanceToWaypoint()           // 1.0f; 0.5f for water
if close || (canCutCorner(path.getNextNode().type) && shouldTargetNextNodeInDirection(pos)):
    path.advance()
doStuckDetection(pos)
```

The closeness test uses the mob's own position, not `pos`. A cow (0.9 wide): 0.45; a
chicken (0.4): 0.55.

`canCutCorner(type)` (1115–1129): false for `FIRE_IN_NEIGHBOR`, `DAMAGING_IN_NEIGHBOR`,
`WALKABLE_DOOR`, true otherwise. The frog's navigation also refuses `WATER_BORDER`
(`Frog$FrogPathNavigation.canCutCorner`).

`shouldTargetNextNodeInDirection(pos)` (723–820):

```
if path.getNextNodeIndex() + 1 >= path.getNodeCount() → false
c = Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(path.getNextNodePos())          // (x + 0.5, y, z + 0.5)
if !pos.closerThan(c, 2.0) → false                         // distanceToSqr < 4.0
if canMoveDirectly(pos, path.getNextEntityPos(mob)) → true   // false on the ground; a clip for the others
d = Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(path.getNodePos(nextIndex + 1))
a = c − pos; b = d − pos
if b.lengthSqr() < a.lengthSqr() || a.lengthSqr() < 0.5:
    return b.normalize().dot(a.normalize()) < 0.0
return false
```

That is: skip the next node when the one after it is nearer, or the next is very near,
and the two lie on opposite sides of the mob. `Vec3.normalize()` (`Vec3` 173–): `len =
Math.sqrt(x × x + y × y + z × z)`; if `len < 9.999999747378752E-6` (the float `1.0E-5f`
widened) the zero vector, else `(x / len, y / len, z / len)`. `Vec3.closerThan(p, d)`
(351–) is `distanceToSqr(p) < d × d`; `Vec3.distanceTo` (371–) `Math.sqrt` of the summed
squared differences; `Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(v)` (88–) `atLowerCornerWithOffset(v, 0.5,
0.0, 0.5)`.

`isClearForMovementBetween(mob, from, to, fluids)` (1131–1170): a `ClipContext` from
`from` to `(to.x, to.y + mob.getBbHeight() × 0.5, to.z)` with `Block.COLLIDER` and
`Fluid.ANY` if `fluids` else `Fluid.NONE`, through `level.clip`; clear when the result is
`MISS`. The ray's end is raised half the mob's height; its start is not. The context
is made with `CollisionContext.of(mob)` (`ClipContext` 13–25); `BlockGetter.clip` (58–)
walks the blocks along the ray and at each takes, by `BlockGetter.lambda$clip$0`
(968–), the block's shape from `ClipContext.getBlockShape` (`Block.COLLIDER`: the
collision shape for the mob's context, 58–68) and the fluid's from `getFluidShape`
(only when `Fluid.canPick` accepts the fluid state, 70–), the nearer hit to `from`
winning; nothing hit gives `BlockHitResult.miss` (`lambda$clip$1`, 945–). The bodies of
the `ClipContext$Block` and `$Fluid` enums are not dumped: `COLLIDER` is read as the
collision shape and `Fluid.NONE`/`ANY` as never/any non-empty fluid, as their names
say.

### 3.6 Stuck detection and the timeout (`doStuckDetection`, 822–957)

#### 3.6.1 The stuck check, every 101 navigation ticks

```
if tick − lastStuckCheck > 100:
    s = mob.getSpeed() >= 1f ? mob.getSpeed() : mob.getSpeed() × mob.getSpeed()     // float
    t = s × 100f × 0.25f                                                            // float
    if pos.distanceToSqr(lastStuckCheckPos) < (double)(t × t): isStuck = true; stop()
    else isStuck = false
    lastStuckCheck = tick; lastStuckCheckPos = pos
```

`mob.getSpeed()` is `LivingEntity.speed` (`LivingEntity` 7349), which the move control
sets from the speed modifier and `MOVEMENT_SPEED`. A cow wandering at 1.0 × 0.2: `s` =
0.04, `t` = 1.0: a cow that has moved less than one block in 101 ticks is stuck and
stops. Nothing dumped reads `isStuck()` (grep): it is for goals of later steps.

#### 3.6.2 The timeout, every tick with a path

```
if path != null && !path.isDone():
    n = path.getNextNodePos(); now = level.getGameTime()
    if n.equals(timeoutCachedNode): timeoutTimer += now − lastTimeoutCheck
    else:
        timeoutCachedNode = n
        dist = pos.distanceTo(Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(n))
        timeoutLimit = mob.getSpeed() > 0f ? dist / (double) mob.getSpeed() × 20.0 : 0.0
    if timeoutLimit > 0.0 && (double) timeoutTimer > timeoutLimit × 3.0: timeoutPath()   // resetStuckTimeout(); stop()
    lastTimeoutCheck = now
```

`resetStuckTimeout()` (967–981): `timeoutCachedNode = Vec3i.ZERO`, `timeoutTimer = 0`,
`timeoutLimit = 0`, `isStuck = false`; it leaves `lastTimeoutCheck` as it was.

Three consequences a porter must keep:
- the timer is **not** reset when the next node changes: it sums every tick spent with an
  unchanged node since the last reset (a path made, or a timeout), and is compared with
  three times the limit of the current node only;
- it counts **game time**: ticks in the air (no `followThePath`) or frozen in a chunk
  that stops ticking are added in one step at the next check, if the node is unchanged;
- a first next node at `(0, 0, 0)` equals the initial `Vec3i.ZERO`, and the game time
  since `lastTimeoutCheck` (0 at first) is added at once.

### 3.7 `trimPath`, and what `GroundPathNavigation` changes

#### 3.7.1 `PathNavigation.trimPath()` (1018–1108): cauldrons

```
for i in 0 until path.getNodeCount():
    node = path.getNode(i); next = i + 1 < count ? path.getNode(i + 1) : null
    if level.getBlockState(node.x, node.y, node.z).is(BlockTags.CAULDRONS):
        path.replaceNode(i, node.cloneAndMove(node.x, node.y + 1, node.z))
        if next != null && node.y >= next.y:
            path.replaceNode(i + 1, node.cloneAndMove(next.x, node.y + 1, next.z))
```

`node` is the original (unraised) node in both lines; the clone keeps every field but the
position (`Node.cloneAndMove` 81–127). `CAULDRONS`: cauldron, water, lava and powder snow
cauldrons.

#### 3.7.2 `GroundPathNavigation` (349 lines)

- `canUpdatePath()` (30–47): `mob.onGround() || mob.isInLiquid() || mob.isPassenger()`.
- `getTempMobPos()` (49–63): `(mob.getX(), getSurfaceY(), mob.getZ())`.
- `getSurfaceY()` (200–263): if `mob.isInFloatableFluid() && canFloat()`: `y = mob.getBlockY()`;
  read the state at `containing(x, y, z)`; while its fluid is in `ENTITY_FLOATABLE`:
  `y += 1`, read again, and after the 17th read (`count > 16`) return `mob.getBlockY()`;
  return `y` (the first non-floatable cell above). Otherwise `floor(mob.getY() + 0.5)`.
- `createPath(BlockPos pos, int reach)` (65–95): `chunk = level.getChunkSource().getChunkNow(pos.x >> 4, pos.z >> 4)`
  (`SectionPos.blockToSectionCoord`); null → **no path**. Unless
  `canPathToTargetsBelowSurface`, `pos = findSurfacePosition(chunk, pos, reach)`; then the
  base `createPath(pos, reach)`.
- `findSurfacePosition(chunk, pos, reach)` (97–189), all reads from the target's chunk:

```
if chunk.getBlockState(pos).isAir():
    m = pos.below()
    while m.y >= minY && chunk.getBlockState(m).isAir(): m.y -= 1
    if m.y >= minY: return m.above()                  // stand on the first non-air below
    m.y = pos.y + 1                                    // nothing below: look up
    while m.y <= maxY && chunk.getBlockState(m).isAir(): m.y += 1
    pos = m
if chunk.getBlockState(pos).isSolid():                 // the legacy 'solid' flag
    m = pos.above()
    while m.y <= maxY && chunk.getBlockState(m).isSolid(): m.y += 1
    return m
return pos
```

  `reach` is unused. `isSolid` is `BlockStateBase.isSolid()`, bit 1 of the flags the
  datagen already extracts.
- `createPath(Entity, int)` (191–198): `createPath(entity.blockPosition(), reach)` (finding 7).
- `trimPath()` (265–321): the base's, then if `avoidSun`: if
  `level.canSeeSky(containing(mob.x, mob.y + 0.5, mob.z))` stop (a mob already in the
  sun keeps its path); else truncate the path at the first node whose block can see the
  sky (`Path.truncateNodes(i)`). Needs `canSeeSky`, light's heightmap (N8); used by
  monsters only.
- `canNavigateGround()` true; `setAvoidSun`, `setCanWalkOverFences` (to the evaluator),
  `setCanPathToTargetsBelowSurface` (323–348).
- Not overridden: `isStableDestination` (the base: the block below is `isSolidRender`,
  1172–1182), `canMoveDirectly` (false, 1110–1113), `getMaxVerticalDistanceToWaypoint` (1.0).

#### 3.7.3 Doors

Passing and opening doors are the evaluator's flags (`NodeEvaluator` 15–19, 156–206):
`canPassDoors` (default **true**), `canOpenDoors` (false), `canFloat` (false),
`canWalkOverFences` (false). `PathNavigation.setCanOpenDoors` and `setCanFloat` pass them
on (1190–1203, 1292–1298); `setCanFloat` is a no-op in the amphibious and water
navigations. What they do is in 3.16.4: a closed wooden door becomes `WALKABLE_DOOR`
(malus 0) for a mob that can open and pass doors, an open door `BLOCKED` for one that
cannot pass doors. A `WALKABLE_DOOR` is never entered diagonally, never cut past, and the
door is opened by a goal, not by the navigation (section 2).

#### 3.7.4 The box for an entity target

The base form with an entity (regionOffset 16, start one up) is reached only by the
amphibious and water navigations; `GroundPathNavigation`, `WallClimberNavigation` (through
Ground's) and `FlyingPathNavigation` search the box of a block target.

### 3.8 The other navigations as differences

**`AmphibiousPathNavigation`** (93 lines): evaluator `AmphibiousNodeEvaluator(false)`;
`canUpdatePath()` always true; `getTempMobPos()` `(x, mob.getY(0.5), z)` (the middle of the
box); `getGroundY(v)` `v.y`; `canMoveDirectly(from, to)` only in liquid:
`isClearForMovementBetween(mob, from, to, false)`; `isStableDestination(pos)`: the block
below is not air; `setCanFloat` does nothing; `canNavigateGround()` true.

**`Turtle$TurtlePathNavigation`**: `isStableDestination(pos)`: while the turtle has a
`travelPos`, whether the block at `pos` is `Blocks.WATER`; otherwise the block below is
not air.

**`Frog$FrogPathNavigation`**: evaluator `Frog$FrogNodeEvaluator(true)`, `canCutCorner`
also refuses `WATER_BORDER`.

**`WaterBoundPathNavigation`** (113 lines): `allowBreaching = mob.is(DOLPHIN)`; evaluator
`SwimNodeEvaluator(allowBreaching)` with `setCanPassDoors(false)`; `canUpdatePath()`
`allowBreaching || mob.isInLiquid()`; temp position `(x, getY(0.5), z)`; ground y `v.y`;
`canMoveDirectly` = `isClearForMovementBetween(mob, from, to, false)`;
`isStableDestination(pos)`: the block **at** `pos` is not `isSolidRender`;
`canNavigateGround()` false; `getMaxVerticalDistanceToWaypoint()` 0.5; `setCanFloat`
nothing.

**`FlyingPathNavigation`** (172 lines): evaluator `FlyNodeEvaluator`; `canUpdatePath()`
`(canFloat() && mob.isInLiquid()) || !mob.isPassenger()`; temp position `mob.position()`;
`createPath(Entity)` the block form; `canMoveDirectly` with fluids (`Fluid.ANY`);
`isStableDestination(pos)`: `state(pos).entityCanStandOn(level, pos, mob)`;
`canNavigateGround()` false. Its own `tick()` (70–152): as the base, but the
not-updatable branch advances when `mob.getBlockX/Y/Z()` all equal the floors of the
next entity position, and the wanted position is the next entity position itself (y =
node y, no ground y). `Bee$1` (the bee's): `isStableDestination` the block below is not
air, and `tick()` does nothing while the bee pollinates. `HappyGhast$BabyFlyingPathNavigation`:
`canMoveDirectly` without fluids.

**`WallClimberNavigation`** (spiders, 135 lines): remembers `pathToPosition` at every
`createPath`; `moveTo(Entity, speed)` makes the path with reach **0**, and when that
gives none still keeps `pathToPosition = entity.blockPosition()`, sets the speed and
**returns true**. `tick()`: when the navigation is done and `pathToPosition` is set, clear
it if `pathToPosition.closerToCenterThan(mob.position(), bbWidth)` or (the mob is above it
and the block at its x, z at the mob's y is that close); otherwise aim the move control
straight at `pathToPosition`'s integer corner `(x, y, z)` with the speed. Otherwise the
ground tick. Monsters' (N9); recorded here because it is in the package.

### 3.9 `Path`

Fields (`Path` 3–15): `nodes` (a mutable `List<Node>`), `debugData`, `nextNodeIndex`
(int, 0), `target` (`BlockPos`, the requested target as given), `distToTarget` (float),
`reached` (boolean). Constructor (17–49): `distToTarget` = `MAX_VALUE` for an empty list,
else `lastNode.distanceManhattan(target)` (a float sum of int absolute differences).

| Method | Rule |
|---|---|
| `advance()` (51–59) | `nextNodeIndex += 1` |
| `isDone()` (71–82) | `nextNodeIndex >= nodes.size()` |
| `getEndNode()` | last node or null |
