## 5. Tamed and ridden animals

Read from `reference/n7-javap/` (names are Mojang's; "X.txt 120–180" is the line range of
the `javap -p -c -constants` output of class X): `TamableAnimal` (712 lines) and
`TamableAnimal$TamableAnimalPanicGoal`, `OwnableEntity`, `NeutralMob`, `PlayerRideable`,
`PlayerRideableJumping`; `animal.wolf.Wolf` (1900) with `$WolfAvoidEntityGoal`,
`$WolfPackData`, `WolfVariant(s)`, `WolfSoundVariant(s)`; `animal.feline.Cat` (1312) with
`$CatRelaxOnOwnerGoal`, `$CatTemptGoal`, `$CatAvoidEntityGoal`, `CatVariant(s)`,
`CatSoundVariant(s)`, `Ocelot` with `$OcelotTemptGoal` and `$OcelotAvoidEntityGoal`;
`animal.parrot.Parrot` (1107) with `$1`, `$ParrotWanderGoal`, `$Variant`,
`ShoulderRidingEntity`; `animal.equine.AbstractHorse` (2780) with `$MountPanicGoal`,
`Horse` and `$HorseGroupData`, `AbstractChestedHorse` and `$1`, `Donkey`, `Mule`, `Llama`
(1007) with `$Variant`, `$LlamaGroupData`, `$LlamaHurtByTargetGoal`, `$LlamaAttackWolfGoal`,
`TraderLlama` and its goal, `SkeletonHorse`, `SkeletonTrapGoal`, `ZombieHorse`, `Markings`,
`Variant`; the goals only tamed and ridden animals use (`SitWhenOrderedToGoal`,
`FollowOwnerGoal`, `BegGoal`, `CatLieOnBlockGoal`, `CatSitOnBlockGoal`, `OcelotAttackGoal`,
`LandOnOwnersShoulderGoal`, `LlamaFollowCaravanGoal`, `RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal`,
`RandomStandGoal`, `target.OwnerHurtByTargetGoal`, `target.OwnerHurtTargetGoal`,
`target.NonTameRandomTargetGoal`, `target.ResetUniversalAngerTargetGoal`);
`variant.VariantUtils`, `PriorityProvider`, `SpawnContext`, `MoonBrightnessCheck`,
`StructureCheck`; `npc.CatSpawner`; `SwampHutPiece.spawnCat`; `WorldGenRegion`'s constructor;
`AgeableMob.finalizeSpawn` and `$AgeableMobGroupData`; and, for what they bear on here,
`LivingEntity.travelRidden`, `aiStep`'s travel dispatch, `maxUpStep`, `getJumpPower`,
`isEquippableInSlot`, `Mob.getControllingPassenger`, `isSaddled`, `ItemStack.
interactLivingEntity`, `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePlayerCommand` (n7 dump);
`EntityReference` and `ServerPlayer`'s shoulder and horse-inventory methods (n6 dump);
`EntityDataSerializers`, `Avatar`, `EquipmentSlot`, `RandomSource` (n5 dump). Data:
`data/minecraft/{wolf,cat}_variant/`, `{wolf,cat}_sound_variant/`, the item, block and
entity-type tags named below, `timeline/day.json`, `loot_table/gameplay/
cat_morning_gift.json`.

The generic goals (`FloatGoal`, `PanicGoal`, `BreedGoal`, `TemptGoal`, `FollowParentGoal`,
`WaterAvoidingRandomStrollGoal`, `WaterAvoidingRandomFlyingGoal`, `LookAtPlayerGoal`,
`RandomLookAroundGoal`, `LeapAtTargetGoal`, `MeleeAttackGoal`, `AvoidEntityGoal`,
`FollowMobGoal`, `MoveToBlockGoal`, `RangedAttackGoal`, `HurtByTargetGoal`,
`NearestAttackableTargetGoal`, `TargetGoal`) are section 2's: this section names which each
animal uses, at which priority and with what arguments. The path finder
(`WalkNodeEvaluator.getPathTypeStatic`, navigation, `DefaultRandomPos`, `LandRandomPos`) is
section 3's. `Animal`, `AgeableMob` (ageing, love, the golden dandelion's age lock),
`Mob.finalizeSpawn`'s own draws and `Mob.interact` (name tags, leads) belong to whichever
section covers `Animal` and `Mob`; they are pointed at, not repeated. Riding in `Entity`,
`handleMoveVehicle`, `handlePlayerInput`, dismount helpers and leashes are the N5 brief's
(`docs/groundwork/n5-brief.md`, sections 1, 2 and 7); this section says how a horse differs.

### 5.0 Findings of this section

1. **An owner the region cannot find makes a tamed animal sit down.**
   `SitWhenOrderedToGoal.canUse` (SitWhenOrderedToGoal.txt 26–79): after "not ordered to
   sit and not tame → false", "in water → false", "not on ground → false", it returns
   **true** when `getOwner()` is null or in another level, whatever `isOrderedToSit()`
   says. `getOwner()` is a lookup of the owner's UUID among the level's entities
   (`EntityReference.getEntity`, EntityReference.txt (n6) 69–146), so an owner who is
   offline, or in another dimension, is "no owner": the wolf, cat or parrot sits, and
   `FollowOwnerGoal` (which needs the owner) never runs. In Clustine an owner is almost
   always a player, and **players are not in copies** (the N5 named difference): a dog
   whose owner walks over a line sits down at it, on the first tick the owner is out of
   the region's reach, and stays sitting until the owner comes back. ADR-0028 section 5
   ("an owner … read across a line through the copies") assumes the owner is in the
   copies; for players it is not. The plan must decide how a region sees a player of
   another region (position, level, alive, spectator, sleeping, last hurt mob and its
   timestamp, last damage source: every field this section's goals read, 11.5), or merge
   where a tamed animal's owner is across, or name the difference. It is what a player
   meets first with a dog.
2. **A tamed animal teleports to its owner from 12 blocks** (`shouldTryTeleportToOwner`,
   TamableAnimal.txt 524–541: `distanceToSqr(owner) >= 144`), to a spot 2 to 3 blocks off
   the owner's block (`teleportToAroundBlockPos`, 543–595), checked by the path finder's
   static path type and a collision test there (632–671). The target is the owner's land,
   so the teleport is an arrival when the owner is in another region's land, and needs the
   blocks there (copies reach one chunk beyond the line; the owner can be 12 or more blocks
   further). Draws: up to ten tries of `nextIntBetweenInclusive(-3, 3)` twice, and
   `nextIntBetweenInclusive(-1, 1)` only for a try whose `|dx|` or `|dz|` is at least 2
   (10.5).
3. **Anger is an end time in game ticks, synched and saved** (`NeutralMob`, Wolf's
   `DATA_ANGER_END_TIME`, a `LONG` at index 22, saved as `anger_end_time`). The client
   tests `endTime - its own game time > 0` for the angry texture and tail. Clustine's
   regions count ticks "each from their own start" (`entity.rs` 20–24) and the edge sends no
   `set_time`: anger needs the world's game time, the same in every region and on every
   client, or a wolf crossing a line comes calm or angry for longer. The same holds for
   `ServerPlayer.timeEntitySatOnShoulder` (20 ticks before parrots can be shaken off) and
   the cat's gift chance and the moon phase, which are read from the day's timeline.
4. **While a wolf has a target its anger timer is restarted every tick, with a draw**:
   `Wolf.aiStep` calls `updatePersistentAnger(level, true)` (Wolf.txt 715–759), and with a
   target and `true` it calls `startPersistentAngerTimer` (NeutralMob.txt 98–186), a
   `UniformInt` of 400 to 780 ticks (`TimeUtil.rangeOfSeconds(20, 39)` multiplies both by
   20, TimeUtil.txt 19–28; `UniformInt.sample` is `Mth.randomBetweenInclusive(r, 400,
   780)` = `r.nextInt(381) + 400`, UniformInt.txt 30–38, Mth.txt (n6) 1932–1943) from the
   wolf's random. A wolf chasing a sheep draws once a tick for its anger alone.
5. **A riding player steers a horse only when it is saddled**:
   `AbstractHorse.getControllingPassenger` (AbstractHorse.txt 2420–2438) is the first
   passenger if the horse `isSaddled()` and that passenger is a `Player`; else `Mob`'s
   (a first passenger that is a `Mob` and `canControlVehicle`, Mob.txt 306–326). An
   unsaddled horse with a player on it (taming) is moved by the server and its own AI;
   the player's `move_vehicle` goes to `handleMoveVehicle`'s "not controlling" branch
   (n5-brief 2.3 step 4) and is corrected. N5's `drives()` (boats.rs 225–232) is "first seat
   a player"; a horse's is "saddled and first seat a player".
6. **A controlled horse does nothing of its own on the server.** With a player in control
   `isEffectiveAi()` is false, so `serverAiStep` (its goals) does not run
   (LivingEntity.txt 8316–8342); `travelRidden` (7051–7077) runs `getRiddenInput` and
   `tickRidden`, then, because `canSimulateMovement()` is false for a client-authoritative
   vehicle, sets the motion to **zero** every tick instead of `travel`. The position is
   only what `handleMoveVehicle` accepts. `tickRidden` (AbstractHorse.txt 1711–1767) sets
   the horse's rotation from the rider every tick: `yRot = rider.yRot`, `xRot =
   rider.xRot · 0.5f`, and `yRotO = yBodyRot = yHeadRot = yRot`; its jump branch runs only
   on the authoritative side, the client.
7. **The jump bar is the client's; the server only rears the horse.** `PlayerCommand
   START_RIDING_JUMP` (ordinal 3) with `data > 0` and `canJump()` (saddled) calls
   `handleStartJump(data)` (SGPLI 5269–5289; AbstractHorse.txt 2229–2238):
   `allowStandSliding = true`, `standIfPossible()` (the standing flag, bit 32 of index 18,
   for 20 ticks) and the jump sound. `data` is ignored; `STOP_RIDING_JUMP` (4) does
   nothing for horses. `onPlayerJump` and `executeRidersJump` (the impulse
   `jumpStrength · scale`, the forward kick `0.4 · scale`) run on the rider's client
   (**Client**, as `LocalPlayer` is not in the jar).
8. **In 26.3 a saddle and horse armour are equipment slots, not inventory slots.**
   `EquipmentSlot` ordinals: `MAINHAND` 0, `OFFHAND` 1, `FEET` 2, `LEGS` 3, `CHEST` 4,
   `HEAD` 5, `BODY` 6, `SADDLE` 7 (EquipmentSlot.txt, n5). `isSaddled()` is "a valid
   equippable item in `SADDLE`" (Mob.txt 2080–2085); armour and carpets are `BODY`. The
   horse's own `inventory` (`SimpleContainer`) holds only a chest's slots: `getInventorySize()
   = AbstractMountInventoryMenu.getInventorySize(getInventoryColumns())` with 0 columns
   for a horse, 5 for a donkey or mule with a chest and the llama's strength for a llama
   with one (AbstractHorse.txt 535–583, AbstractChestedHorse.txt 348–356, Llama.txt
   602–611). A saddle is put on through the item's `equippable` component
   (`equip_on_interact`, `allowed_entities = #can_equip_saddle`), which `clustine-data`
   does not extract yet (5.19).
9. **Horse attributes at spawn draw from the level's random, health then speed then
   jump; at breeding from the parent's own random, health then jump then speed.**
   `AbstractHorse.finalizeSpawn` (2608–2627) passes `ServerLevelAccessor.getRandom()` to
   `randomizeAttributes`; `setOffspringAttributes` (2030–2059) uses `this.random`. The
   foal's value is `mean ± spread · (u1 + u2 + u3)/3 − ½`, reflected at the bounds
   (5.12). Donkeys, mules and llamas randomise only their health; skeleton horses only
   their jump; zombie horses jump and speed by a formula of their own.
10. **At chunk generation the animals' looks are a function of the seed.** Every draw of
    these `finalizeSpawn`s (wolf variant and sound, horse coat, markings and attributes,
    llama strength and variant, parrot colour, the baby chance) is from
    `ServerLevelAccessor.getRandom()`, and a `WorldGenRegion`'s random is
    `randomState.getOrCreateRandomFactory("worldgen_region_random").at(centre chunk's
    world position)` (WorldGenRegion.txt 83–103): positional, from the seed. n-plan 3.7
    ("their colours and variants come from the entity's own random and are judged by
    bounds") is wrong for these: the animals made with a chunk can be judged exactly,
    variants and stats included, provided the spawn step's other users of the region
    random draw in the game's order. The spawn step makes a `WorldGenRegion` of its own
    for every chunk (`ChunkStatusTasks.generateSpawn`, ChunkStatusTasks.txt 274–292, then
    `spawnOriginalMobs`), so the region random starts fresh there.
    `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator.spawnOriginalMobs` (1039–1078) gives
    `NaturalSpawner.spawnMobsForChunkGeneration` a `WorldgenRandom` seeded by
    `setDecorationSeed(seed, minBlockX, minBlockZ)` for the groups, positions and yaw
    (`nextFloat() · 360`, NaturalSpawner.txt 1016–1022), while
    `SpawnPlacements.checkSpawnRules` gets `level.getRandom()` (992–993) and so does every
    `finalizeSpawn` (1044–1048). Both are functions of the seed and the chunk. The
    entity's own random (`EntityType.create`, 1001) is not used.
11. **A wolf's variant is the biome's; a cat's is uniform among ten, black at full moon
    or in a witch hut.** `VariantUtils.selectVariantToSpawn` (VariantUtils.txt 68–86) and
    `PriorityProvider.pick` (PriorityProvider.txt 5–68): every variant's selectors
    unpacked, sorted by priority, highest first (a stable sort, so registry order within a
    priority); those below the best passing priority and those whose condition fails
    dropped; then one of the rest by `nextInt(size)` of the level's random, **a draw even
    when one is left**. A wolf in a forest is `woods`, in a grove `snowy`, and so on
    (5.5); elsewhere `pale`. A cat chooses among the ten `priority 0` variants, with
    `all_black` an eleventh at full moon (`moon_brightness ≥ 0.9`), and `all_black` alone
    in a structure of `#cats_spawn_as_black` (the witch hut).
12. **Kittens bred from cats always have the classic voice**: `Cat.getBreedOffspring`
    (Cat.txt 903–956) copies a parent's variant (`nextBoolean`), and the owner and mixed
    collar if tame, but never sets the sound variant, which keeps its default `classic`
    (defineSynchedData, 413–465); breeding calls no `finalizeSpawn` (`Animal.
    spawnChildFromBreeding`, Animal.txt 404–435). Wolf pups do draw a voice
    (`pickRandomSoundVariant` with the parent's random, Wolf.txt 1560–1620).
13. **`Bred` is never set in 26.3**, so a foal's `followMommy` (AbstractHorse.txt
    1248–1289) never runs except for horses loaded with `Bred: 1`, and even then it only
    computes a path it throws away (`navigation.createPath(mommy, 0)`, result discarded).
    A porter can leave it as a no-op, once the path finder is known to draw nothing.
14. **Parrot imitations pick from a `HashMap` keyed by `EntityType`**
    (`Parrot.MOB_SOUND_MAP`, Parrot.txt 877–1105, built with `Maps.newHashMap`):
    `getAmbient` lists its `keySet()` and takes `nextInt(size)` (583–607). The key order is
    by the types' identity hash codes and changes from run to run: Clustine needs an order
    of its own (the order the map is filled in, say), a named difference in value only,
    the distribution (uniform over 42 types, one being the happy ghast's silent `EMPTY`)
    being the game's.
15. **The parrot's dance is the client's.** `setRecordPlayingNearby` is called by nothing
    in the server jar's dumps (only `LivingEntity` declares it and `Parrot` overrides it):
    **Inferred** the client's level renderer calls it near a jukebox. The server never
    has a party parrot; nothing to port beyond `isPartyParrot` false.
16. **A parrot on a shoulder is not an entity**: `ShoulderRidingEntity.setEntityOnShoulder`
    (ShoulderRidingEntity.txt 17–70) saves the parrot whole (with `id`) into the player's
    `ShoulderEntityLeft` (or `…Right`) compound and discards it. The player carries it, saves
    it, shows its variant in the player's own synched data (indices 19 and 20,
    `OPTIONAL_UNSIGNED_INT`), and puts it back in the world when they fall more than half
    a block, enter water or powder snow, fly, sleep or are hurt, and at least 20 game
    ticks after it landed (ServerPlayer.txt (n6) 1446–1661). In Clustine the shoulder
    compounds belong to the player's carried state (as the ender chest does since N6): a
    hand-over must carry them.
17. **The cat's morning gift is in `CatRelaxOnOwnerGoal`, and needs a sleeping owner and
    the day's timeline.** The goal (Cat$CatRelaxOnOwnerGoal.txt 20–436) has the cat lie on
    its owner's bed while the owner sleeps; when the goal stops and the owner had slept
    100 ticks or more, `level.random.nextFloat()` is tested against the environment
    attribute `gameplay/cat_waking_up_gift_chance` at the cat (0.7 from day time 23667 to
    362, else 0, `timeline/day.json`), and the gift drops by the loot table
    `gameplay/cat_morning_gift`, whose `random_sequence` is passed to the loot context
    (`LivingEntity.dropFromLootTable`, LivingEntity.txt 4027–4056, calls
    `LootTable.getRandomItems(params)`, LootTable.txt 177–188, which hands the table's
    `randomSequence` to `LootContext$Builder.create`; **Inferred** that the builder then
    draws from the level's random sequence of that name, the builder is not dumped).
    Clustine has neither sleeping nor the day's
    timeline: no gift until both come, a named difference until then.
18. **Taming draws**: wolf and cat `nextInt(3) == 0` per item (bone, raw cod or salmon),
    parrot `nextInt(10) == 0` per seed, ocelot trust `nextInt(3) == 0` per fish, all from the
    animal's own random, all on the server; horses by riding: every `nextInt(25)` tick
    (`adjustedTickDelay(50)` on a goal that does not tick every tick, **Inferred** from
    section 2's `Goal.adjustedTickDelay`), tamed if `nextInt(maxTemper) < temper`, else
    `temper += 5` and the rider is thrown. `maxTemper` is 100, a llama's 30. A creative
    player tames by the same draws: nothing is instant, and bones are not used up in
    creative (`ItemStack.consume` spares infinite materials).
19. **An ocelot that is offered a fish draws 42 times on the server for particles it
    never sends**: `Ocelot.mobInteract` calls `spawnTrustingParticles` directly on the
    server (Ocelot.txt 280–346, 369–419): seven particles of three `nextGaussian` and three
    `nextDouble` (`getRandomX/Y/Z`), passed to `Level.addParticle`, which does nothing on a
    server. A wolf shaking off water likewise draws two `nextFloat` per splash particle
    each tick (Wolf.txt 761–961), and a horse eating draws for its sound. With Clustine's
    stateless streams this matters only for the count of draws within the entity's tick.
20. **A cat hit does not stand up; a wolf and a parrot do.** `Wolf.hurtServer` and
    `Parrot.hurtServer` call `setOrderedToSit(false)` before the hurt (Wolf.txt 1053–1070,
    Parrot.txt 709–726); `Cat` does not override it.
21. **Horses and llamas rear, buck and eat by draws every tick**: `aiStep`
    `nextInt(200)` for the tail (both sides) and, on the server, `nextInt(900)` for healing
    one point, `nextInt(300)` to start eating grass when standing on a grass block, eating
    lasting 50 ticks (AbstractHorse.txt 1165–1246); `hurtServer` rears with
    `nextInt(3) == 0` (599–617); `RandomStandGoal` (priority 9) rears when
    `nextInt(1000) < nextStand` counting up from `−400` (RandomStandGoal.txt 47–94). Eating
    grass does not change the block.
22. **An untamed horse offered any item that is not food gets angry** (`makeMad`: rears,
    angry sound) and the click succeeds (Horse.txt 284–343): a saddle or armour on an
    untamed horse does nothing but that. On a tamed horse an empty hand mounts, a sneak
    opens its inventory, a saddle is equipped through `interactLivingEntity`, armour into
    `BODY` if it is not wearing any.
23. **Zombie horses spawned naturally come with a zombie on them holding an iron spear**
    (ZombieHorse.txt 182–233), and a zombie horse ridden by a mob is "mob-controlled", which
    switches off its panic and its bucking: N9's.
24. **The horse inventory menu is not `ChestMenu`**: `ServerPlayer.openHorseInventory`
    (n6 3266–3307) sends `mount_screen_open` (clientbound 42: container id, columns, the
    horse's entity id; `ClientboundMountScreenOpenPacket.write`, 44–58: `writeContainerId`,
    a VarInt, an `int`) and builds a `HorseInventoryMenu` (5.14). The edge must translate
    the entity id in it (n-plan 3.1).
25. **Llama caravans are links in memory only** (`caravanHead`, `caravanTail`, not saved,
    Llama.txt 836–885): a llama within a 9 × 4 × 9 box of a leashed llama or of a caravan's
    end joins behind it (LlamaFollowCaravanGoal.txt 27–156), up to eight behind a leashed
    head. Across a line the box reaches into another region's land.

### 5.1 Ownership: `OwnableEntity`, `EntityReference`, `TamableAnimal`

**`OwnableEntity`** (OwnableEntity.txt): `getOwnerReference()`, `getOwner()` =
`EntityReference.getLivingEntity(ref, level)`; `getRootOwner()` follows owners that are
themselves ownable, with a set to stop at a loop (returns null on a loop). Implemented by
`TamableAnimal` (the reference in synched data) and `AbstractHorse` (a plain field,
`owner`, not synched).

**`EntityReference`** (EntityReference.txt (n6), 329 lines): an `Either<UUID, entity>`.
`getEntity(lookup, class)` (69–121): if it holds an entity that is not removed, that
entity; a removed one turns it back to its UUID. Holding a UUID: `lookup.lookup(uuid)`,
kept if of the class and not removed, else null. `getEntity(level, class)` (123–146) uses
`level`'s player lookup when the class is `Player` or a subclass, else its entity lookup:
**Inferred** `ServerLevel.getPlayerInAnyDimension` and `getEntityInAnyDimension`
(ServerLevel.txt 3088, 3126; the `invokedynamic` targets are method references). An owner
is looked up as `LivingEntity`, so by the entity lookup, which finds players too. Stored
by `store(output, key)` as a UUID (`UUIDUtil.CODEC`: an int array of four); read by
`readWithOldOwnerConversion` (a UUID, or an old player name converted through
`OldUsersConverter`). Its stream codec is the UUID's (static 316–327).

**`TamableAnimal`** (TamableAnimal.txt):
- Synched: `DATA_FLAGS_ID` (`BYTE`, index 18): bit 1 sitting pose, bit 4 tame;
  `DATA_OWNERUUID_ID` (`OPTIONAL_LIVING_ENTITY_REFERENCE`, index 19), empty by default
  (30–46, static 701–711).
- Field `orderedToSit` (false), saved as `Sitting`; the owner saved as `Owner` (48–65).
- Read (67–116): `Owner` read; present → set, `setTame(true, false)` (no side effects);
  absent or failing → owner empty and `setTame(false, true)`. Then `orderedToSit =
  Sitting` (default false) and `setInSittingPose(orderedToSit)`.
- `setTame(tame, applySideEffects)` (215–249) sets or clears bit 4, then
  `applyTamingSideEffects()` if asked (nothing here; the wolf's sets its health, 5.4; the
  cat re-adds its goals, 5.6).
- `tame(player)` (364–383) = `setTame(true, true)`, `setOwner(player)`, the advancement.
- `feed(player, hand, stack, perNutrition, otherwise)` (255–280): `usePlayerItem`, then
  `heal(food != null ? perNutrition · nutrition : otherwise)`, `playEatingSound()`.
- `canAttack(e)` false for its owner (385–396); `isOwnedBy(e)` = `e == getOwner()`
  (identity); `wantsToAttack(target, owner)` true (overridden by the wolf); `getTeam()`
  the owner's when tame and not on a team of its own (414–435); `considersEntityAsAlly`:
  its root owner and the owner's allies (437–459).
- `die`: with `showDeathMessages` and the owner an online `ServerPlayer`, the owner is
  sent the death message (461–496).
- `canBeLeashed()` true (121–124).
- Entity events (178–197, client): 7 hearts (tamed), 6 smoke (failed). Their particles
  draw on the client only.
- **The teleport** (511–695): `shouldTryTeleportToOwner()` = owner found and
  `distanceToSqr(owner) >= 144.0`. `tryToTeleportToOwner()` =
  `teleportToAroundBlockPos(owner.blockPosition())`: ten tries of
  ```
  dx = nextIntBetweenInclusive(-3, 3); dz = nextIntBetweenInclusive(-3, 3)
  if |dx| < 2 && |dz| < 2: next try            // no third draw
  dy = nextIntBetweenInclusive(-1, 1)
  if maybeTeleportTo(owner.x + dx, owner.y + dy, owner.z + dz): stop
  ```
  `maybeTeleportTo(x, y, z)`: `canTeleportTo(pos)` → `snapTo(x + 0.5, y, z + 0.5,
  yRot, xRot)`, `navigation.stop()`. `canTeleportTo(pos)`: the path finder's
  `getPathTypeStatic(mob, pos) == WALKABLE` (section 3); unless `canFlyToOwner()` (the
  parrot) the block below is not `LeavesBlock`; and `level.noCollision(this,
  box.move(pos − blockPosition()))` (blocks, colliding entities, the border).
- `unableToMoveToOwner()` (final): ordered to sit, or a passenger, or `mayBeLeashed()`, or
  the owner a spectator.
- `TamableAnimalPanicGoal` (…$TamableAnimalPanicGoal.txt 34–50): a `PanicGoal` whose tick
  first teleports to the owner when it should and can (the `unableToMoveToOwner` and
  distance tests), so a panicking dog left behind still comes.

### 5.2 Sitting, following, defending

**`SitWhenOrderedToGoal(tamable)`**, flags JUMP and MOVE (SitWhenOrderedToGoal.txt):
```
canUse:  sit = isOrderedToSit()
         if !sit && !isTame: false
         if isInWater: false;  if !onGround: false
         owner = getOwner()
         if owner == null || owner.level != level: true          // finding 1
         if distanceToSqr(owner) < 144 && owner.getLastHurtByMob() != null: false
         return sit
canContinueToUse: isOrderedToSit()
start: navigation.stop(); setInSittingPose(true)       stop: setInSittingPose(false)
```
An animal sat down for want of an owner is stopped next time the selector checks
(`canContinueToUse` false) and started again at once (`canUse` true), so its sitting flag
ends each such tick set (**Inferred** from the selector's order of stop then start,
section 2's).

**`FollowOwnerGoal(tamable, speed, startDistance, stopDistance)`**, flags MOVE and LOOK
(FollowOwnerGoal.txt). The constructor throws unless the navigation is ground or flying.
- `canUse`: an owner, not `unableToMoveToOwner`, `distanceToSqr(owner) >= start²` (float
  square widened).
- `canContinueToUse`: navigation not done, not unable, `distanceToSqr > stop²`.
- `start`: `timeToRecalcPath = 0`; keep the water malus and set it to 0. `stop`: owner
  null, navigation stopped, water malus restored.
- `tick`: `teleport = shouldTryTeleportToOwner()`; unless teleporting, look at the owner
  (10, `getMaxHeadXRot`); every `adjustedTickDelay(10)` ticks (`--timeToRecalcPath > 0`
  returns): teleport if `teleport`, else `navigation.moveTo(owner, speed)`.
- Wolf (1.0, 10, 2), cat (1.0, 10, 5), parrot (1.0, 5, 1).

**`OwnerHurtByTargetGoal`** (TargetGoal, not must-see, flag TARGET): tame, not ordered to
sit, an owner; the owner's last damage source within 100 ticks
(`owner.getLastDamageSource(100)`) must exist and not be of `#no_wolf_retaliation`, so a
creative owner, who takes no damage, is never defended;
`ownerLastHurtBy = owner.getLastHurtByMob()`; usable when its timestamp
(`getLastHurtByMobTimestamp`) differs from the one remembered, `canAttack(it, DEFAULT)`
and `wantsToAttack(it, owner)`; start sets the target and remembers the timestamp
(OwnerHurtByTargetGoal.txt 24–104). **`OwnerHurtTargetGoal`** the same with
`owner.getLastHurtMob()` and `getLastHurtMobTimestamp()` (OwnerHurtTargetGoal.txt 24–92):
what the owner hits, the dog attacks, a creative owner's hits included. Both read the
owner's state, which lives in the owner's region (11.5).

**`NonTameRandomTargetGoal(tamable, class, mustSee, selector)`**: a
`NearestAttackableTargetGoal(…, 10, mustSee, false, selector)` used only while not tame;
`canContinueToUse` tests its conditions again (NonTameRandomTargetGoal.txt 5–52).

### 5.3 Anger: `NeutralMob` (NeutralMob.txt, 348 lines)

State the mob keeps: `persistentAngerEndTime` (a game time, −1 for none) and
`persistentAngerTarget` (an `EntityReference`, nullable). Saved as `anger_end_time` (long)
and `angry_at` (UUID, nullable) (32–45); read (47–96): `anger_end_time`, or the old
`AngerTime` added to the game time, or −1; `angry_at` read and the target set to it if it
resolves (server only).
- `isAngry()` = `end > 0 && end − level.getGameTime() > 0` (263–287).
- `setTimeToRemainAngry(t)`: `end = gameTime + t`.
- `stopBeingAngry()`: last hurt by mob null, anger target null, target null, end −1.
- `updatePersistentAnger(level, ticking)` (98–186):
  ```
  t0 = getTargetUnchecked(); ref = angerTarget
  if t0 != null && t0.isDeadOrDying() && ref != null && ref.matches(t0) && t0 is Mob:
      stopBeingAngry(); return
  t = getTarget()
  if t != null:
      changed = ref == null || !ref.matches(t)
      if changed: angerTarget = EntityReference.of(t)
      if changed || ticking: startPersistentAngerTimer()       // a draw (finding 4)
  if ref != null && !isAngry() && (t == null || !isValidPlayerTarget(t) || !ticking):
      stopBeingAngry()
  e = getLivingEntity(ref, level)          // the reference as it was on entry
  if e is Player && (creative || spectator || difficulty peaceful): stopBeingAngry()
  ```
  `isValidPlayerTarget(e)`: a player, not creative, not spectator, difficulty not
  peaceful (188–210).
- `isAngryAt(e, level)` = `canAttack(e)` and (a valid player while `isAngryAtAllPlayers`,
  or the anger target matches `e`) (212–241). `isAngryAtAllPlayers` = game rule
  `universal_anger`, angry, and no anger target.
- `playerDied(level, player)`: with `forgive_dead_players`, anger at that player stops.
- `ResetUniversalAngerTargetGoal(mob, alertOthers)` (ResetUniversalAngerTargetGoal.txt):
  only with `universal_anger`; when the mob was hurt by a player since it last ran,
  `forgetCurrentTargetAndRefreshUniversalAnger()` (stop, then start the timer), and, if
  `alertOthers`, the same for every mob of its own class in its box inflated by follow
  range horizontally and 10 vertically (not spectators), but itself.

In creative a player is never a valid target, so a wolf is not angry at a creative player
for long: `updatePersistentAnger` stops it the tick after (the last test).

### 5.4 The wolf (Wolf.txt, 1900 lines)

**Attributes** (448–460): `Animal.createAnimalAttributes()` plus movement speed
0.30000001192092896, max health 8, attack damage 4. **Tamed**: `applyTamingSideEffects`
(1150–1169) sets max health's base to 40 and health to 40 when tame, back to 8 when
untamed. Constructor (43–61): `setTame(false, false)`, path malus −1 on powder snow and on
top of it. Baby dimensions (static 1856–1898): scalable 0.3 × 0.425, eye 0.34375,
passenger attachment (0, 0.4375, 0). `getMaxSpawnClusterSize` 8. Sound volume 0.4.

**Goals** (registerGoals 63–263): goal selector
1 `FloatGoal`; 1 `TamableAnimalPanicGoal(1.5, #panic_environmental_causes)`;
2 `SitWhenOrderedToGoal`; 3 `WolfAvoidEntityGoal(Llama, 24, 1.5, 1.5)`;
4 `LeapAtTargetGoal(0.4)`; 5 `MeleeAttackGoal(1.0, true)`;
6 `FollowOwnerGoal(1.0, 10, 2)`; 7 `BreedGoal(1.0)`; 8 `WaterAvoidingRandomStrollGoal(1.0)`;
9 `BegGoal(8)`; 10 `LookAtPlayerGoal(Player, 8)`; 10 `RandomLookAroundGoal`.
Target selector: 1 `OwnerHurtByTargetGoal`; 2 `OwnerHurtTargetGoal`;
3 `HurtByTargetGoal()` with `setAlertOthers()` (no classes: alerts wolves of its own type);
4 `NearestAttackableTargetGoal(Player, 10, true, false, this::isAngryAt)` (**Inferred**
the method reference); 5 `NonTameRandomTargetGoal(Animal, false, PREY_SELECTOR)` with
`PREY_SELECTOR` sheep, rabbit or fox (lambda$static$0, 1837–1854); 6
`NonTameRandomTargetGoal(Turtle, false, Turtle.BABY_ON_LAND_SELECTOR)`; 7
`NearestAttackableTargetGoal(AbstractSkeleton, false)`; 8
`ResetUniversalAngerTargetGoal(true)`.

`WolfAvoidEntityGoal` (Wolf$WolfAvoidEntityGoal.txt 27–87): an `AvoidEntityGoal` usable
when the base finds a llama, the wolf is not tame and `llama.getStrength() >=
random.nextInt(5)` (a draw only when a llama was found); start and tick clear the wolf's
target first.

`BegGoal(wolf, 8)` (BegGoal.txt), flag LOOK: the nearest player in non-combat range 8
(`ServerLevel.getNearestPlayer(forNonCombat().range(8), wolf)`) holding a bone or wolf
food in either hand (main hand first); no test of tameness. Start: interested flag on,
`lookTime = adjustedTickDelay(40 + nextInt(40))`. Continue while the player is alive,
within 8, `lookTime > 0` and still holding it. Tick: look at the player's eyes (10,
`getMaxHeadXRot`), `lookTime−−`. Stop: flag off.

**`wantsToAttack(target, owner)`** (1684–1755): never creepers, ghasts or armour stands; a
wolf only if it is wild or has another owner; a player only if the owner `canHarmPlayer`
it; never a tamed horse; any other tame animal only if it is not tame.

**Interaction, `mobInteract`** (1192–1379), in order:
```
stack = hand's item
if isTame:
  if isFood(stack) && health < max: feed(…, 2.0, 2.0) → SUCCESS      // heal 2·nutrition
  if stack in #wolf_collar_dyes && isOwnedBy(player):
      dye = stack.DYE; if dye != null && dye != collar: collar = dye; consume 1 → SUCCESS
      else fall to the end (super)
  else if equippable in BODY && !wearing body armour && owned && !baby:
      BODY = copy of 1; consume 1 → SUCCESS
  else if inSittingPose && wearing armour && owned && armour damaged
          && armour.isValidRepairItem(stack):
      stack.shrink(1)                     // even in creative: shrink, not consume
      sound wolf armour repair; damage = max(0, damage − (int)(maxDamage · 0.125f)) → SUCCESS
  else:
      r = TamableAnimal.mobInteract (Animal's: food breeds or ages)
      if !r.consumesAction && owned: orderedToSit = !orderedToSit; jumping = false;
          navigation.stop(); target = null; → SUCCESS.withoutItem
      return r
else (wild), server only: if bone && !isAngry: consume 1; tryToTame → SUCCESS_SERVER
super
```
`tryToTame` (1381–1411): `nextInt(3) == 0` → `tame(player)`, navigation stop, target null,
`orderedToSit = true`, entity event 7; else event 6. Wolf food: `#wolf_food` (meats, cod,
salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish, rabbit stew). Breeding (`canMate`, 1632–1672): not
itself, tame, the other a tame wolf not in sitting pose, both in love.

**Armour.** `canArmorAbsorb(source)` (1134–1148): wearing `wolf_armor` and the source not
of `#bypasses_wolf_armor`. `actuallyHurt` (1072–1132): absorbed → the armour takes
`Mth.ceil(damage)` (`hurtAndBreak` to `BODY`), the wolf takes none; if the armour's
`Crackiness.WOLF_ARMOR` level changed, sound `wolf_armor_crack` and 20 `item` particles of
armadillo scute at (x, y + 1, z) spread (0.2, 0.1, 0.2) speed 0.1 (`sendParticles`). Hurt
sound `wolf_armor_damage` when the armour would absorb (686–699). `hurtArmor` damages only
`BODY`. `canShearEquipment(player)` = owned by them (shears take the armour, `Mob`'s).
Armour repair unit 0.125.

**`hurtServer`** (1053–1070): invulnerable → false; `setOrderedToSit(false)`; then the base.

**`aiStep`** (715–759): base first; on the server, wet and not shaking and not path
finding and on ground → `isShaking = true`, `shakeAnim = shakeAnimO = 0`, entity event 8;
then `updatePersistentAnger(level, true)`.

**`tick`** (761–961), both sides, after the base, if alive: the interested angle eases
(visual); if `isInWaterOrRain()`: `isWet = true`, and if shaking on the server, event 56
and `cancelShake()`; else if wet or shaking, while shaking: at `shakeAnim == 0` the shake
sound (volume 0.4, pitch `(nextFloat − nextFloat)·0.2 + 1`) and game event
`entity_action`; `shakeAnimO = shakeAnim; shakeAnim += 0.05`; when `shakeAnimO >= 2`, wet,
shaking and both animations reset; when `shakeAnim > 0.4`, `n = (int)(Mth.sin((shakeAnim −
0.4f)·3.1415927f) · 7)` splash particles each drawing two `nextFloat` (offsets `(2u − 1) ·
width · 0.5`) at `(float)y + 0.8`: on the server only the draws happen. `die` clears the
shake first (976–993). Rain needs weather, which Clustine has not: only water wets a wolf.

**Ambient sound** (643–684): angry → growl; else `nextInt(3) == 0` → tame with health
below 20 → whine, else pant; else ambient. Step sound at 0.15. Sounds are the variant's
set, the baby set if a baby (327–343). Tail angle (client): angry 1.5393804, tame
`(0.55 − (max − health)/max · 0.4) · π`, wild 0.62831855.

**Leash** (1757–1783): `canBeLeashed` unless angry; offset (0, 0.6·eyeHeight, 0.4·width).

**Spawn rules** (`checkWolfSpawnRules`, 1785–1801): block below in `#wolves_spawnable_on`
(grass, snow, snow block, coarse dirt, podzol) and bright enough.

**Spawn** (`finalizeSpawn`, 593–641):
```
if group is WolfPackData: variant = pack's
else: v = selectVariantToSpawn(SpawnContext(level, blockPosition()), wolf_variant)   // level random
      if v: variant = v; group = WolfPackData(v)        // shouldSpawnBaby false: no baby draw
soundVariant = pickRandomSoundVariant(registryAccess, level.getRandom())
super.finalizeSpawn(level, difficulty, reason, group)
```
`pickRandomSoundVariant` is `Registry.getRandom(random)` of `wolf_sound_variant`
(WolfSoundVariants.txt): `MappedRegistry.getRandom` is `Util.getRandomSafe(byId,
random)` (MappedRegistry.txt 538–544), `nextInt(7)` over the entries in id order.

**Breeding** (`getBreedOffspring`, 1560–1620): new wolf (`BREEDING`); variant `nextBoolean
? this : partner` (this wolf's random); if this wolf is tame: owner reference copied,
`setTame(true, true)` (40 health), collar `DyeColor.getMixedColor(level, this, partner)`
(DyeColor.txt 193–304: for each item whose `dye` component is this collar's colour, and
each whose is the partner's, in the item registry's component lookup order, a 2 × 1
crafting input of the two; the first crafting recipe that matches is assembled, and its
result's `dye` colour, if any, is the pup's; with none, `level.getRandom().nextBoolean()
? this : partner`, a draw of the level's random); then sound variant
`pickRandomSoundVariant(…, this.random)`.

**Saved** (529–591): the base's (`Owner`, `Sitting`, age, love, …), `CollarColor` (the
dye's legacy id, default red 14), `variant` (identifier), `anger_end_time`, `angry_at`,
`sound_variant` (identifier). Read: variant if known, collar or red, anger, sound
variant if known.

**Synched data** (defineSynchedData 462–514, static 1856–1879), after `TamableAnimal`'s:
20 `DATA_INTERESTED_ID` (BOOLEAN, false), 21 `DATA_COLLAR_COLOR` (INT, red's id 14),
22 `DATA_ANGER_END_TIME` (LONG, −1), 23 `DATA_VARIANT_ID` (WOLF_VARIANT, default `pale`
or any), 24 `DATA_SOUND_VARIANT_ID` (WOLF_SOUND_VARIANT, `classic` or any).

**Components** (354–446): `wolf/variant`, `wolf/sound_variant`, `wolf/collar` are
readable and applied from a spawn egg's or bucket's components (`applyImplicitComponents`).

### 5.5 Wolf and cat variants (data and selection)

`wolf_variant/` (nine files): `pale` `{priority 0}` (fallback); `ashen` biome
`snowy_taiga`; `black` `old_growth_pine_taiga`; `chestnut` `old_growth_spruce_taiga`;
`rusty` `#is_jungle`; `snowy` `grove`; `spotted` `#is_savanna`; `striped` `#is_badlands`;
`woods` `forest`; each of these at priority 1. Each has `assets` and `baby_assets` (wild,
tame, angry textures; the client's).

`wolf_sound_variant/` (seven): `angry`, `big`, `classic`, `cute`, `grumpy`, `puglin`,
`sad`, each with adult and baby sounds (ambient, death, growl, hurt, pant, step, whine).

`cat_variant/` (eleven): `all_black` with `[structure #cats_spawn_as_black, priority 1;
moon_brightness ≥ 0.9, priority 0]`; `black`, `british_shorthair`, `calico`, `jellie`,
`persian`, `ragdoll`, `red`, `siamese`, `tabby`, `white` each `{priority 0}`. Default
`black` (Cat static).

`cat_sound_variant/`: `classic`, `royal` (adult and baby: ambient, beg for food, death,
eat, hiss, hurt, purr, purreow, stray ambient).

**Registry order**: the synched data and `nextInt(size)` both go by the registry's ids,
and `listElements()` (which `selectVariantToSpawn` walks) streams `byId` in id order
(MappedRegistry.txt 497–502); ids are given in the order entries are registered
(`register`, 240–246, appends to `byId`). `clustine-data` sends these registries in
identifier order (registries.rs 130–200), which the comparisons with the official server
have accepted: **Inferred** that the data pack's loader registers them in that order (the
loader, `RegistryDataLoader`, is not dumped).

**Selection** (`PriorityProvider.select` and `pick`, PriorityProvider.txt 5–68):
```
entries = [(variant, selector.priority, selector.condition or always) for variant in
           registry order for selector in variant.selectors]
stable sort entries by priority, highest first
best = i32::MIN
for e in entries: if e.priority < best: drop
                  elif e.condition(context): best = e.priority
                  else: drop
return entries.is_empty ? none : entries[random.nextInt(len)]
```
A variant with two passing selectors at the best priority would be in twice (none does).
`SpawnContext.create(level, pos)` = (pos, level, level's environment attributes,
`level.getBiome(pos)`) (SpawnContext.txt 29–43). `BiomeCheck`: the biome in the set.
`StructureCheck` (16–28): `structureManager.getStructureWithPieceAt(pos, set).isValid()`.
`MoonBrightnessCheck` (16–37): `DimensionType.MOON_BRIGHTNESS_PER_PHASE[moon phase at the
block's centre]` within the range; full moon is 1.0, the next phase 0.75, so only a full
moon passes 0.9.

**Attributes** (642–654): health 10, speed 0.30000001192092896, attack 3. Baby dimensions

**Goals** (53–201): `temptGoal = CatTemptGoal(0.6, cat food, canScare true)`. Goal

And, while **not** tame, 4 `CatAvoidEntityGoal(Player, 16, 0.8, 1.33)` with

`CatTemptGoal` (Cat$CatTemptGoal.txt): usable only while not tame. Its tick: with no
selected player, `nextInt(adjustedTickDelay(600)) == 0` selects the tempting player; with

**`customServerAiStep`** (523–568): with a wanted move, speed modifier 0.6 → pose crouching,
not sprinting; 1.33 → standing, sprinting; else standing, not sprinting; no wanted move →
standing, not sprinting. (`Ocelot` the same.) `isSteppingCarefully` when crouching.

**Lying** (`handleLieDown`, 713–789, in `tick`, both sides): lying or relaxed and
`tickCount % 5 == 0` → purr at volume `0.6 + 0.4 · (nextFloat − nextFloat)`; the lie and
relax amounts ease (visual); `isLyingOnTopOfSleepingPlayer` from players sleeping in the
block's box inflated 2 (unused on the server).

**`CatRelaxOnOwnerGoal`** (Cat$CatRelaxOnOwnerGoal.txt):
- `canUse` (20–99): tame, not ordered to sit, the owner a player who is sleeping and within
  10 blocks (`distanceToSqr ≤ 100`), the owner's block in `#cats_can_lie_on` (beds);
  `goalPos` = that block moved opposite the bed's `FACING` (or the block itself), and no
  other cat lying or relaxed in its box inflated 2.
- `canContinueToUse` (142–168): the same owner still sleeping, the spot free.
- `start` (170–197): sitting pose off, `navigation.moveTo(goalPos, 1.100000023841858)`.
- `tick` (320–395): sitting pose off, move to the spot again; within `distanceToSqr <
  2.5` of the owner: `onBedTicks++`; past `adjustedTickDelay(16)` lying on, relaxed off;
  before that, look at the owner (45, 45) and relaxed on; farther: lying off.
- `stop` (199–241): lying off; if the owner's `getSleepTimer() >= 100` and
  `level.random.nextFloat() < cat_waking_up_gift_chance` at the cat: `giveMorningGift()`;
  `onBedTicks = 0`, relaxed off, navigation stopped.
- `giveMorningGift` (243–318): from the leash holder's block if leashed, else the cat's,
  `randomTeleport(x + nextInt(11) − 5, y + nextInt(5) − 2, z + nextInt(11) − 5, false,
  #cat_does_not_teleport_to)` (the cat's random; `LivingEntity.randomTeleport`, LivingEntity.txt 10092–10236,
  makes no random call; its search, from the target clamped to the world border down to
  a block it can stand on, then the box's collision, liquid and excluded-tag tests
  before `teleportTo`, is another section's), then the gift loot table `gameplay/cat_morning_gift` (one roll: rabbit hide,
  rabbit foot, chicken, feather, rotten flesh, string at weight 10, phantom membrane 2),
  each stack as an `ItemEntity` at `(x − Mth.sin(yBodyRot·π/180), y, z +
  Mth.cos(yBodyRot·π/180))` of the cat's new block (lambda$giveMorningGift$0, 397–434).

**`CatLieOnBlockGoal(cat, 1.1, 8)`** (CatLieOnBlockGoal.txt): a `MoveToBlockGoal` with
range 8, vertical range 6, `verticalSearchStart = −2`, flags JUMP and MOVE; usable when
tame, not ordered to sit, not lying; target a block in `#cats_can_lie_on` (beds) with air
above; `nextStartTick` 40; start: sitting pose off; tick: sitting pose off, lying while
the target is reached; stop: lying off.

**`CatSitOnBlockGoal(cat, 0.8)`** (CatSitOnBlockGoal.txt): `MoveToBlockGoal` range 8;
tame and not ordered to sit; target in `#cats_can_sit_on` (furnace, chest, beds) with air
above and: a chest with `ChestBlockEntity.getOpenCount < 1`; a furnace that is `LIT`; a
bed whose part is not `HEAD` (any other block of the tag: true). Tick: sitting pose
while reached. A cat sitting on a chest stops it opening (N6 brief 3.0 item 5).

**`OcelotAttackGoal(mob)`** (OcelotAttackGoal.txt), flags MOVE and LOOK, every tick:
usable with a target; continues while it lives, within 15 blocks (`≤ 225`) and the
navigation not done or it could start again. Tick: look at it (30, 30); `reach = (2w)²`
widened; `d²` to the target; speed 0.8, 1.33 when `reach < d² < 16`, 0.6 when `d² < 225`
otherwise; `moveTo(target, speed)`; `attackTime = max(0, attackTime − 1)`; within reach and
`attackTime <= 0`: `attackTime = 20`, `doHurtTarget`.

**Interaction** (`mobInteract`, 1014–1134):
```
if tame:
  if owned:
    if stack in #cat_collar_dyes: dye != null && dye != collar → (server) collar = dye,
        consume 1, setPersistenceRequired → SUCCESS
    elif isFood && health < max: (server) feed(…, 1, 1) → SUCCESS     // heal nutrition
    r = super; if !r.consumes: orderedToSit = !orderedToSit → SUCCESS; return r
elif isFood: (server) usePlayerItem; tryToTame; setPersistenceRequired; eat sound → SUCCESS
r = super; if r.consumes: setPersistenceRequired; return r
```
`tryToTame` (1198–1222): `nextInt(3) == 0` → tame, ordered to sit, event 7; else 6. Cat
food `#cat_food` (cod, salmon). `canMate`: tame, the other a tame cat, and `Animal`'s.
`removeWhenFarAway`: wild and `tickCount > 2400`.

**Spawn** (`finalizeSpawn`, 986–1012), in an order unlike the wolf's: **the base first**
(`TamableAnimal`… `AgeableMob`, `Mob`: their draws), then the variant at
`blockPosition()` (level random), then the sound variant (`nextInt(2)`, by
`MappedRegistry.getRandom`).

**Where cats come from**: `CatSpawner` (npc.CatSpawner.txt), a custom spawner run every
1200 ticks with a random player: a spot 8 to 31 blocks off on x and z
(`nextInt(24) + 8`, `nextBoolean` for the sign, each axis), with loaded chunks 10 around;
in a village with more than four occupied homes within 48 and fewer than five cats in a
48 × 8 × 48 box, or in a `#cats_spawn_in` structure with no cat within 16 × 8 × 16 (then
persistent). Its `spawnCat` calls `finalizeSpawn` **before** `snapTo(pos)` (183–215), so
the variant is chosen at the block (0, 0, 0): a spawner's cat in a witch hut is not
black by the structure. That is N9's (natural spawning) or N10's (villages). A **witch
hut** places its cat at generation (`SwampHutPiece.spawnCat`, 537–595): `STRUCTURE`
reason, persistent, `snapTo(x + 0.5, y, z + 0.5)` first, then `finalizeSpawn`: in the hut,
so `all_black` alone passes, and the draw `nextInt(1)` is still made.

**Saved** (467–521): the base's, `variant`, `sound_variant`, `CollarColor` (default red).
**Synched** (413–465, static 1272–1311): 20 `DATA_VARIANT_ID` (CAT_VARIANT, default
`black`), 21 `IS_LYING` (BOOLEAN), 22 `RELAX_STATE_ONE` (BOOLEAN), 23 `DATA_COLLAR_COLOR`
(INT, red 14), 24 `DATA_SOUND_VARIANT_ID` (CAT_SOUND_VARIANT, `classic`). Components
`cat/variant`, `cat/sound_variant`, `cat/collar`.

**Breeding** (903–956): variant `nextBoolean`; tame → owner, `setTame(true, true)`, mixed
collar. No sound variant (finding 12).

Monsters' fear of cats (creepers and phantoms avoid them) is on the monsters' side: N9.

**`aiStep`** (200–241): a jukebox farther than 3.46 or gone → not partying;

(visual, with a fall slowed to `y · 0.6` while airborne and falling, 259–337, both sides).

`imitateNearbyMobs(level, e)` (339–401): alive, not silent and `level.random.nextInt(2)
== 0`; the mobs in its box inflated 20 whose type is in the map; if any, one by
`nextInt(size)`; if it is not silent, its imitated sound at the parrot, volume 0.7, pitch
`getPitch(level random)`; true. Ambient (`getAmbient`, 583–607, the level's random): not
peaceful and `nextInt(1000) == 0` → a random type's imitation (finding 14), else
`parrot_ambient`. `getPitch(r)` = `(nextFloat − nextFloat) · 0.2 + 1`. Sound source neutral.
Flap sound `parrot_fly` (0.15) when `flyDist > nextFlap`, `nextFlap = flyDist + flapSpeed /
2`. No fall damage; pushable, but not by players (`doPush`).

**Taming and feeding** (`mobInteract`, 403–534):
```
if !tame && stack in #parrot_food (seeds, pitcher pod):
    usePlayerItem; unless silent the eat sound (pitch (nextFloat − nextFloat)·0.2 + 1)
    server: nextInt(10) == 0 → tame(player), event 7; else event 6 → SUCCESS
if stack in #parrot_poisonous_food (cookie):
    usePlayerItem; poison 900 ticks; if player is creative || !invulnerable:
    hurt(playerAttack(player), Float.MAX_VALUE) → SUCCESS      // the cookie kills it
if !flying && tame && owned: server: orderedToSit = !orderedToSit → SUCCESS
super
```
`isFood` is false (no breeding food). `hurtServer`: sit cleared first.

**Spawn** (59–81): variant `Util.getRandom(values, level random)` = `nextInt(5)` **first**;
no group → `AgeableMobGroupData(false)`; base. Rules: block below in
`#parrots_spawnable_on` and bright enough (541–557). Variants `$Variant`: red_blue 0, blue
1, green 2, yellow_blue 3, gray 4 (clamped `byId`), default red_blue; saved `Variant` as
the int (810–837). Synched 20 `DATA_VARIANT_ID` (INT, 0). Component `parrot/variant`.

**`ShoulderRidingEntity`**: `rideCooldownCounter` counts every tick from 0 (not saved);
`canSitOnShoulder()` = counter > 100 (72–93). `LandOnOwnersShoulderGoal`
(LandOnOwnersShoulderGoal.txt): usable when the owner is a server player not spectator,
not flying, not in water or powder snow, the parrot not ordered to sit and able; not
interruptible once seated; tick: unless seated, sitting or leashed, if its box meets the
owner's, `setEntityOnShoulder(owner)`.

`setEntityOnShoulder(player)` (ShoulderRidingEntity.txt 17–70): its save without id plus
`id`, offered to `ServerPlayer.setEntityOnShoulder(tag)` (n6 1533–1578): refused while the
player rides, is off the ground, in water or powder snow; else the left shoulder if empty,
else the right, with `timeEntitySatOnShoulder = gameTime`; on success the parrot is
discarded. The player then (`handleShoulderEntities`, from `Player.aiStep`, n6
1446–1476): plays each shoulder's ambient (`nextInt(200) == 0` of the player's random;
a parrot that is not silent: an imitation if `imitateNearbyMobs` succeeds, else
`getAmbient(level, level.random)`, volume 1, pitch `getPitch(player random)`); and drops
them (`removeEntitiesOnShoulder`, 1580–1609, only once `timeEntitySatOnShoulder + 20 <
gameTime`) when falling more than 0.5, in water, flying, sleeping or in powder snow;
`Player.hurtServer` drops them too (Player.txt 1511–1520), and a riptide spin. A dropped
parrot is made again from its compound (`EntityType.create` with reason `LOAD`) at the
player's position (`respawnEntityOnShoulder`, 1611–1661). Saved with the player as
`ShoulderEntityLeft` and `ShoulderEntityRight` (n6 434–449, 529–546); the player's
synched data shows the variants: `Avatar` 15 main hand, 16 model customisation; `Player`
17 absorption, 18 score, 19 `DATA_SHOULDER_PARROT_LEFT`, 20 `…_RIGHT`
(`OPTIONAL_UNSIGNED_INT`, the parrot's variant id) (Player static, Avatar static in n5).

### 5.9 Horses: state, goals, attributes (AbstractHorse.txt, 2780 lines)

**State**: synched `DATA_ID_FLAGS` (BYTE, index 18; static 2775–2778): bit 2 tame, 8 bred,
16 eating, 32 standing, 64 mouth open (222–270). Fields: `temper` (0), `owner`
(`EntityReference`), `inventory`, `playerJumpPendingScale`, `allowStandSliding`,
`canGallop` (true; false for chested ones), counters `eatingCounter`, `mouthCounter`,
`standCounter`, `tailCounter`, `sprintCounter`, `gallopSoundCounter` (none saved), the
animation floats `eatAnim`, `standAnim`, `mouthAnim` and their previous values.

**Attributes** (`createBaseHorseAttributes`, 760–781): jump strength 0.7, max health 53,
speed 0.22499999403953552, step height 1, safe fall distance 6, fall damage multiplier 0.5.
Chested (`createBaseChestedHorseAttributes`, AbstractChestedHorse.txt 64–73): speed
0.17499999701976776, jump 0.5. Skeleton horse: health 15, speed 0.2000000029802322
(SkeletonHorse.txt 37–46). Zombie horse: health 25 (ZombieHorse.txt 23–29). Llama: the
chested ones. The randomised base values replace these at spawn (5.11). Max spawn cluster
6. Ambient interval 400. Volume 0.8.

**Goals** (`registerGoals`, 105–175; `addBehaviourGoals` 177–207): 1
`RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal(1.2)`; 2 `BreedGoal(1.0, AbstractHorse)`; 4 `FollowParentGoal(1.0)`;
6 `WaterAvoidingRandomStrollGoal(0.7)`; 7 `LookAtPlayerGoal(Player, 6)`; 8
`RandomLookAroundGoal`; 9 `RandomStandGoal` if `canPerformRearing()`; then behaviour goals:
0 `FloatGoal`; 1 `MountPanicGoal(1.2)` (a `PanicGoal` unless mob-controlled); 3
`TemptGoal(1.25, #horse_tempt_items, false)` (golden carrot, golden apple, enchanted golden
apple). Skeleton horses add no behaviour goals (and gain `SkeletonTrapGoal` at 1 while a
trap); zombie horses: 0 `FloatGoal`, 3 `TemptGoal(1.25, #zombie_horse_food, false)`; llamas
have their own list (5.16).

**`RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal(horse, 1.2)`**, flag MOVE (RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal.txt 29–175):
usable when not mob-controlled, not tame and ridden, and `DefaultRandomPos.getPos(horse,
5, 4)` gives a spot (section 3); start: `moveTo(spot, 1.2)`; continues while not tame, the
navigation not done and ridden. **Tick** (taming by riding):
```
if !tame && nextInt(adjustedTickDelay(50)) == 0:
    p = first passenger; if p == null: return
    if p is Player:
        if maxTemper > 0 && nextInt(maxTemper) < temper: tameWithName(p); return
        modifyTemper(5)
    ejectPassengers(); makeMad(); event 6
```
`modifyTemper(d)` clamps to `[0, maxTemper]` (429–444). `tameWithName(p)` (1685–1709):
owner, tamed flag, the advancement, event 7.

`RandomStandGoal` (RandomStandGoal.txt), ticked every tick: `nextStand` starts at
`−getAmbientStandInterval()` (−400); `canUse`: `nextStand++`; if `nextStand > 0 &&
nextInt(1000) < nextStand`: reset to −400, and true if not immobile and `nextInt(10) ==
0`; never continues; start: `standIfPossible()` and the ambient stand sound.

`standIfPossible()` (1651–1666): rearing allowed (not llamas) and on the server →
`setStanding(20)`: eating off, flag 32 on, `standCounter = 20`. `makeMad()` (1668–1683):
not standing, server: `standIfPossible`, angry sound. `hurtServer` (599–617): a hurt that
took → `nextInt(3) == 0` → stand. `isImmobile()` (1091–1111): `(dead && ridden && saddled)
|| eating || standing` (llamas: dead or eating). `isPushable()`: not ridden.

**`aiStep`** (1165–1246): `nextInt(200) == 0` → tail counter 1 (both sides); base; on the
server and alive: `nextInt(900) == 0 && deathTime == 0` → heal 1; if it can eat grass (not
llamas): not eating, not ridden and `nextInt(300) == 0` and on a grass block → eating on;
eating: after 50 ticks off; then `followMommy` (finding 13).

**`tick`** (1296–1533), both sides, after the base: mouth counter to 30 then the mouth flag
off; `standCounter` down to 0 then `clearStanding()`; tail counter to 8; sprint counter
to 300; the eat, stand and mouth animations ease (`eatAnim += (1 − eatAnim)·0.4 + 0.05`,
and so on, clamped to 0..1; standing sets `eatAnim = 0`; not standing clears
`allowStandSliding` and eases `standAnim += ((0.8·s·s·s − s)·0.6 − 0.05)`). The stand
animation moves the rider (`getPassengerAttachmentPoint`, 2646–2680: `+(0, 0.15 ·
standAnimO · scale, −0.7 · standAnimO · scale)` turned by `−yRot`), so the server needs it.

**Sounds**: step (634–723): not on liquid; the block above's sound if snow; ridden and
able to gallop: `gallopSoundCounter++`, past 5 every third step the gallop (a horse also
`nextInt(10) == 0` breathes, Horse.txt 208–232), up to 5 the wooden step; else wooden
blocks' step, else step or baby step, at volume 0.15 · the sound type's. Jump 0.4. Land:
`causeFallDamage` (495–533) above 1 block the land sound (0.4), then fall damage by the
attributes, passed to the passengers.

### 5.10 Feeding (`handleEating`, 850–1064; `fedFood`, 826–848)

`fedFood`: `handleEating` and, if it ate, the item consumed (1); `SUCCESS_SERVER` if it ate
or on the client, else `PASS`. The table (heal, age-up seconds, temper):

| item | heal | age | temper | breeds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wheat | 2 | 20 | 3 | |
| sugar | 1 | 30 | 3 | |
| hay block | 20 | 180 | 0 | |
| apple | 3 | 60 | 3 | |
| red mushroom | 3 | 0 | 3 | |
| carrot | 3 | 60 | 3 | |
| golden carrot | 4 | 60 | 5 | tamed, adult (`getAge() == 0`), not in love → love |
| golden apple, enchanted golden apple | 10 | 240 | 10 | the same |

Then: health below max and heal > 0 → heal, ate. Baby, age > 0 and not age-locked →
happy-villager particle (three draws for its place on the client; on the server
`getRandomX/Y/Z` still draw) and, server, `ageUp(age)`, ate. Temper > 0 and (ate or not
tamed) and temper below max, server → `modifyTemper`, ate. Ate → `eating()` (mouth open,
eat sound with pitch draws) and game event `eat`. Horse food tag `#horse_food`; zombie
horses `#zombie_horse_food` (red mushroom); llamas 5.16.

### 5.11 Spawn: variant, markings, attributes

`AbstractHorse.finalizeSpawn` (2608–2627): no group → `AgeableMobGroupData(0.2f)` (the
second and later of a group a baby when `nextFloat() <= 0.2`); `randomizeAttributes(level
random)`; then `Animal`'s (`AgeableMob.finalizeSpawn`, AgeableMob.txt 44–81: the baby draw
from the level's random when the group wants babies and already has one; then `Mob`'s).

`Horse.finalizeSpawn` (482–518), level random `r`:
```
if group is HorseGroupData: variant = group's
else: variant = Variant.values()[r.nextInt(7)]; group = HorseGroupData(variant)  // babies 0.05
markings = Markings.values()[r.nextInt(5)]
setVariantAndMarkings(variant, markings)
AbstractHorse.finalizeSpawn(…, group)       // randomizeAttributes, then the baby draw
```
A herd shares its coat, not its markings. `Variant`: white 0, creamy 1, chestnut 2, brown
3, black 4, gray 5, dark brown 6; `Markings`: none 0, white 1, white field 2, white dots 3,
black dots 4 (both `byId` wrap). `DATA_ID_TYPE_VARIANT` (INT, index 19) = `(variant & 255)
| ((markings << 8) & 0xFF00)` (110–125), saved as `Variant`.

`randomizeAttributes(r)` by kind, each `setBaseValue`:
- **Horse** (Horse.txt 17–50): max health `generateMaxHealth(r::nextInt)` = `15.0f +
  (float)r.nextInt(8) + (float)r.nextInt(9)` (float arithmetic, then widened), so 15 to
  30; speed `generateSpeed(r::nextDouble)` = `(0.44999998807907104 + a·0.3 + b·0.3 +
  c·0.3) · 0.25` (left to right, each `nextDouble`), 0.1125 to 0.3375; jump
  `generateJumpStrength` = `0.4000000059604645 + a·0.2 + b·0.2 + c·0.2`, 0.4 to 1.0
  (2335–2390). Order: health, speed, jump.
- **Donkey, mule, llama** (AbstractChestedHorse.txt 36–49): health only (two draws); speed
  and jump stay the chested defaults 0.175 and 0.5.
- **Skeleton horse** (SkeletonHorse.txt 72–84): jump only.
- **Zombie horse** (ZombieHorse.txt 54–118): jump `0.5 + (a + b + c)·0.06666666666666667`
  (each added in turn), then speed `(9.0 + a + b + c) / 42.15999984741211`.
The `IntUnaryOperator` and `DoubleSupplier` are method references to `r.nextInt` and
`r.nextDouble` (**Inferred** from the `invokedynamic` capturing `r`).

**Llama** (`finalizeSpawn`, Llama.txt 507–542), level random: `setRandomStrength`
(48–66): `n = nextFloat() < 0.04f ? 5 : 3`; strength `1 + nextInt(n)` (clamped 1..5); then
variant from `LlamaGroupData` or `Llama$Variant.values()[nextInt(4)]` (creamy 0, white 1,
brown 2, gray 3; clamped; default creamy) with a new `LlamaGroupData` (babies 0.05); then
`AbstractChestedHorse`'s (health). **Trader llama** (TraderLlama.txt 214–235): reason
`EVENT` → `setAge(0)`; no group → `AgeableMobGroupData(false)`, which the llama's then
replaces with its own (babies at 0.05 from the second).

**Zombie horse** (182–233): reason `NATURAL` → a zombie made with reason `JOCKEY`, placed
at the horse (yaw, pitch 0), its own `finalizeSpawn(level, difficulty, JOCKEY, null)` (its
draws first), an iron spear in its main hand, `startRiding(horse, false, false)`; then the
horse's. N9's.

### 5.12 Breeding horses

`canParent()` (1992–2018): not ridden, not riding, tamed, adult, at full health, in love.
`canMate`: a horse with a horse or donkey (Horse.txt 345–370), a donkey with a donkey or
horse (Donkey.txt 36–61), a llama with a llama (Llama.txt 623–643), both `canParent`;
mules, skeleton and zombie horses cannot (`AbstractHorse.canMate` false; zombie horses
cannot fall in love). The foal is made by `getBreedOffspring` of the parent that runs the
breed (section 2's `BreedGoal`); no `finalizeSpawn`; not tamed; `Bred` not set (finding
13).

**Horse × horse** (Horse.txt 372–461), all draws of **this parent's own random**:
```
k = nextInt(9): variant = k < 4 ? this : k < 8 ? partner : values()[nextInt(7)]
k = nextInt(5): markings = k < 2 ? this : k < 4 ? partner : values()[nextInt(5)]
setVariantAndMarkings; setOffspringAttributes(partner, foal)
```
Horse × donkey → mule, donkey × horse → mule, donkey × donkey → donkey: attributes only.
**Llama** (Llama.txt 645–692): `setOffspringAttributes` first, then strength `nextInt(max(
sA, sB)) + 1`, `+1` if `nextFloat() < 0.03f` (clamped to 5), variant `nextBoolean ? this
: partner`. A trader llama's foal is a persistent trader llama (`makeNewLlama`).

**`setOffspringAttributes(partner, foal)`** (2030–2080): for max health in `[15.0, 30.0]`,
then jump strength in `[(double)0.4f, (double)1.0f]` = `[0.4000000059604645, 1.0]`, then
speed in `[(double)0.1125f, (double)0.3375f]` = `[0.11249999701976776,
0.3375000059604645]` (the statics, 2742–2765, are floats widened; **Inferred** the
lambdas behind `#1` to `#6`: zeros for the minimums and ones for the maximums), the foal's
base is `createOffspringAttribute(this's base, partner's base, min, max, this.random)`
(2082–2168):
```
if max <= min: throw
a = clamp(a, min, max); b = clamp(b, min, max)
margin = 0.15 · (max − min)
spread = |a − b| + margin · 2.0
mean = (a + b) / 2.0
r = (nextDouble() + nextDouble() + nextDouble()) / 3.0 − 0.5
v = mean + spread · r
if v > max: return max − (v − max)
if v < min: return min + (min − v)
return v
```
Nine draws in all, three per attribute. Java's `Math.abs` and plain `double` arithmetic;
no fused operations.

### 5.13 Equipment and what a click does

**Slots a horse may use** (`canUseSlot`, 357–378): `SADDLE` only when alive, adult and
tamed; others as `Animal`. `Horse`, `Llama`, `SkeletonHorse`, `ZombieHorse` override it to
true for every slot (Horse.txt 463–466, Llama.txt 613–616, …): the item's allowed entities
are what stop a llama's saddle. `isEquippableInSlot(stack, slot)` (LivingEntity.txt
10755–10792): no `equippable` → main hand only; else the component's slot is `slot`,
`canUseSlot` and `equippable.canBeEquippedBy(type)`. **Tags**: `#can_equip_saddle` (horse,
skeleton and zombie horse, donkey, mule, pig, strider, camel, camel husk, nautilus, zombie
nautilus), `#can_wear_horse_armor` (horse, zombie horse); which tag or list each item's
`allowed_entities` names: the saddle `#can_equip_saddle`, carpets llama and trader llama
(Equippable.txt 68–119, below); horse and wolf armour by `Item$Properties` methods not
dumped (12.5). None of it is in Clustine's extraction yet.

**Dispensers**: `canDispenserEquipIntoSlot` (396–414): `BODY`, or `SADDLE` when tamed, or
`Animal`'s. N6's equipment dispensing then puts saddles and armour on horses.

**`AbstractHorse.mobInteract`** (1535–1595):
```
if ridden || baby: return Animal.mobInteract
if tamed && player.isSecondaryUseActive(): openCustomInventoryScreen(player) → SUCCESS
if !stack.isEmpty:
    r = stack.interactLivingEntity(player, this, hand)     // equippable with equip_on_interact
    if r.consumesAction: return r
    if equippable in BODY && !wearing body armour: equipBodyArmor → SUCCESS
doPlayerRide(player) → SUCCESS
```
`ItemStack.interactLivingEntity` (ItemStack.txt 1044–1074): an `equippable` with
`equip_on_interact` → `Equippable.equipOnTarget(player, entity, stack)` (Equippable.txt
259–299): `PASS` unless the target `isEquippableInSlot(stack, slot)`, has nothing in that
slot and is alive; then on the server `setItemSlot(slot, stack.split(1))`, and a `Mob`
gets `setGuaranteedDrop(slot)`; `SUCCESS`. **`split`, not `consume`: a creative player's
saddle is used up.** A result other than `PASS` returns; else the item's own (lead, name
tag, …). `canBeEquippedBy(type)` (301–317): no `allowed_entities` → anyone, else the set
contains the type.

The components (Equippable.txt): **saddle** (`saddle()`, 97–119): slot `SADDLE`, sound
`horse_saddle`, allowed `#can_equip_saddle`, `equip_on_interact`, `can_be_sheared` with
sound `saddle_unequip` (Items.txt 9111). **Carpets** (`llamaSwag(dye)`, 68–95): slot
`BODY`, sound `llama_swag`, allowed llama and trader llama, `can_be_sheared` (sound
`llama_carpet_unequip`), not equip-on-interact: a carpet goes on by
`AbstractHorse.mobInteract`'s `BODY` branch. **Horse armour** and **wolf armour** are made
by `Item$Properties.horseArmor(material)` and `wolfArmor(material)` (Items.txt 12188–12229,
9519), which are not dumped: their allowed entities, `equip_on_interact` and shearing are
not read (12.5). `equipBodyArmor` (380–394): `setItemSlotAndDropWhenKilled(BODY, consumeAndReturn(1))`.
`doPlayerRide` (1066–1089): eating off, standing cleared; server: the player's yaw and pitch
set to the horse's, `player.startRiding(this)`. `addPassenger` (1782–1795) then snaps the
passenger's rotation to the horse's view rotation.

`Horse.mobInteract` (284–343) and `AbstractChestedHorse.mobInteract` (230–302) put first:
```
secondary = !baby && tamed && player.isSecondaryUseActive()
if ridden || secondary || (baby && player.isHolding(golden_dandelion)): AbstractHorse's
if !stack.isEmpty:
    if isFood(stack): fedFood
    if !tamed: makeMad → SUCCESS
    (chested) if !hasChest && stack is chest: equipChest → SUCCESS
AbstractHorse's
```
`SkeletonHorse.mobInteract` (297–308): untamed → `PASS`. `ZombieHorse` (235–287): as the
horse, without the dandelion test; `interact` (31–40) makes it persistent first.
`TraderLlama.doPlayerRide` (115–127): refused while leashed to a wandering trader.

**Saddle sound** `horse_saddle` (`getEquipSound` for `SADDLE`, 585–597). **Death drops**
(`dropEquipment`, 1127–1163): the base's (equipment), then every inventory stack without
`prevent_equipment_drop`; chested ones then a chest block, and the chest flag off
(AbstractChestedHorse.txt 108–124).

**Armour on a horse** is protection by the armour's attributes (`LivingEntity`'s), the
horse's `hurtArmor` damaging `BODY` (Horse.txt 468–480). Wolf armour 5.4.

### 5.14 Chests on donkeys, mules and llamas; the inventory

`AbstractChestedHorse` (AbstractChestedHorse.txt): synched `DATA_ID_CHEST` (BOOLEAN, index
19, false); `canGallop = false`; baby dimensions: the type's with the passenger at (0,
height + 0.03125, −0.3125), scaled 0.5 (9–34). `equipChest(player, stack)` (304–317):
chest flag on, the chest sound (`donkey_chest`, llama `llama_chest`, pitch draws), consume
1, `createInventory()`. `getSlot(499)` is the chest as a slot access (an item stack of
`chest` while it has one; setting empty removes it and remakes the inventory, setting a
chest adds it) (215–228, $1 382–432); `getSlot(500 + i)` the inventory's slot `i`
(AbstractHorse.txt 2397–2418). `createInventory()` (542–583) makes a new container of the
size and copies over the old one's stacks that fit. Saved (126–213): `ChestedHorse`, and
with a chest `Items` (each `Slot` and stack); read: flag, new inventory, stacks that fit.

**Opening** (`openCustomInventoryScreen`, 803–824): server, (not ridden or ridden by this
player) and tamed → `player.openHorseInventory(this, inventory)`: close any open menu,
next container id, send `mount_screen_open(containerId, getInventoryColumns(), entity id)`,
open `HorseInventoryMenu(id, playerInventory, inventory, horse, columns)` and `initMenu`
(n6 ServerPlayer 3266–3307). Also by `PlayerCommand OPEN_INVENTORY` from a player whose
vehicle `HasCustomInventoryScreen` (SGPLI 5304–5317).

**The menu** (`HorseInventoryMenu`, HorseInventoryMenu.txt 9–108, a
`AbstractMountInventoryMenu` with menu type null): slot 0 the saddle (an anonymous slot
class `$1` over `horse.createEquipmentSlotContainer(SADDLE)`, at (8, 18), sprite
`container/slot/saddle`), slot 1 the body (`$2` over the `BODY` container, at (8, 36),
sprite `llama_armor` for a llama, else `horse_armor`): **both always present**, whatever
the horse can wear; then, if `columns > 0`, three rows of `columns` slots of the horse's
inventory, container index `column + row · columns`, at (80 + 18·column, 18 + 18·row);
then the player's standard slots at (8, 84) (27 then 9). Opening calls the container's
`startOpen`, closing its `stopOpen` (AbstractMountInventoryMenu.txt 15–80).
`getInventorySize(columns) = columns · 3` (237–242). `stillValid` (44–69): the horse's
inventory unchanged (`hasInventoryChanged`, AbstractHorse.txt 2629–2638: the same
container object), the container valid for the player, the horse alive and
`player.isWithinEntityInteractionRange(horse, 4.0)`. What `$1` and `$2` accept
(`mayPlace`, `isActive`, max stack size) is not dumped (12.5).

**Shift-click** (`quickMoveStack`, 82–235), `inv = 2 + container size`:
```
from a slot below inv (saddle, body, chest): move to [inv, slots.size) from the end;
    fails → EMPTY
else (player's slots):
    if slot 1 may take it and is empty: move into [1, 2); fails → EMPTY
    elif slot 0 may take it and is empty: move into [0, 1); fails → EMPTY
    elif container size != 0 and moving into [2, inv) succeeds: done
    main = [inv, inv + 27), hotbar = [inv + 27, inv + 36):
    from the hotbar: move into main; from main: move into the hotbar;
    else: move into [inv + 27, inv + 27)  (an empty range: nothing)
    return EMPTY whether these last moves succeed or not       // no setChanged
done: the slot emptied (setByPlayer(EMPTY)) or setChanged; return the copy
```
A move inside the player's slots returns `EMPTY` at once, so the click's loop stops after
one move and the slot is not marked changed.

### 5.15 Riding a horse, and how it differs from N5's vehicles

What N5 built for boats (n5-brief sections 1, 2): `startRiding`, seats by order,
`positionRider`, the dismount helpers, `handleMoveVehicle`'s checks, `handlePlayerInput`'s
sneak dismount, `ClientboundMoveVehicle` corrections. A horse adds or changes:

1. **Who steers**: saddled and a player first (finding 5). The client drives a saddled
   horse exactly as it drives a boat (`isClientAuthoritative`), and `handleMoveVehicle`'s
   controlling branch applies with the horse as root; its `move` uses the horse's
   `maxUpStep()` = `max(STEP_HEIGHT, 1.0)` while a player controls it (LivingEntity.txt
   11025–11041), and the accepted move's `doCheckFallDamage` gives the horse its fall
   damage (safe fall 6, ×0.5) and its passengers theirs (`propagateFallToPassengers`).
2. **The server's tick of a controlled horse** (finding 6): no AI, zero motion, rotation
   from the rider. `positionRider` (2317–2333) also sets the rider's `yBodyRot` to the
   horse's; the rider's seat is the type's passenger point plus the rearing offset (5.9).
3. **Input**: the client reads `xxa · 0.5` sideways and `zza` (× 0.25 backwards) and
   nothing while standing on the ground without a pending jump unless `allowStandSliding`
   (`getRiddenInput`, 1797–1839); speed is the movement speed attribute
   (`getRiddenSpeed`, 1841–1847); flying speed `speed · 0.1` (LivingEntity.txt 7335–7347).
   **Client**, but the server's `travelRidden` computes the same input and drops it.
4. **Jumps** (finding 7): `PlayerRideableJumping.getPlayerJumpPendingScale(power)` =
   `power >= 90 ? 1.0 : 0.4 + 0.4 · power / 90` (PlayerRideableJumping.txt);
   `executeRidersJump(scale, input)` (1849–1906): `motion.y = getJumpPower(scale)` =
   `jumpStrength · scale · blockJumpFactor + jumpBoost` (LivingEntity.txt 6107–6121), and
   with forward input `+(−0.4·sin(yaw)·scale, 0, 0.4·cos(yaw)·scale)` (`Mth.sin`, `Mth.cos`
   of `yRot · 0.017453292f`). Both the client's. The server: rear (20 ticks of the standing
   flag) and the jump sound.
5. **Inventory key** opens the horse's menu (5.14); N5 had it for chest boats.
6. **Dismount** (`getDismountLocationForPassenger`, 2544–2602): first the side of the
   rider's main arm (`getCollisionHorizontalEscapeVector(horse width, rider width, yRot
   ± 90)`: +90 for a right-handed rider), then the other side, then the horse's position.
   `getDismountLocationInDirection(v, rider)` (2440–2542): from `(x + v.x, box.minY, z +
   v.z)`, for each of the rider's dismount poses, climbing block by block while below
   `box.maxY + 0.75`: a valid floor (`DismountHelper.isBlockFloorValid`) where the pose's
   box fits (`canDismountTo`) → set the pose, return `(x', floorY, z')`. N5's helpers
   (`riding.rs` 894–1066) apply.
7. **Water**: horses, donkeys, mules, llamas, trader llamas and zombie horses are in
   `#dismounts_underwater` (the rider is put off when the horse's eyes go under, n5-brief
   1.1); horses, zombie horses, mules, donkeys and camels in `#can_float_while_ridden`
   (a `LivingEntity` rule of another section).
8. **Leads**: a horse is leashed by four points (`supportQuadLeash`,
   `createQuadLeashOffsets(0.04, 0.52, 0.23, 0.87)`, chested `(0.04, 0.41, 0.18, 0.73)`,
   llamas not), and an elastic pull stops it eating (301–311). N5's leashes held only
   boats.
9. **Tracking**: horse tracking range 10 chunks, update interval 3 (entity_types.rs); a
   ridden horse is shown as far as its rider (n5-brief 1.0 item 11).

### 5.16 Llamas, caravans, spit, the trader llama

**Goals** (Llama.txt 118–238, replacing the horse's): 0 `FloatGoal`; 1
`RunAroundLikeCrazyGoal(1.2)`; 2 `LlamaFollowCaravanGoal(2.0999999046325684)`; 3
`RangedAttackGoal(1.25, 40, 20)`; 3 `PanicGoal(1.2)`; 4 `BreedGoal(1.0)`; 5
`TemptGoal(1.25, #llama_tempt_items (hay block), false)`; 6 `FollowParentGoal(1.0)`; 7
`WaterAvoidingRandomStrollGoal(0.7)`; 8 `LookAtPlayerGoal(Player, 6)`; 9
`RandomLookAroundGoal`. Targets: 1 `LlamaHurtByTargetGoal` (a `HurtByTargetGoal` that stops
once it has spat, clearing `didSpit`); 2 `LlamaAttackWolfGoal`
(`NearestAttackableTargetGoal(Wolf, 16, false, true, wild wolves)` whose follow distance
is a quarter of the base's). Trader llama adds (TraderLlama.txt 64–106): goal 1
`PanicGoal(2.0)`; targets 1 `TraderLlamaDefendWanderingTraderGoal` (the trader it is leashed
to: its last hurt-by mob, by timestamp, as the owner goals do), 2
`NearestAttackableTargetGoal(Zombie, true, not zombified piglins)`, 2
`NearestAttackableTargetGoal(AbstractIllager, true)`.

Not grazing (`canEatGrass` false), no rearing, `maxTemper` 30; fall damage only from 6
blocks (806–834); immobile when dead or eating. `followMommy` only for a baby not in a
caravan. Leash follow speed 2.0. Passengers sit at the type's point (the default rule,
957–964). Leash offset (0, 0.75·eye, 0.5·width).

**Feeding** (`handleEating`, 339–492): wheat → age 10, temper 3, heal 2; hay block → age
90, temper 6, heal 10, and love if tamed, adult and able; then as the horse's (heal, age
up a baby, temper while wild or when it ate). The eat sound with pitch draws when it ate.
Food `#llama_food` (wheat, hay block).

**Spit** (`spit(target)`, 704–797; `performRangedAttack`): a `LlamaSpit` projectile from
the llama towards `(dx, target.y(1/3) − spit.y + 0.2·horizontal distance, dz)` at
power 1.5 and inaccuracy `rangedAttackUncertainty` = 10, with
`Projectile.spawnProjectileUsingShoot` (draws of the projectile: N9); the spit sound with
pitch draws; `didSpit = true`. **`LlamaSpit` is a projectile, N9's.** What it is
(LlamaSpit.txt, 253 lines): owner the llama; placed at `(x − (width + 1)·0.5 ·
Mth.sin(yBodyRot · 0.017453292f), eyeY − 0.10000000149011612, z + (width + 1)·0.5 ·
Mth.cos(…))` (11–62); each tick after `Projectile.tick` it finds what its move hits
(`ProjectileUtil.getHitResultOnMoveVector`), acts on it, turns, and is discarded when
no block state in its box is air (`findBlocksIn(box).filterState(…).noneMatched()`,
**Inferred** the predicate is `isAir`, a method reference) or when it is in water; else
motion × 0.99 (air drag), gravity
0.06 (64–139); hitting an entity with a living owner deals 1.0 of damage source `spit`
and the owner's post-attack enchantment effects (146–188); hitting a block discards it on
the server (190–201).

**Caravans** (`LlamaFollowCaravanGoal`, LlamaFollowCaravanGoal.txt), flag MOVE:
- `canUse` (27–156): not leashed and not in a caravan; among llamas and trader llamas in
  its box inflated (9, 4, 9) (`getEntities` order): the nearest already in a caravan and
  without a tail; failing that, the nearest leashed one without a tail; none, or nearer
  than 2 (`< 4`), → false; if that one is not leashed, it must be within eight links of a
  leashed head (`firstIsLeashed(it, 1)`); then `joinCaravan(it)` (head set, its tail set).
- `canContinueToUse` (158–220): in a caravan, the head alive, a leashed head within eight;
  beyond 26 blocks (`> 676`): while `speedModifier <= 3`, `speed ·= 1.2` and a
  `reducedTickDelay(40)` grace, else stop after the grace runs out.
- `stop`: leave the caravan, speed 2.1. `tick` (232–311): in a caravan, not tied to a
  fence knot: move to the head's position offset towards it by `max(distance − 2, 0)`
  (normalised direction from the llama to the head).

**Trader llama** (TraderLlama.txt): `despawnDelay` 47999, saved `DespawnDelay`; `aiStep`
(server) `maybeDespawn`: when despawnable (not tamed, not leashed to anything but a
wandering trader, not ridden by exactly one player, not age-locked, not persistent), the
delay is the trader's delay − 1 while leashed to one, else its own − 1; at 0 the leash is
removed and the llama discarded. In Clustine the delay is a counter to derive ("until
tick", n-plan 3.3). Wandering traders and their spawner are N10's.

### 5.17 Skeleton horses, the trap, zombie horses (names)

`SkeletonHorse` (SkeletonHorse.txt): `isTrap`, `trapTime` saved as `SkeletonTrap` and
`SkeletonTrapTime`; `setTrap(true)` adds `SkeletonTrapGoal` at goal priority 1, false
removes it; a trap not persistent is discarded when `trapTime++ >= 18000` (aiStep,
192–213). Water slow-down 0.96 (it swims), swim and gallop-in-water sounds, jump in water
`skeleton_horse_jump_water`. Spawn rules: from a spawner (and not ignoring light) bright
enough, else the animal rules. Cannot age up; untamed cannot be ridden.
`SkeletonTrapGoal` (SkeletonTrapGoal.txt): usable when a live player is within 10;
tick: trap off, tamed, adult; a visual-only lightning bolt at it; a skeleton rider; three
more skeleton horses each with a skeleton rider, pushed by `triangle(0, 1.1485)` on x and z
(the trap horse's random); all `TRIGGERED`, invulnerable for 60 ticks, persistent;
skeletons with an iron helmet if they wore nothing on their head, their main hand and head
enchanted by `mob_spawn_equipment` (their own random). The trap comes from a thunderstorm's
lightning (`ServerLevel`'s weather), so it waits for weather and monsters: N9 and later.

`ZombieHorse` (ZombieHorse.txt): health 25; jump and speed as 5.11; `removeWhenFarAway`
true (made persistent when used); mob-controlled when its first passenger is a mob;
leashable when tamed or not mob-controlled; protected from the sun by `BODY` (N9's
burning); `chargeSpeedModifier` 1.4; cannot breed or age up. The natural jockey (5.11) is
N9's.

Camels (`animal.camel.Camel`, an `AbstractHorse` with a brain and a dash on
`handleStopJump`) and nautiluses (`AbstractNautilus`, `openNautilusInventory`) use the
same riding and inventory paths and are not read here (12.5).
