   266–274, LevelReader.txt 258–266). It looks its liked player up by UUID in the whole level
   (`Level.getEntity(UUID)`, the level's entity lookup at any distance, Level.txt
   1386–1393) and accepts them within 64 blocks. A region has its
   own land and one chunk of copies (n-plan 3.5): both reads can fall outside (11.7).
   The note block is liked only from a vibration heard within 16 blocks, and
   `StayCloseToTarget` pulls the allay back when it strays more than 16 from it, so in
   play it stays near; the porter has to decide what a read outside the region means
   (proposed: "not known", which the game never has: keep the memory, do not deposit).
6. **The happy ghast is two different mobs.** A ghastling (baby) has a brain and no
   goals; an adult has goals (float, tempt, the ghast's random float) and its brain is
   never ticked (`customServerAiStep` ticks it only `isBaby()`). Crossing the age
   boundary (`ageBoundaryReached`) swaps the move control, look control and navigation,
   removes all goals, and for the adult re-registers goals, stops all running
   behaviours and clears all memories (7.11.3). The adult's navigation is `Mob`'s
   default ground navigation (`HappyGhast` overrides only the baby's).
7. **The adult happy ghast moves as a ghast, by impulses, not by paths**
   (`Ghast$GhastMoveControl`, `Ghast$RandomFloatAroundGoal`, 7.11.2): every 2 to 6 ticks
   it adds `flyingSpeed × 5 / 3` toward its wanted point if a "careful" sweep of the
   blocks finds nothing it avoids (`#happy_ghast_avoids`: sweet berry bush, cactus,
   wither rose, magma block, fire, pointed dripstone, sulfur spike; water unless it is
   in water; lava unless in lava); its wander targets are up to 16 blocks away on each
   axis, inside its home, in air within 15 blocks of a block along an axis, and are
   pulled down to its own height when they lie above the ground's surface. The sweep
   reads every block of its box moved to the target and grown by one: up to about 17
   blocks away, across a line (11.7).
8. **A happy ghast with a harness carries up to four riders, steered by the first
   player** (`getControllingPassenger`), with input from the client (`getRiddenInput`
   reads the player's `xxa`, `zza`, pitch and jump: the client drives it, as a player's
   boat in N5). When a player stands on top or gets off, it **stays still** for 10 ticks
   after the last such moment (`serverStillTimeout`), sends an exact position packet when
   it begins to stay still, snaps its yaw to a multiple of 90°, and becomes a solid
   collider for entities (`canBeCollidedWith`). Several players in one vehicle crossing a
   line is the case ADR-0028 left to N3's design (11.7).
9. (Every `Behavior` start draws the level's random, 7.0.1 point 4: a sniffer's `Searching` (600 to 600) and `FinishedDigging` (40 to 40) and an allay's `GoAndGiveItemsToTarget` (20 to 20) draw `nextInt(1)` each time they start; the allay's throw sound draws twice more from the level's random, 7.10.6.)
10. **The allay hears note blocks through the vibration system, and jukeboxes through a
    second listener.** Clustine's vibrations (`region/vibrations.rs`) have block entities
    as listeners only; an entity's listeners move with it, re-registered by section as it
    moves (`DynamicGameEventListener`, 7.10.6).
11. (`ActivityData`'s numbering is read: 7.1.4.)
12. **Duplication in creative**: `Allay.removeInteractionItem` is `stack.consume(1,
    player)`, which takes nothing from a creative player (7.10.5), so a creative player
    duplicates allays with one shard as often as the 6000-tick cooldown allows. Items the
    allay is given are also kept by a creative player (the same call).
13. **Sounds that leave out the interacting player.** The allay's duplication chime and
    "item given/taken" sounds are played with `Level.playSound(player, entity, …)`: the
    interacting player is left out (their client plays them itself). The edge must not
    send them to that player.

#### 7.0.5 The nautilus, the zombie nautilus and the copper golem (7.12, 7.13)

(Files are named by their simple class name; `TIBC.txt` is `ai.behavior.TransportItemsBetweenContainers.txt`.)

1. **Two of the golem's memories are sets, and they are saved.** `VISITED_BLOCK_POSITIONS`
   and `UNREACHABLE_TRANSPORT_BLOCK_POSITIONS` are `MemoryModuleType<Set<GlobalPos>>`
   registered with `GlobalPos.CODEC.listOf().xmap(…)` (MemoryModuleType.txt 470–483), and are
   saved in the brain with their time to live (6,000 ticks). These two are the only memory
   types whose codec is built that way (7.1.2).
2. **The copper golem's first transport cooldown is lost on every load.** The
   constructor draws `getRandom().nextInt(60, 100)` into `TRANSPORT_ITEMS_COOLDOWN_TICKS`
   (CopperGolem.txt 112–120), a memory without a codec. `LivingEntity.
   readAdditionalSaveData` remakes the brain from the saved memories (LivingEntity.txt
   11555–11562, n5), so a golem read from disk has no cooldown and starts sorting at
   once; a newly made one waits 60–99 ticks. The remade brain also draws its sensors'
   start offsets again from the entity's random.
3. **Weathering catches up one stage per tick after a golem was frozen.** The next stage
   is `nextWeatheringTick += nextIntBetweenInclusive(504000, 552000)` from the *old*
   deadline, not from the game time (CopperGolem.txt 581–589), and it is checked against
   the absolute game time. A golem that was not ticked for weeks advances one stage per
   tick until its deadline is in the future. The deadline is a derived counter (ADR-0028
   section 3 holds), but the region's notion of game time while the golem's chunk was
   held by nobody decides how far it weathers; that must be the world's game time.
4. **An oxidised golem turns into a statue within seconds, not days.** Once oxidised,
   every tick with air at its feet draws `level.getRandom().nextFloat() <= 0.0058f`
   (CopperGolem.txt 601–618): on average about 172 ticks. A waxed golem never weathers
   and never becomes a statue (`nextWeatheringTick == -2` returns at once). A golem
   standing in water, snow layers, a carpet or grass (any non-air block at its block
   position) never turns and draws nothing.
5. **The copper golem's chest sorting reads up to three chunks beyond its own, and moves
   items between two containers that need not be in its region.** The search goes over
   the 7×7 chunks around it (`floorDiv(32, 16) + 1 = 3`) that are loaded (`getChunkNow`),
   every `ChestBlockEntity` whose position is in the box `blockPosition ± (32, 8, 32)`;
   it picks the nearest by `distToCenterSqr`. The item is taken out of a copper chest
   and later put into a chest or trapped chest, each when the golem is within 0.5 to 1
   block of it, which can be across a line (section 11). Copper chests are the source,
   plain and trapped chests the destination; barrels, shulker boxes and others are never
   used.
6. **A golem puts an item only into a chest that is empty or already holds that item**
   (`ItemStack.isSameItem`, components ignored, TIBC.txt 1206–1243), filling slots in
   order: the first empty slot takes the whole stack, a matching unfilled stack before it
   is topped up first (1318–1388). It takes at most 16 of the first non-empty slot of the
   source (1286–1316), marked as a guaranteed drop. It visits at most 10 destinations
   (then a 140-tick cooldown) and remembers up to 50 unreachable ones, for 6,000 ticks.
7. **A golem counts as an opener of the chest it works at**, through the N6 brief's
   `ContainerOpenersCounter` (3.4): `startOpen` at the first tick of the 60-tick
   interaction, `stopOpen` at the 60th, and `hasContainerOpen` while `openedChestPos` is
   set, with an interaction range of 3.0. A golem pushed away, hurt or leashed mid-way
   clears `openedChestPos` without `stopOpen`; the chest's 5-tick recheck then finds no
   opener and closes the lid. Clustine's openers' count (`containers.rs`) is a number and
   its recheck knows only players: golems must be counted by the recheck too. A player
   with the chest open makes a golem **queue** (stand still within 3 blocks) until the
   chest has no openers (`shouldQueueForTarget`, CopperGolemAi.txt 165–185).
8. **Every brain behaviour's start draws the level's random**; the golem's
   `TransportItemsBetweenContainers` never times out (`timedOut` is false, TIBC.txt
   139–142) but still draws `nextInt(1)` when it starts; the nautilus's `ChargeAttack` is
   a `Behavior` of 60 ticks. The nautilus's and the golem's own draws use the level's
   random for gameplay (attack cooldowns, the choice to attack a pufferfish, weathering,
   the statue) and the entity's random for taming, bubbles and the statue's pose.
9. **The nautilus draws from its own random every tick it is in water, on the server**,
   for bubble particles the server never sends (`spawnBubbles`, AbstractNautilus.txt
   582–680, called from `tick` without a side check): one `nextFloat`, and four more draws
   when it passes. This shifts every later draw of the entity's random.
10. **A nautilus is angry at a UUID**: `ANGRY_AT` holds the attacker's UUID for 400 ticks
    and is resolved with `getLivingEntityFromUUIDMemory`, a world-wide lookup, not a
    nearby search (NautilusAi.txt 187–199). Across a line the attacker may be in another
    region's land (section 11). Only wild adults in water attack, and only targets in
    water; their only natural prey is the pufferfish (`#nautilus_hostiles`).
11. **`ChargeAttack` hits whatever living entity its box meets first, not only its
    target**, through `ATTACK_TARGET_CONDITIONS` (combat targeting, no range, line of
    sight, within the world border, armour stands spared only when `mobGriefing` is off),
    and it calls its own `stop` from inside `tick` (ChargeAttack.txt 182–247), so the
    cooldown of 80 is written twice: at the hit and again by `doStop` the next tick.
12. **The nautilus has no saved inventory.** `getInventoryColumns()` is 0 and
    `AbstractNautilus` writes nothing of its own; the saddle and the body armour are the
    mob's equipment slots (saved by `Mob`/`LivingEntity`). The copper golem's antenna is
    the **saddle slot** (`EQUIPMENT_SLOT_ANTENNA = EquipmentSlot.SADDLE`, CopperGolem.txt
    1100–1101), which holds a poppy an iron golem gave it (`OfferFlowerGoal.stop`,
    OfferFlowerGoal.txt 98–142) and which shears remove.

### 7.1 The brain's machinery

Classes read: `ai.Brain` (1,100 lines) with `$1`, `$Packed`, `$Provider`, `$ActivitySupplier`,
`$Visitor`; `ai.memory.MemorySlot`, `ExpirableValue`, `MemoryMap` and `$Value`,
`$Builder`, `MemoryModuleType` (703), `MemoryStatus`, `WalkTarget`,
`NearestVisibleLivingEntities`; `ai.behavior.Behavior`, `BehaviorControl`, `OneShot`,
`GateBehavior` and its policies, `RunOne`, `TriggerGate`, `ShufflingList` and
`$WeightedEntry`, `DoNothing`, `EntityTracker`, `BlockPosTracker`, `BehaviorUtils`;
`ai.sensing.Sensor`, `SensorType`, `Sensing`; `ai.targeting.TargetingConditions`;
`LivingEntity` (the brain's creation, saving, removal), `Mob.serverAiStep`; from the
second dump `ai.ActivityData`, `schedule.Activity` and the whole `ai.behavior.declarative`
package (`BehaviorBuilder` and its nested classes, `MemoryAccessor`, `MemoryCondition` and
its three records, `Trigger`). Still not dumped: DataFixerUpper's `OptionalBox`, `IdF`,
`Const` (plain wrappers: 12.7.1).

#### 7.1.1 Findings of this subsection

1. **The brain is rebuilt from scratch at every load, and almost all of its state is
   lost then.** `LivingEntity.<init>` makes it with `makeBrain(Brain.Packed.EMPTY)`
   (LivingEntity.txt 347–351), and `readAdditionalSaveData` makes it again from the saved
   `"Brain"` (1791–1797, lambda 11555–11562). What survives is only the memories whose
   type has a codec (7.1.2), with their time to live. Every behaviour's status, end time
   and private fields, every sensor's countdown, every memory without a codec
   (`walk_target`, `look_target`, `attack_target`, `breed_target`, `path`,
   `tempting_player`, the `nearest_*` lists, `hurt_by`, …) are gone. In the game that
   happens only at a chunk's load. In Clustine a crossing, a merge, a split, a lend and a
   restore must not behave like a load (an animal that stops following its player, or
   ends its panic, at a line is a seam a player sees within minutes), so the region's
   entity record has to carry **the whole live brain**: all memories (entity references
   by key), each sensor's countdown, each behaviour's status and fields. ADR-0028's record
   is the game's saved data plus what changes per tick; for a brain the second part is
   far larger than the first.
2. **A brain changes something every tick, even for an animal standing still.** Every
   memory with an expiry counts down by one per brain tick (`MemorySlot.tick`,
   MemorySlot.txt 21–41); every sensor counts down per tick (`Sensor.tick`, Sensor.txt
   50–74); `CountDownCooldownTicks` rewrites its memory every tick (7.3.12). ADR-0028
   section 3 asks that "counters are derived": here that means storing a memory's
   **expiry tick** instead of its time to live, a sensor's **next scan tick** instead of
   its countdown, and a cooldown memory's **end tick**, and rebuilding the game's values
   from them when read (and when saving in the game's form). One catch: these counters
   advance only on ticks where the brain ticks (`customServerAiStep`, which `Mob.serverAiStep`
   calls only while the mob has effective AI; a mob in a frozen chunk does not tick). An
   expiry tick must therefore be shifted forward by the ticks a mob spends not ticking
   (frozen, `NoAI`), or be counted in brain ticks: the plan should choose.
3. **The level's random is drawn by every behaviour's start.** `Behavior.tryStart`
   (Behavior.txt 63–105) draws `level.getRandom().nextInt(maxDuration + 1 - minDuration)`
   whenever its memories and extra conditions hold, **also when min equals max**
   (`nextInt(1)` still consumes a draw); `DoNothing.tryStart` likewise (DoNothing.txt
   37–63). The game's level random is shared by everything in the level; Clustine replaces
   it with streams of place and tick elsewhere (`hoppers.rs:25`, `fluids.rs:63`), and for a
   brain the natural stream is the entity's own (ADR-0028 section 4): every start costs one
   draw, so the draw index of an entity's tick depends on which behaviours started.
4. **Three sources of randomness are not the entity's and not the level's.** Each
   `ShufflingList` (inside every `GateBehavior`, `RunOne` and `TriggerGate`) owns a
   `RandomSource.create()` seeded from the clock (ShufflingList.txt 7–17), one per mob per
   gate; `LongJumpToRandomPos.calculateOptimalJumpVector` calls `Collections.shuffle(list)`
   without a random, which is the JDK's process-wide `java.util.Random`
   (LongJumpToRandomPos.txt 460–503). The owner's parity for draws is the distribution;
   all three are drawn from the entity's stream in a port.
5. **More uses of HotSpot's `Math`.** `ShufflingList$WeightedEntry.setRandom` uses
   `Math.pow(r, 1/weight)` (WeightedEntry.txt 27–40); `LongJumpUtil.calculateJumpVectorForAngle`
   uses `Math.atan2`, `Math.sin`, `Math.cos`, `Math.pow` and `Math.sqrt` (LongJumpUtil.txt
   9–236); `RandomPos.generateRandomDirectionWithinRadians` uses `Math.sin`, `Math.cos`
   and `Math.sqrt` (RandomPos.txt 51–121). `Math.sqrt` is exact and `Math.pow(x, 2.0)` is
   `x*x` in both HotSpot and fdlibm, so the real exceptions are `sin`, `cos`, `atan2` and
   the fractional `pow`: a long jump's arc (after its candidate is drawn), random
   directions for wandering and panic, and the shuffle's weights. ADR-0028 names three
   HotSpot uses; these are more, all after a draw, so their effect is within the
   distributions the owner judges by. Port with `libm` and name them as the TNT's are.
6. **Order within one priority is the `HashMap`'s, and it is fixed.** Behaviours are
   kept in a `TreeMap<Integer, HashMap<Activity, LinkedHashSet<BehaviorControl>>>`
   (Brain.txt 4–64, 759–821). Within a priority, the activities are visited in the
   `HashMap`'s order of `Activity` keys. `Activity` overrides `hashCode` with its name's
   `String.hashCode()`, computed in the constructor, and `equals` by name (Activity.txt
   59–120), so the order is the same on every run and is computable: Java's `HashMap`
   puts a key in bucket `(h ^ (h >>> 16)) & (capacity − 1)` and visits buckets in
   ascending order, keys in one bucket in insertion order (the order the activities were
   added, as `ActivityData` list order). The inner maps are `Maps.newHashMap()` with
   capacity 16 and hold only the activities with behaviours at that priority (never more
   than 12, so never resized). The buckets (capacity 16) of the game's activities:
   `play` 0; `core` 1, `rest` 1; `hide` 2, `admire_item` 2; `dig` 3; `meet` 4; `idle` 5,
   `pre_raid` 5, `celebrate` 5, `tongue` 5; `work` 6, `sniff` 6; `lay_spawn` 8; `emerge`
   10; `avoid` 11, `investigate` 11, `roar` 11; `ride` 13; `fight` 14, `swim` 14; `panic`
   15, `raid` 15, `play_dead` 15, `long_jump` 15, `ram` 15. So at one priority `CORE`'s
   behaviours always try to start before `IDLE`'s, `FIGHT`'s, `PANIC`'s and the rest but
   `PLAY`'s, and `PLAY`'s before `CORE`'s. A port keeps this order (a table of the
   bucket and the insertion order, or the same hash).
7. **A behaviour keeps running after its activity stops.** `tickEachRunningBehavior`
   ticks every `RUNNING` behaviour of every activity, active or not
   (`getRunningBehaviors`, Brain.txt 528–579); only starting is limited to active
   activities (911–975). A switch from `IDLE` to `PANIC` stops nothing by itself: the idle
   behaviours run on until their own `canStillUse` fails or they time out, unless the
   activity's "memories to erase when stopped" pull their conditions away.
8. **A behaviour that starts also ticks in the same tick**, and a `OneShot` or a gate
   whose children all fail stops in the same tick it started (7.1.6). Porters used to
   goal selectors (which start and tick on alternate passes) get this wrong.
9. **Visible means "seen when first asked".** `NearestVisibleLivingEntities` decides
   line of sight lazily, entity by entity, the first time a behaviour asks, and keeps the
   answer for the life of the memory (up to the sensor's 20 ticks; NearestVisibleLivingEntities.txt
   21–43, 183–197). The range it checks is the static `Sensor.TARGET_CONDITIONS`, whose
   range is reset to **the follow range of whichever mob's sensor last scanned, anywhere
   in the server** (`Sensor.updateTargetingConditionRanges`, Sensor.txt 76–106). A mob
   whose follow range differs from the last scanner's tests visibility with the other
   mob's range. The port uses the asking mob's own follow range (all the animals of this
   section use 16 unless 7.4–7.13 say otherwise), a difference to name.
10. **Creative players are never attack targets.** `TargetingConditions.forCombat`
    calls `attacker.canAttack(target)` (TargetingConditions.txt 148–160), which is
    `target.canBeSeenAsEnemy()` (LivingEntity.txt 2162–2176), and a player's is false
    while `abilities.invulnerable` (Player.txt, N5 dump, 1603–1615). Clustine is creative
    only, so every `NEAREST_VISIBLE_ATTACKABLE_PLAYER(S)` memory is empty, and nothing in
    this section rams, attacks or eats a player. Non-combat conditions (looking,
    temptation, following) need only `canBeSeenByAnyone`: alive and not a spectator.
11. **Memories are registered implicitly.** In 26.3 `Brain.provider(sensors, activities)`
    passes an empty memory list (Brain.txt 25–33); the memories a brain has are those its
    sensors `requires()` and its behaviours' entry conditions name (Brain.txt 106–209,
    786–804). A memory not registered cannot be set (silently ignored) or loaded, and a
    `registered()` condition on it fails. A port registers by the same rule, or a
    behaviour's start condition differs.

#### 7.1.2 Memories

A memory is a `MemorySlot<T>` (MemorySlot.txt): a value or null, and a `timeToLive`
(`long`), where `Long.MAX_VALUE` means it never expires.

- `set(value)` sets the value with `MAX_VALUE`; `set(value, ttl)` with `ttl`; `clear()`
  sets null and `MAX_VALUE` (52–78). `hasValue` is value non-null.
- **`tick()`** (21–41): if it has a value and `ttl != MAX_VALUE`: if `ttl <= 0`, clear;
  else `ttl -= 1`. So a memory set with expiry `n` during tick T is present for the
  behaviours of ticks T to T+n (it is counted down to 0 in the forget pass of T+n) and
  cleared in the forget pass of T+n+1. A memory set with expiry 0 lives through the rest
  of its tick and the next whole tick.
- **`Brain.setMemory(type, value)`** (Brain.txt 380–409): if the type is not registered,
  nothing. If the value is a `Collection` and empty, it is treated as null. Null clears;
  otherwise `slot.set(value)` (no expiry, and it **replaces** any expiry the slot had).
  `setMemory(type, Optional)` is `setMemory(type, opt.orElse(null))`.
  **`setMemoryWithExpiry(type, value, ttl)`** (380–406): the same with `slot.set(value,
  ttl)`. `eraseMemory` clears if registered. `getMemory(type)` throws
  `IllegalStateException` if the type is not registered (411–418) and is
  `Optional.ofNullable(value)` otherwise; `getMemoryInternal` returns null for an
  unregistered type. `isMemoryValue(type, v)` is registered and `Objects.equals`.
  `getTimeUntilExpiry` is the slot's ttl.
- **`checkMemory(type, status)`** (478–506): false if not registered; then `REGISTERED`
  is true, `VALUE_PRESENT` is `hasValue`, `VALUE_ABSENT` is `!hasValue`.
  `hasMemoryValue(type)` is `checkMemory(type, VALUE_PRESENT)`.
- **`clearMemories()`** clears every slot (lambda over `memories.values()`);
  `LivingEntity.remove(reason)` calls it after `Entity.remove` (LivingEntity.txt 1479–1488).
- **When memories are cleared** besides expiry: `eraseMemory` by behaviours and sensors;
  an activity's "memories to erase when stopped" (7.1.4); `clearMemories` at removal; a
  collection set empty; and any memory not saved, at every load.

**Saving.** `Brain.pack()` visits every slot (`forEach` over the `HashMap`, Brain.txt
443–458) with `Brain$1` (Brain$1.txt): an empty slot is skipped; a slot whose type
`canSerialize()` (it was registered with a codec) is added to a `MemoryMap` as
`ExpirableValue.of(value)` or `ExpirableValue.of(value, ttl)` when `ttl != MAX_VALUE`.
`LivingEntity.addAdditionalSaveData` stores it as `"Brain"` with `Brain$Packed.CODEC`
(LivingEntity.txt 1599–1605): `{memories: {<memory id>: {value: <codec>, ttl: <long>?}}}`
(`MemoryMap.CODEC` is a `dispatchedMap` keyed by the registry name, validated to types
that can serialise, MemoryMap.txt 131–150; `ExpirableValue.codec` has `value` and a
lenient optional `ttl`, ExpirableValue.txt 58–107). Loading makes a new brain from the
packed map; in the constructor each saved value is set only if its slot is registered
(`setMemoryInternal(MemoryMap$Value)`, Brain.txt 343–378), with its ttl if it has one.

**The memory types with a codec** (MemoryModuleType.txt 172–703, `register(name,
codec)`), so the only memories that survive a save, with their value types: `home`,
`job_site`, `potential_job_site`, `meeting_point` (GlobalPos); `golem_detected_recently`,
`danger_detected_recently`, `has_hunting_cooldown`, `is_panicking`, `universal_anger`,
`admiring_item`, `admiring_disabled`, `hunted_recently` (bool); `last_slept`,
`last_woken`, `last_worked_at_poi` (long); `play_dead_ticks`, `temptation_cooldown_ticks`,
`gaze_cooldown_ticks`, `long_jump_cooling_down` (the `LONG_JUMP_COOLDOWN_TICKS` field),
`ram_cooldown_ticks`, `charge_cooldown_ticks`, `attack_target_cooldown`,
`liked_noteblock_cooldown_ticks`, `item_pickup_cooldown_ticks` (int); `is_in_water`,
`is_pregnant`, `recent_projectile`, `is_sniffing`, `is_emerging`, `roar_sound_delay`,
`dig_cooldown`, `roar_sound_cooldown`, `sniff_cooldown`, `touch_cooldown`,
`vibration_cooldown`, `sonic_boom_cooldown`, `sonic_boom_sound_cooldown`,
`sonic_boom_sound_delay`, the breeze's seven (`Unit`); `angry_at`, `liked_player`
(UUID); `liked_noteblock` (`LIKED_NOTEBLOCK_POSITION`, GlobalPos); `sniffer_explored_positions`
(list of GlobalPos); `visited_block_positions`, `unreachable_transport_block_positions`
(sets of GlobalPos, saved as lists: `GlobalPos.CODEC.listOf().xmap(…)`, 470–483; 7.13);
`breeze_jump_target` (BlockPos). Every other memory (`walk_target`, `look_target`,
`attack_target`, `attack_cooling_down`, `breed_target`, `path`, `mobs`, `visible_mobs`,
`nearest_players`, `nearest_visible_player`, `nearest_visible_adult`, `tempting_player`,
`hurt_by`, `hurt_by_entity`, `cant_reach_walk_target_since`, `ram_target`,
`long_jump_mid_jump`, `nearest_visible_wanted_item`, `dancing`, `sniffer_*` but explored
positions, `transport_items_cooldown_ticks`, …) is lost at a save.

**Values that are entities.** `EntityTracker` (EntityTracker.txt) holds an `Entity`
reference with two flags: `trackEyeHeight` (its `currentPosition` is the entity's
position plus eye height) and `targetEyeHeight` (its `currentBlockPosition` is the block
of the eye position rather than `blockPosition`). `isVisibleBy(mob)`: a non-living entity
is always visible; a living one must be alive and in the mob's
`NEAREST_VISIBLE_LIVING_ENTITIES` (7.1.3). `BlockPosTracker` (BlockPosTracker.txt) holds a
block and its centre, or a `Vec3` as given with its containing block; always visible.
`WalkTarget` (WalkTarget.txt) is a tracker, a `float` speed modifier and an `int`
"close enough" distance; the `Vec3` constructor rounds to `BlockPosTracker(BlockPos
.containing(v))`, so a walk target given as a point walks to that block's centre; the
`Entity` constructor makes `EntityTracker(entity, false)`. In Clustine all of these refer
to entities by key and resolve through the region's table and its copies.

#### 7.1.3 Sensors

`Sensor<E>` (Sensor.txt): a `scanRate` (default 20) and a `long timeToTick`.

- **Creation.** `Brain.<init>` (Brain.txt 46–319) walks the provider's sensor types **in
  their list order**: `SensorType.create()`, then `sensor.randomlyDelayStart(random)`, which
  sets `timeToTick = random.nextInt(scanRate)` (Sensor.txt 39–48), then puts it in a
  `LinkedHashMap` (so sensors tick in list order) and registers its `requires()`
  memories. `random` is `entity.getRandom()` (`Brain$Provider.makeBrain`,
  Brain$Provider.txt 24–43). So every brain's creation (each construction and each load)
  draws one `nextInt(scanRate)` from the entity's own random per sensor, in order.
- **`tick(level, entity)`** (50–74): `timeToTick -= 1`; if it is now `<= 0`:
  `timeToTick = scanRate`, `updateTargetingConditionRanges(entity)`, `doTick(level,
  entity)`. A delay of 0 or 1 scans at the first tick; a delay of k ≥ 1 scans at the k-th;
  then every `scanRate` ticks.
- **`updateTargetingConditionRanges`** (76–106) sets the range of six static
  `TargetingConditions` to the entity's `FOLLOW_RANGE`: `TARGET_CONDITIONS` (non-combat),
  `…_IGNORE_INVISIBILITY_TESTING`, `ATTACK_TARGET_CONDITIONS` (combat), and the combat ones
  ignoring invisibility, line of sight, or both (static initialiser 224–255, all made with
  range 16). Finding 9 says what sharing them means.
- **`isEntityTargetable(level, mob, target)`** (112–131): if `target` is the mob's
  `ATTACK_TARGET`, the non-combat conditions ignoring invisibility, else
  `TARGET_CONDITIONS`. **`isEntityAttackable`** (133–152): the same with the combat ones.
  **`isEntityAttackableIgnoringLineOfSight`** (162–181). **`wasEntityAttackableLastNTicks(e,
  n)`** wraps `isEntityAttackable` in `rememberPositives(n, …)` (183–214): a positive sets
  a counter to n and is true; a negative decrements it and is true while it is still ≥ 0.

**`TargetingConditions.test(level, attacker, target)`** (TargetingConditions.txt
111–217): false if `attacker == target`; false unless `target.canBeSeenByAnyone()` (not a
spectator and alive); false if a selector is set and rejects; if `attacker` is null: for
combat, false if `!target.canBeSeenAsEnemy()` or the difficulty is peaceful; if `attacker`
is not null: for combat, false if `!attacker.canAttack(target)` or
`attacker.isAlliedTo(target)`. Then if `range > 0`: `visibility = testInvisible ?
target.getVisibilityPercent(level, attacker) : 1.0`, `max = Math.max(range × visibility,
2.0)`, false if `attacker.distanceToSqr(target.x, y, z) > max²`. Then if
`checkLineOfSight` and the attacker is a `Mob`: false unless
`mob.getSensing().hasLineOfSight(target)`. `Sensing` (Sensing.txt) caches each answer by
entity id in a `seen` and an `unseen` set, cleared at the start of each
`Mob.serverAiStep` (Mob.txt 1719–1720), so a mob computes `Mob.hasLineOfSight` at most
once per target per tick. The line of sight itself and `getVisibilityPercent` are the
mob section's.

**`NearestVisibleLivingEntities`** (NearestVisibleLivingEntities.txt), the value of
`NEAREST_VISIBLE_LIVING_ENTITIES`: the sensor's sorted list and a predicate that tests
`Sensor.isEntityTargetable(level, mob, e)` lazily and memoises it per entity in an
`Object2BooleanOpenHashMap` (`computeIfAbsent`, 183–197). `findClosest(p)` returns the
first in list order that passes `p` **and** the line-of-sight test (56–83); `findAll`,
`find` filter the same way; `contains(e)` is "in the list and passes the test" (106–121);
`contains(p)` is any that passes both. The empty instance answers false to everything.

Which sensors each animal uses, and the sensors themselves, are in 7.2.

#### 7.1.4 Activities, the provider, and the brain's construction

- **`Brain$Provider`** (Brain$Provider.txt) holds a memory list (empty for every brain
  made by `Brain.provider(sensors[, activities])`, Brain.txt 25–44), the sensor types, and
  a `Brain$ActivitySupplier` whose `createActivities(entity)` returns a `List<ActivityData>`.
  `makeBrain(entity, packed)` calls `createActivities(entity)` **for each brain**, so every
  mob has its own behaviour objects with their own state (the villager's provider is a
  static, but its supplier makes new lists per call: Villager.txt 2216–2311). The
  animals' own `makeBrain` overrides are in 7.4–7.13.
- **`ActivityData`** (ActivityData.txt, a record): `activityType`,
  `behaviorPriorityPairs` (an `ImmutableList<Pair<Integer, BehaviorControl>>`),
  `conditions` (a set of `Pair<MemoryModuleType, MemoryStatus>`) and
  `memoriesToEraseWhenStopped` (a set of memory types). Its `create` overloads:
  - `create(a, start, list)` (29–36): pairs numbered by `createPriorityPairs(start,
    list)` (96–123: `start`, `start + 1`, … in list order), no conditions, nothing to
    erase;
  - `create(a, start, list, memory)` (38–55): numbered pairs, conditions `{(memory,
    VALUE_PRESENT)}`, erase `{memory}` when stopped;
  - `create(a, start, list, conditions)` (66–74): numbered pairs, the given conditions,
    nothing to erase;
  - `create(a, pairs)` (57–64): explicit pairs, no conditions (`ImmutableSet.of()`),
    nothing to erase (an empty `HashSet`);
  - `create(a, pairs, conditions)` (76–83): explicit pairs, the conditions, nothing to
    erase;
  - `create(a, pairs, conditions, toErase)` (85–94): all four given.
- **Construction order** (Brain.txt 46–319): register the provider's memory types; for
  each sensor type in order, create, delay, store, register its memories; for each
  `ActivityData` in list order, `addActivity(type, pairs, conditions, toErase)`; restore
  the packed memories; `setCoreActivities({CORE})`; `useDefaultActivity()`.
- **`addActivity`** (759–821): `activityRequirements[activity] = conditions`; if
  `toErase` is not empty, `activityMemoriesToEraseWhenStopped[activity] = toErase`; for each
  pair in order: register every memory in `behaviour.getRequiredMemories()`, then add the
  behaviour to `availableBehaviorsByPriority[priority][activity]`, a `TreeMap` of
  `HashMap`s of `LinkedHashSet`s (lambdas 1078–1086). A behaviour object added twice to
  one set is kept once.
- **State**: `coreActivities` (a set, `{CORE}` after construction), `activeActivities` (a
  `HashSet`), `defaultActivity` (`IDLE` unless `setDefaultActivity` is called),
  `schedule` (an `EnvironmentAttribute<Activity>`, null unless set), `lastScheduleUpdate`
  (−9999).
- **`setActiveActivity(a)`** (628–652): if `a` is already active, nothing. Otherwise
  `eraseMemoriesForOtherActivitesThan(a)` (654–693: for each currently active activity
  other than `a`, erase each memory in its "to erase when stopped" set), then `active =
  coreActivities ∪ {a}`. Note that the erase covers the core activities too, if they had
  such a set, and that it happens only when the non-core activity actually changes.
- **`useDefaultActivity()`**: `setActiveActivity(defaultActivity)`.
  **`setActiveActivityIfPossible(a)`** (614–626): if `a`'s requirements are met, set it,
  else use the default. **`setActiveActivityToFirstValid(list)`** (729–750): the first in
  list order whose requirements are met is set; if none, **nothing changes** (no default).
  **`activityRequirementsAreMet(a)`** (1001–1041): false if `a` was never added; else every
  `(memory, status)` pair passes `checkMemory`.
- **`getActiveNonCoreActivity()`** (589–612): the first active activity not in the core
  set, in `HashSet` order (only one exists at a time unless the core set has several).
- **`updateActivityFromSchedule(attributes, gameTime, pos)`** (695–727): only if `gameTime
  − lastScheduleUpdate > 20`: `lastScheduleUpdate = gameTime`; `a = schedule != null ?
  attributes.getValue(schedule, pos) : IDLE`; if `a` is not active,
  `setActiveActivityIfPossible(a)`. The villager's (7.14).
- **`stopAll(level, entity)`** (886–909): `doStop` on every running behaviour, in
  `getRunningBehaviors` order, with the level's game time.
- **`removeAllBehaviors()`** clears the priority map. **`isBrainDead()`**: no memories, no
  sensors, no behaviours (the base brain `LivingEntity.makeBrain` makes, LivingEntity.txt
  372–377, for every living entity without one of its own).

Each animal calls its own activity update (`XAi.updateActivity`) from its AI step; they
are in 7.4–7.13.

#### 7.1.5 `Brain.tick(level, entity)`, in order (Brain.txt 838–999)

```
tick(level, e):
    forgetOutdatedMemories()          # every slot's tick(); the HashMap's order is immaterial
    for sensor in sensors (list order): sensor.tick(level, e)
    startEachNonRunningBehavior(level, e)
    tickEachRunningBehavior(level, e)

startEachNonRunningBehavior:
    t = level.getGameTime()
    for priority in ascending order:
        for (activity, set) in availableBehaviorsByPriority[priority]   # bucket order: finding 6
            if activity in activeActivities:
                for b in set (insertion order):
                    if b.getStatus() == STOPPED: b.tryStart(level, e, t)

tickEachRunningBehavior:
    t = level.getGameTime()
    for b in getRunningBehaviors():     # a list made now: every RUNNING behaviour of every
        b.tickOrStop(level, e, t)       # activity, active or not, in the same order as above
```

The list of running behaviours is taken once, before any of them ticks: a behaviour
stopped by an earlier one's `doStop` (they share no objects, but a gate's children are not
in the list: only the gate is) is still asked `tickOrStop`, which then checks its own
conditions. Memories changed by sensors in this tick are seen by every start and tick of
the same tick; memories changed by one behaviour's start are seen by the starts after it.

**Where the brain ticks.** `Mob.serverAiStep` (Mob.txt 1705–1815), in order:
`noActionTime += 1`… `sensing.tick()` (the line-of-sight cache cleared), the target and
goal selectors (every tick when `(tickCount + getId()) % 2 == 0` or `tickCount <= 1`,
else only their running goals), `navigation.tick()`, **`customServerAiStep(level)`**
(where each animal of this section calls `brain.tick`, then its activity update and
other work), then `moveControl.tick()`, `lookControl.tick()`, `jumpControl.tick()`. So a
path a behaviour sets in the brain is first followed by the next tick's
`navigation.tick()`, while a look target a behaviour sets is acted on by the look control
in the same tick. Whether `serverAiStep` runs at all (effective AI, `NoAI`, being dead) is
`LivingEntity.aiStep`'s, the mob section's.

#### 7.1.6 Behaviours

`BehaviorControl<E>` (BehaviorControl.txt): `getStatus()`, `getRequiredMemories()`,
`tryStart(level, e, time)`, `tickOrStop(level, e, time)`, `doStop(level, e, time)`.
`Behavior$Status` is `STOPPED` or `RUNNING`. Three kinds implement it.

**`Behavior<E>`** (Behavior.txt): `entryCondition` (a map of memory to `MemoryStatus`),
`status` (starts `STOPPED`), `long endTimestamp`, `minDuration`, `maxDuration`
(constructors: `(map)` is 60/60, `(map, d)` is d/d, `(map, min, max)`).

```
tryStart(level, e, t):                                   # final, 63–105
    if hasRequiredMemories(e) and checkExtraStartConditions(level, e):
        status = RUNNING
        d = min + level.getRandom().nextInt(max + 1 - min)  # always one draw
        endTimestamp = t + d
        start(level, e, t)
        return true
    return false

tickOrStop(level, e, t):                                 # final, 111–134
    if not timedOut(t) and canStillUse(level, e, t): tick(level, e, t)
    else: doStop(level, e, t)

doStop(level, e, t): status = STOPPED; stop(level, e, t) # final, 140–150
timedOut(t) = t > endTimestamp                           # overridable, 161–171
canStillUse = false; checkExtraStartConditions = true; start, tick, stop do nothing
hasRequiredMemories: every entry passes brain.checkMemory  # 185–217
```

Consequences: a behaviour that keeps the default `canStillUse` runs `start` then `stop`
in the same brain tick (its duration and its draw are spent for nothing but the order of
draws). One that can still be used runs `start` and then `tick` in its first tick, and
runs to `t = start + d` inclusive (d + 1 calls of `tick`), stopping in the tick after.
Since `startEachNonRunningBehavior` runs before `tickEachRunningBehavior`, a behaviour that
stops in tick T can start again only in tick T+1. `getRequiredMemories` is the entry
condition's keys.

**`OneShot<E>`** (OneShot.txt), also a `Trigger`: `tryStart` calls `trigger(level, e, t)`;
if true, `status = RUNNING` and true. `tickOrStop` is `doStop` (status `STOPPED`). So a
one-shot that fires is `RUNNING` for the rest of the brain tick and is stopped by
`tickEachRunningBehavior` in the same tick; it can fire again the next tick. It draws
nothing itself.

**`BehaviorBuilder` behaviours** (the `declarative` package). Most shared behaviours are
`BehaviorBuilder.create(instance -> instance.group(instance.present(M1),
instance.absent(M2), instance.registered(M3), …).apply(instance, (a1, a2, …) ->
(level, e, t) -> { … }))`; the body is in the class's `lambda$create$N` methods.

- `BehaviorBuilder.create(f)` (BehaviorBuilder.txt 18–30) applies `f` to a new
  `Instance`, takes the resulting `TriggerWithResult` and wraps it in `BehaviorBuilder$1`,
  a `OneShot` (BehaviorBuilder$1.txt): `trigger(level, e, t)` calls
  `tryTrigger(level, e, t)`; if that returns null, false; else it is a `Trigger`, and its
  `trigger(level, e, t)` is the result (14–33). `getRequiredMemories` is the
  builder's `memories()` (35–40).
- **The memory conditions** (`Instance.registered`, `present`, `absent`,
  BehaviorBuilder$Instance.txt 23–54) each make a `PureMemory` whose `tryTrigger`
  (BehaviorBuilder$PureMemory$1.txt 14–34) reads `brain.getMemoryInternal(type)`: **null
  (the condition fails) if the memory is not registered**, whatever the kind; else
  `condition.createAccessor(brain, optional)`: `Present` gives null if the memory is empty,
  else an accessor holding the value (MemoryCondition$Present.txt 19–35); `Absent` null
  if it has a value (MemoryCondition$Absent.txt 19–34); `Registered` always an accessor
  holding the `Optional` (MemoryCondition$Registered.txt 19–29). `memories()` is the one
  type.
- **`group(…).apply(instance, fn)`** is `ap2`, `ap3`, `ap4` (Instance.txt 102–175; the
  `$3`, `$4`, `$5` classes) or `map` for one (`$2`): `tryTrigger` evaluates the
  conditions **left to right, stopping at the first that fails** (null), then the
  function and applies it to the accessors (BehaviorBuilder$Instance$3.txt 29–69). So the
  values a body reads are those of the moment the conditions were checked; the body's
  closure (the `Trigger`) is made anew each time.
- **`MemoryAccessor`** (MemoryAccessor.txt): `set(v)` is `brain.setMemory(type,
  Optional.of(v))`; `setOrErase(opt)` is `brain.setMemory(type, opt)`; `setWithExpiry(v,
  n)` is `brain.setMemoryWithExpiry`; `erase()` is `brain.eraseMemory`.
  `Instance.get(accessor)` returns the value it holds and `tryGet` the `Optional`
  (Instance.txt 9–21).
- **`Instance.point(a)`** (64–79) is a `Constant`: its `tryTrigger` returns `a` and its
  memories are none (BehaviorBuilder$Constant$1.txt). `create(instance ->
  instance.point(trigger))` (used by `TriggerGate`, `UpdateActivityFromSchedule`,
  `triggerIf`) is a one-shot that just runs the trigger.
- **`Instance.ifTriggered(trigger)`** (56–62) is a `TriggerWrapper`: `tryTrigger` runs the
  trigger and gives `Unit` if true, null if false (BehaviorBuilder$TriggerWrapper$1.txt
  14–26).
- **`triggerIf(predicate)`** (BehaviorBuilder.txt 54–59, lambdas 108–121) is a one-shot
  whose result is `predicate(e)`; `triggerIf(biPredicate)` (61–66, 92–106) with
  `(level, e)`. **`sequence(first, second)`** (32–44, 123–143) is a `BehaviorBuilder$2`
  (BehaviorBuilder$2.txt) whose `trigger` runs `first`; only if it is true, `second`'s
  `trigger`, whose result is the sequence's; its memories are both's.
  **`triggerIf(predicate, oneShot)`** (46–52) is `sequence(triggerIf(predicate),
  oneShot)`: the one-shot runs only while the predicate holds. As a gate's child,
  `triggerIf(p)` alone is a child that "starts" (and does nothing) whenever `p` holds.

**`GateBehavior<E>`** (GateBehavior.txt): an entry condition, a set of memories to erase
on exit, an `OrderPolicy` (`ORDERED`, `SHUFFLED`), a `RunningPolicy` (`RUN_ONE`,
`TRY_ALL`), and a `ShufflingList` of children with weights, in constructor order.

```
tryStart(level, e, t):                                   # 114–140
    if every entry memory condition holds:
        status = RUNNING
        orderPolicy.apply(children)      # SHUFFLED: children.shuffle(); ORDERED: nothing
        runningPolicy.apply(children.stream(), level, e, t)
        return true                      # true even if no child started
    return false

RUN_ONE ($RunningPolicy$1, 11–44):  the first child in list order whose status is STOPPED
                                    and whose tryStart returns true; the children after it
                                    are not tried (a lazy stream with findFirst)
TRY_ALL ($RunningPolicy$2, 11–43):  tryStart on every STOPPED child in order

tickOrStop(level, e, t):                                 # 142–165
    for child in children (list order) if RUNNING: child.tickOrStop(level, e, t)
    if no child is RUNNING: doStop(level, e, t)

doStop(level, e, t):                                     # 167–191
    status = STOPPED
    for child in children if RUNNING: child.doStop(level, e, t)
    for m in exitErasedMemories: brain.eraseMemory(m)
```

`getRequiredMemories` is the gate's entry keys and all children's (a `HashSet`). A gate
whose children all fail to start is `RUNNING` and then stopped in the same tick (erasing
its exit memories). While any child runs, the gate is `RUNNING` and so is not tried again:
no other child of a `RUN_ONE` gate can start until that child stops.

**`RunOne<E>`** (RunOne.txt) is `GateBehavior(entry, {}, SHUFFLED, RUN_ONE, children)`; its
one-argument constructor has no entry condition.

**`ShufflingList<U>`** (ShufflingList.txt): entries `(data, weight)` and its own
`RandomSource.create()`. `shuffle()` (56–69): for each entry in list order,
`randWeight = -Math.pow(random.nextFloat(), 1.0 / weight)` (the exponent is `1.0f /
(float) weight` widened: `(double)(1.0f / (float) w)`, WeightedEntry.txt 27–40); then
the list is sorted by `randWeight` ascending (a stable sort). The effect is a weighted
random order: an entry of weight w comes first with probability proportional to w. The
order persists until the next shuffle (`stream()` and `iterator()` walk it in its current
order).

**`TriggerGate.triggerGate(triggers, order, running)`** (TriggerGate.txt): a one-shot made
with `instance.point`, around its own `ShufflingList` of `Trigger`s: if `SHUFFLED`,
shuffle; then for each trigger in order: if `trigger(level, e, t)` is true and the policy
is `RUN_ONE`, stop looking; always returns true. `triggerOneShuffled` is `SHUFFLED,
RUN_ONE`.

**`DoNothing(min, max)`** (DoNothing.txt): `tryStart` always succeeds, sets `RUNNING`, draws
`level.getRandom().nextInt(max + 1 - min)` for `endTimestamp = t + min + draw`;
`tickOrStop` stops once `t > endTimestamp`. No memories.

#### 7.1.7 Determinism and draws, summed up

Deterministic given the state: the forget pass, the sensors' countdowns, the order of
sensors, of priorities, of the activities at one priority (by their names' hashes,
finding 6) and of behaviours within an activity's set, every entry condition, the gates'
`ORDERED` policy. Not settled: the iteration order of the `HashSet` of `GlobalPos` that
`InteractWithDoor` keeps (`DOORS_TO_CLOSE`, 7.3.21), which depends on `ResourceKey`'s
hash (not dumped, 12.7.1).

Draws, by source:

| Source | Where |
|---|---|
| entity's `getRandom()` | each sensor's start delay at every brain creation (7.1.3); behaviours' own draws (`AnimalMakeLove`'s child time, `Swim`, `RandomLookAround`, every `RandomPos` helper, `getVoicePitch`), listed in 7.3 |
| level's `getRandom()` | every `Behavior` and `DoNothing` start (one `nextInt`), `SetEntityLookTargetSometimes`'s ticker, `MoveToTargetSink`'s retry cooldown, the long jump's and the ram's cooldowns and candidates (7.3) |
| a `ShufflingList`'s own clock-seeded random | each `SHUFFLED` gate's start and each `TriggerGate` trigger: one `nextFloat` per child |
| the JDK's global `java.util.Random` | `Collections.shuffle` of the four jump angles (7.3.16) |

For Clustine, every one of these comes from the entity's stateless stream (world seed,
key, tick, draw index), in the order the game draws them; the draws that the game takes
from the level's random are then ordered by the entity's own tick rather than
interleaved with other entities', which the owner's parity (distributions) allows.

### 7.2 The sensors these animals use

Each sensor's `requires()` is what it registers; each runs every `scanRate` ticks (20
unless said) after its random start delay, in the order of the animal's sensor list. The
sensors only one animal uses (`AXOLOTL_ATTACKABLES`, `FROG_ATTACKABLES`,
`FROG_TEMPTATIONS`, `NAUTILUS_TEMPTATIONS`, `ARMADILLO_SCARE_DETECTED`) are given with
their animal in 7.4–7.13. `SensorType`'s registrations (SensorType.txt 111–208) name the
factories by method reference, which `javap -c` does not show (the bootstrap arguments
are not printed): each is **Inferred** to be the class's constructor (`NearestLivingEntitySensor::new`, …), except
`FOOD_TEMPTATIONS`, **Inferred** to be `TemptingSensor::forAnimal` (the only static
factory, and no lambda in `SensorType` makes it), and the three lambdas read here:
`FROG_TEMPTATIONS` is `new TemptingSensor(FrogAi.getTemptations())` (91–97),
`NAUTILUS_TEMPTATIONS` `new TemptingSensor(NautilusAi.getTemptations())` (83–89),
`ARMADILLO_SCARE_DETECTED` `new MobSensor(5, <BiPredicate>, <Predicate>,
DANGER_DETECTED_RECENTLY, 80)` (99–109, its two method references in 7.8).

#### 7.2.1 `NEAREST_LIVING_ENTITIES`: `NearestLivingEntitySensor` (74 lines)

Requires `NEAREST_LIVING_ENTITIES` (`mobs`) and `NEAREST_VISIBLE_LIVING_ENTITIES`
(`visible_mobs`). `doTick` (9–53): `r = FOLLOW_RANGE`; `box = boundingBox.inflate(r, r,
r)` (all three axes, so a mob sees 16 blocks up and down too);
`level.getEntitiesOfClass(LivingEntity, box, e -> e != mob && e.isAlive())`, sorted by
`mob.distanceToSqr(e)` (a stable sort, so ties keep the lookup's order: by section and
then, in Clustine, by key); set `mobs` to that list (empty means erased) and
`visible_mobs` to `new NearestVisibleLivingEntities(level, mob, list)` (never empty as an
object, even for an empty list). Players are living entities and are in the list.

#### 7.2.2 `NEAREST_PLAYERS`: `PlayerSensor` (127 lines)

Requires `nearest_players`, `nearest_visible_player`, `nearest_visible_targetable_player`
(`NEAREST_VISIBLE_ATTACKABLE_PLAYER`) and `nearest_visible_targetable_players`. `doTick`
(18–93): `level.players()` (every player in the dimension) that are not spectators and
`mob.closerThan(p, FOLLOW_RANGE)` (a sphere), sorted by distance; `nearest_players` =
that list; `visible` = those for which `Sensor.isEntityTargetable(level, mob, p)`;
`nearest_visible_player` = the first or null; `attackable` = the visible ones for which
`Sensor.isEntityAttackable`; `nearest_visible_targetable_players` = that list,
`nearest_visible_targetable_player` = its first or null. In creative, the last two are
always empty (finding 10).

#### 7.2.3 `HURT_BY`: `HurtBySensor` (70 lines)

Requires `hurt_by`, `hurt_by_entity`. `doTick` (16–55): `src = getLastDamageSource()`; if
non-null: `hurt_by = src`, and if `src.getEntity()` is a living entity, `hurt_by_entity =
it`; else erase `hurt_by` (but **not** `hurt_by_entity`). Then if `hurt_by_entity` is
present and that entity is dead or in another level, erase it (lambda 57–69). How long
`getLastDamageSource` stays non-null after a hurt is `LivingEntity`'s (the mob section's).

#### 7.2.4 `NEAREST_ADULT` and `NEAREST_ADULT_ANY_TYPE`: `AdultSensor`, `AdultSensorAnyType`

Require `nearest_visible_adult` and `visible_mobs`. `AdultSensor.doTick` (16–26): from the
current `visible_mobs` (as the earlier sensor left it; if absent, nothing), `findClosest(e
-> e.getType() == mob.getType() && !e.isBaby())`, set as an `Optional` (absent erases).
`AdultSensorAnyType` (9–34): `findClosest(e -> e.is(FOLLOWABLE_FRIENDLY_MOBS) &&
!e.isBaby())`. The tag (`tags/entity_type/followable_friendly_mobs.json`): armadillo, bee,
camel, cat, chicken, cow, donkey, fox, goat, happy_ghast, horse, skeleton_horse, llama,
mule, ocelot, panda, parrot, pig, polar_bear, rabbit, sheep, sniffer, strider, villager,
wolf. Both read `visible_mobs`, so they must come after `NEAREST_LIVING_ENTITIES` in the
list to see this scan's (each animal's list says).

#### 7.2.5 `FOOD_TEMPTATIONS` (and the frog's and nautilus's): `TemptingSensor` (191 lines)

Requires `tempting_player`. A `BiPredicate<PathfinderMob, ItemStack>`: `forAnimal()` is
`mob instanceof Animal a && a.isFood(stack)` (163–176); the `Predicate` constructor ignores
the mob (178–183). `doTick` (32–90): `conditions = TEMPT_TARGETING.copy().range((double)
(float) TEMPT_RANGE)` where `TEMPT_TARGETING` is non-combat **ignoring line of sight**
(185–190), so the range is the `tempt_range` attribute rounded to a float; players of the
level, not spectators, passing `conditions.test(level, mob, p)` (range and not a spectator,
alive; visibility percent applies since invisibility is tested), holding a temptation in
the main hand or the off hand (main first, 92–109), and **not riding the mob**
(`!mob.hasPassenger(p)`, 135–144); sorted by `mob.distanceToSqr`; the first is
`tempting_player`, or it is erased.

#### 7.2.6 `IS_IN_WATER`: `IsInWaterSensor` (31 lines)

Requires `is_in_water` (a `Unit`). `doTick`: set it if `mob.isInWater()`, else erase.

#### 7.2.7 `NEAREST_ITEMS`: `NearestItemSensor` (98 lines; the allay's and the villager's)

Requires `nearest_visible_wanted_item`. `doTick` (21–66): item entities in
`boundingBox.inflate(32, 16, 32)`, sorted by distance; the first that the mob
`wantsToPickUp(level, stack)`, that is `closerThan(mob, 32)`, and (**Inferred**, a method
reference on the mob, 56–59) that the mob `hasLineOfSight` of; set or erased.

#### 7.2.8 `DUMMY`

`DummySensor` (17 lines) requires nothing and does nothing; it still draws its start delay.

### 7.3 The shared behaviours

Each is given as: its kind (`Behavior` with durations, or a `BehaviorBuilder` one-shot),
its memories (P present, A absent, R registered), what it does at start, tick and stop,
and its draws. "Level draw" is `level.getRandom()`, "own draw" the entity's
`getRandom()`. Every `Behavior` start costs the level draw of 7.1.6 before `start`; it is
not repeated below. The animal sections give the arguments each animal passes.

#### 7.3.1 Findings of this subsection

1. **Most wandering is two one-shots and a sink.** `RandomStroll` sets a walk target
   when there is none; `SetWalkTargetFromLookTarget` turns a look target into a walk
   target; `MoveToTargetSink` is the only behaviour that makes paths, and
   `LookAtTargetSink` the only one that turns the head. Everything else just writes
   `walk_target` and `look_target`. A port can share one sink and one looker for every
   brain.
2. **`MoveToTargetSink` erases the walk target when it reaches it or cannot path**, and
   then waits a random 0 to 39 ticks (a level draw) before trying again only when the
   navigation got stuck; a mob whose target is unreachable keeps
   `cant_reach_walk_target_since` from the first failure, which is what
   `StopAttackingIfTargetInvalid` reads to give up after 200 ticks.
3. **Breeding writes the partner's memories.** `AnimalMakeLove` sets the partner's
   `breed_target`, `look_target` and `walk_target` every tick it runs, and calls
   `spawnChildFromBreeding` on itself with the partner. Across a line that is a write
   into another region's entity, which ADR-0028 section 7's list of entity effects (a hit,
   a push, an explosion) does not have (11.7).
4. **Panic re-arms itself.** `AnimalPanic` starts while `hurt_by` holds a panic-causing
   damage or `is_panicking` is set, runs 100 to 120 ticks, and erases `is_panicking` when
   it stops, but not `hurt_by`, so it starts again at once while the hurt is still
   remembered. `is_panicking` is saved; a panic survives a reload as a fresh panic.
5. **The long jump keeps state for up to 200 ticks** (candidates, tries, the chosen
   vector, the start position and time), all lost in the game at a load and all needed in
   a Clustine record. It draws the level's random once per candidate examined, its four
   angles are shuffled by the JDK's global random, and its arc uses HotSpot's `Math`.
6. **The ram writes nothing into its target but a hit and a knockback**, which are the
   entity effects ADR-0028 section 7 already has.

#### 7.3.2 `RandomStroll` (RandomStroll.txt, 361 lines): one-shots

Factories, all `BehaviorBuilder` one-shots made by `strollFlyOrSwim(speed, posFn,
predicate)` (60–67, body `lambda$strollFlyOrSwim$0`–`$3`, 171–226):

- `stroll(speed)` = `stroll(speed, true)`.
- `stroll(speed, mayStrollInWater)`: position `LandRandomPos.getPos(mob, 10, 7)`
  (`lambda$stroll$0`, 269–275); predicate always true if `mayStrollInWater`
  (`lambda$stroll$1`), else `!mob.isInWater()` (`lambda$stroll$2`, 254–262).
- `stroll(speed, h, v)`: `LandRandomPos.getPos(mob, h, v)`, always (`lambda$stroll$3`,
  `$4`).
- `fly(speed)`: `getTargetFlyPos(mob, 10, 7)` = `AirAndWaterRandomPos.getPos(mob, 10, 7,
  -2, view.x, view.z, 1.5707963705062866)` with `view = mob.getViewVector(0f)` (153–169);
  always.
- `swim(speed)`: position `getTargetSwimPos` and a predicate, both method references
  (**Inferred**: `RandomStroll::getTargetSwimPos` and `Entity::isInWater`-like; no lambda
  of `swim` exists, 52–58).

Memories: A `walk_target`. Trigger: if `!predicate(mob)`, false; else `p = posFn(mob)`;
`walk_target` set to `WalkTarget(p, speed, 0)` if `p` is non-null (erased otherwise,
which changes nothing as it was absent); **true either way**.

**`getTargetSwimPos(mob)`** (69–151), with `SWIM_XY_DISTANCE_TIERS = {{1,1}, {3,3}, {5,5},
{6,5}, {7,7}, {10,7}}` (277–360):

```
best = null; cand = null
for (xz, y) in tiers:
    if best == null: cand = BehaviorUtils.getRandomSwimmablePos(mob, xz, y)
    else: cand = mob.position() + mob.position().vectorTo(best).normalize() * (xz, y, xz)
    restricted = GoalUtils.mobRestricted(mob, xz)
    if cand == null or level.getFluidState(BlockPos.containing(cand)).isEmpty()
       or GoalUtils.isRestricted(restricted, mob, cand):
        return best
    best = cand
return cand
```

The first tier draws a random position; the later ones push it out along the same
direction, as far as water lasts. `getRandomSwimmablePos(mob, h, v)` (BehaviorUtils.txt
381–411): `p = DefaultRandomPos.getPos(mob, h, v)`; up to 10 more times, while `p` is
non-null and the block at `p` is not pathfindable for `WATER`, draw again.

#### 7.3.3 The random-position helpers (`ai.util`), as these behaviours use them

They draw from the **entity's** random. `getWalkTargetValue` and the path types are the
mob and path-finder sections'.

- `RandomPos.generateRandomDirection(r, h, v)` (RandomPos.txt 11–49): `(r.nextInt(2h+1) −
  h, r.nextInt(2v+1) − v, r.nextInt(2h+1) − h)`, x then y then z: three draws.
- `RandomPos.generateRandomDirectionWithinRadians(r, minH, maxH, v, yOff, x, z, range)`
  (51–121): `a = Mth.atan2(z, x) − 1.5707963705062866 + (double)(2f × r.nextFloat() − 1f) ×
  range`; `d = Mth.lerp(Math.sqrt(r.nextDouble()), minH, maxH) × (double) Mth.SQRT_OF_TWO`;
  `px = −d × Math.sin(a)`, `pz = d × Math.cos(a)` (HotSpot's `Math`); if `|px| > maxH` or
  `|pz| > maxH`, null (two draws spent); else `py = r.nextInt(2v+1) − v + yOff` and
  `BlockPos.containing(px, py, pz)`: three draws.
- `RandomPos.generateRandomPosTowardDirection(mob, h, r, dir)` (268–355): `x = dir.x, z =
  dir.z`; if `mob.hasHome()` and `h > 1`: `x −= r.nextDouble() × h / 2` if `mob.getX() >
  home.x` else `x += …`; then the same for z (two draws); `BlockPos.containing(x +
  mob.getX(), dir.y + mob.getY(), z + mob.getZ())`.
- `RandomPos.generateRandomPos(supplier, score)` (228–266): ten calls of the supplier;
  keep the non-null result with the strictly greatest score (starting from −∞); return
  `Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(best)` or null. `generateRandomPos(mob, supplier)` scores with
  `mob.getWalkTargetValue` (**Inferred**, a method reference, 217–226).
- `RandomPos.moveUpOutOfSolid(pos, maxY, solid)` (123–151): if `solid(pos)`, step up
  while `y <= maxY` and still solid.
- `LandRandomPos.getPos(mob, h, v)` (LandRandomPos.txt 9–36): `restricted =
  GoalUtils.mobRestricted(mob, h)`; `generateRandomPos(supplier, mob.getWalkTargetValue)`
  where each try is (220–243): `dir = generateRandomDirection(r, h, v)`; `p =
  generateRandomPosTowardDirection(mob, h, r, dir)`, null if outside the build height,
  `isRestricted(restricted, mob, p)` or `isNotStable(navigation, p)` (151–177); then
  `movePosUpOutOfSolid`: up out of solid blocks to `level.getMaxY()`, null if the result
  is water or has a path malus (128–149).
- `LandRandomPos.getPosTowards`, `getPosAway` (38–113): the same through
  `generateRandomDirectionWithinRadians(r, 0 or minH, h, v, 0, dir.x, dir.z, π/2)`;
  `getPosAway` with a zero vector replaces it by `(r.nextDouble() − 0.5, 0, r.nextDouble()
  − 0.5)` first.
- `DefaultRandomPos.getPos(mob, h, v)` (DefaultRandomPos.txt 9–23, 161–174): as
  `LandRandomPos` but each try is `generateRandomPosTowardDirection` checked by outside
  limits, restricted, not stable and `hasMalus` (74–105), with no moving up.
  `getPosTowards(mob, h, v, target, range)` and `getPosAway` (25–72, 107–159) go through
  `generateRandomDirectionWithinRadians(r, 0, h, v, 0, dir.x, dir.z, range or π/2)`.
- `AirAndWaterRandomPos.getPos(mob, h, v, yOff, x, z, range)` (AirAndWaterRandomPos.txt
  9–100): each try is `withinRadians(r, 0, h, v, yOff, x, z, range)`, then
  `generateRandomPosTowardDirection`, null if outside limits or restricted, then up out of
  solid, null if it has a malus.
- `GoalUtils` (GoalUtils.txt): `mobRestricted(mob, d)` = `mob.hasHome() &&
  home.closerToCenterThan(mob.position(), homeRadius + d + 1)`; `isRestricted(flag, mob,
  p)` = `flag && !mob.isWithinHome(p)`; `isOutsideLimits` = outside the build height;
  `isNotStable` = `!navigation.isStableDestination(p)`; `isWater` = water fluid;
  `hasMalus` = `mob.getPathfindingMalus(WalkNodeEvaluator.getPathTypeStatic(mob, p)) !=
  0`; `isSolid` = `state.isSolid()`.

#### 7.3.4 `SetWalkTargetFromLookTarget` (93 lines): one-shot

`create(speed, dist)`: predicate always true, speed constant. `create(predicate,
speedFn, dist)`: A `walk_target`, P `look_target`. Trigger (`lambda$create$4`, 57–81): if
`!predicate(e)`, false; else `walk_target = WalkTarget(<the look target's tracker itself>,
speedFn(e), dist)`; true. No draws. The walk goes to the tracker's
`currentBlockPosition`, re-read by `MoveToTargetSink` as the tracked entity moves.

#### 7.3.5 `MoveToTargetSink` (434 lines): `Behavior`, 150–250 ticks by default

State: `remainingCooldown` (int), `path`, `lastTargetPos`, `speedModifier`. Memories: R
`cant_reach_walk_target_since`, A `path`, P `walk_target` (13–34; `(min, max)`
constructor).

```
checkExtraStartConditions(level, mob):                    # 36–88
    if remainingCooldown > 0: remainingCooldown -= 1; return false
    wt = walk_target
    reached = reachedTarget(mob, wt)
    if not reached and tryComputePath(mob, wt, gameTime):
        lastTargetPos = wt.target.currentBlockPosition(); return true
    erase walk_target
    if reached: erase cant_reach_walk_target_since
    return false

start: path memory = path; navigation.moveTo(path, (double) speedModifier)    # 180–197

canStillUse(level, mob, t):                               # 90–135
    if path == null or lastTargetPos == null: false
    wt = walk_target (optional)
    spectator = wt is present and its tracker is an EntityTracker of a spectator
    return not navigation.isDone() and wt present and not reachedTarget(mob, wt)
           and not spectator

tick(level, mob, t):                                      # 199–257
    np = navigation.getPath()
    if path != np: path = np; path memory = np
    if np == null or lastTargetPos == null: return
    wt = walk_target.get()
    if wt.target.currentBlockPosition().distSqr(lastTargetPos) > 4.0
       and tryComputePath(mob, wt, gameTime):
        lastTargetPos = wt.target.currentBlockPosition(); start(level, mob, t)

stop(level, mob, t):                                      # 137–178
    if walk_target present and not reached and navigation.isStuck():
        remainingCooldown = level.getRandom().nextInt(40)            # level draw
    navigation.stop(); erase walk_target; erase path; path = null

tryComputePath(mob, wt, t):                               # 259–350
    pos = wt.target.currentBlockPosition()
    path = navigation.createPath(pos, 0); speedModifier = wt.speedModifier
    if reachedTarget(mob, wt): erase cant_reach_walk_target_since
    else:
        if path != null and path.canReach(): erase cant_reach_walk_target_since
        elif cant_reach_walk_target_since absent: set it to t
    if path != null: return true
    v = DefaultRandomPos.getPosTowards((PathfinderMob) mob, 10, 7,
                                       Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(pos), 1.5707963705062866)
    if v != null: path = navigation.createPath(v.x, v.y, v.z, 0); return path != null
    return false

reachedTarget(mob, wt) = wt.target.currentBlockPosition().distManhattan(mob.blockPosition())
                         <= wt.closeEnoughDist                            # 352–366
```

The cooldown is counted down only by start attempts (one per brain tick while a walk
target is present). A path that is null makes it try a random position towards the
target (own draws, 7.3.3). The "spectator" check is a method reference to
`isWalkTargetSpectator` (**Inferred**, 106).

#### 7.3.6 `LookAtTargetSink(min, max)` (90 lines): `Behavior`

P `look_target`. `canStillUse`: the look target is present and `tracker.isVisibleBy(mob)`
(lambda 84–89). `tick`: `mob.getLookControl().setLookAt(tracker.currentPosition())`
(lambda 75–83; the look control's default speeds, the controls' section). `stop`: erase
`look_target`. So a mob looks for its duration (each animal's min and max) or until the
target is out of sight, then forgets it; a `BlockPosTracker` is always visible, so a
looked-at block holds for the full duration.

#### 7.3.7 `SetEntityLookTargetSometimes` (136 lines) with `$Ticker` (51): one-shot

`create(maxDist, interval)` (any entity) or `create(type, maxDist, interval)` (that type
only); `maxDistSqr = maxDist × maxDist` in `float` (26–42). The `Ticker` (one per
behaviour object, so per mob) holds `UniformInt interval` (its minimum must be ≥ 1, else
`IllegalArgumentException`) and `ticksUntilNextStart` (0).

A `look_target`, P `visible_mobs`. Trigger (`lambda$create$4`, 74–109):

```
c = visible_mobs.findClosest(predicate and (e -> mob.distanceToSqr(e) <= (double) maxDistSqr))
if c is empty: return false
if not ticker.tickDownAndCheck(level.getRandom()): return false
look_target = EntityTracker(c, true); return true

tickDownAndCheck(r):                                      # Ticker 24–50
    if ticksUntilNextStart == 0:
        ticksUntilNextStart = interval.sample(r) - 1; return false   # level draw
    ticksUntilNextStart -= 1
    return ticksUntilNextStart == 0
```

The ticker counts only on ticks where a candidate is in sight and no look target is set;
`UniformInt.sample(r)` is `Mth.randomBetweenInclusive(r, min, max)` = `r.nextInt(max −
min + 1) + min` (UniformInt.txt 30–38; Mth.txt in n5-javap 1932–1943): one draw. The line-of-sight test of the candidate runs before the ticker (7.1.3).

#### 7.3.8 `SetEntityLookTarget` (140 lines): one-shot

`create(category, maxDist)`, `create(type, maxDist)`, `create(maxDist)` (any). A
`look_target`, P `visible_mobs`. Trigger (`lambda$create$5`, 72–100): the closest visible
entity passing the predicate with `distanceToSqr <= (double) maxDistSqr` and **not a
passenger of the mob** (`!mob.hasPassenger(e)`, 102–118); `look_target =
EntityTracker(it, true)`; true. No ticker, no draw.

#### 7.3.9 `AnimalMakeLove(partnerType[, speed = 1.0, closeEnough = 2])` (333 lines): `Behavior`, 110 ticks

Memories (28–53): P `visible_mobs`, A `breed_target`, R `walk_target`, R `look_target`,
A `is_panicking`. Duration 110/110 (the level draw is `nextInt(1)`). State:
`spawnChildAtTime`.

```
checkExtraStartConditions = animal.isInLove() and findValidBreedPartner(animal) present

findValidBreedPartner(a) = visible_mobs.findClosest(e -> e.is(partnerType)
        and e instanceof Animal p and a.canMate(p) and not p.isPanicking())     # 240–332

start(level, a, t):                                       # 70–108
    p = findValidBreedPartner(a).get()
    a.breed_target = p; p.breed_target = a
    BehaviorUtils.lockGazeAndWalkToEachOther(a, p, speed, closeEnough)
    spawnChildAtTime = t + 60 + a.getRandom().nextInt(50)                       # own draw

canStillUse(level, a, t):                                 # 110–148
    a.breed_target present and of partnerType, p = it
    and p.isAlive() and a.canMate(p) and BehaviorUtils.entityIsVisible(a.brain, p)
    and t <= spawnChildAtTime and not a.isPanicking() and not p.isPanicking()

tick(level, a, t):                                        # 150–186
    p = breed_target
    lockGazeAndWalkToEachOther(a, p, speed, closeEnough)
    if not a.closerThan(p, 3.0): return
    if t >= spawnChildAtTime:
        a.spawnChildFromBreeding(level, p)
        erase a.breed_target; erase p.breed_target

stop: erase breed_target, walk_target, look_target (on a only); spawnChildAtTime = 0
```

`lockGazeAndWalkToEachOther(a, b, speed, d)` (BehaviorUtils.txt 9–146): `a.look_target =
EntityTracker(b, true)`, `b.look_target = EntityTracker(a, true)`, then for each of
(a→b) and (b→a): `look_target = EntityTracker(other, true)`, `walk_target =
WalkTarget(EntityTracker(other, true), speed, d)`. Since the partner's `breed_target` is
set, its own `AnimalMakeLove` cannot start: only the initiator runs it, and the partner
walks only because its walk target is set. A pair that is never within 3 blocks by
`spawnChildAtTime` stops (`t <= spawnChildAtTime` fails) without a child. `canMate`,
`isInLove`, `spawnChildFromBreeding` are `Animal`'s (the animals section's).

#### 7.3.10 `BabyFollowAdult` (131 lines): one-shot

`create(range, speed)` = `create(range, e -> speed, NEAREST_VISIBLE_ADULT, false)`.
`create(range, speedFn, memory, eyes)`: P `memory`, R `look_target`, A `walk_target`.
Trigger (`lambda$create$3`, 63–124): if `!mob.isBaby()`, false; `adult = memory`; if
`mob.closerThan(adult, range.max + 1)` and `!mob.closerThan(adult, range.min)`:
`look_target = EntityTracker(adult, true, eyes)`, `walk_target =
WalkTarget(EntityTracker(adult, eyes, eyes), speedFn(mob), range.min − 1)`; true. Else
false. No draws (the `UniformInt` is used only for its bounds).

#### 7.3.11 `FollowTemptation(speedFn[, closeEnoughFn = 2.5[, lookInTheEyes = false]])` (243 lines): `Behavior`

Memories (lambda 200–236): R `look_target`, R `walk_target`, A `temptation_cooldown_ticks`,
P `tempting_player`, A `breed_target`, A `is_panicking`. Duration 60/60, but `timedOut` is
always false (68–71): it runs as long as `canStillUse`. Constants: `TEMPTATION_COOLDOWN =
100`, `DEFAULT_CLOSE_ENOUGH_DIST = 2.5`, `BACKED_UP_CLOSE_ENOUGH_DIST = 3.5`.

- `canStillUse` (73–93): `tempting_player` present, `breed_target` and `is_panicking`
  absent.
- `start`: nothing.
- `tick` (113–168): `p = tempting_player`; `look_target = EntityTracker(p, true)`; if
  `mob.distanceToSqr(p) < Mth.square(closeEnough(mob))`, erase `walk_target`; else
  `walk_target = WalkTarget(EntityTracker(p, lookInTheEyes, lookInTheEyes),
  speedFn(mob), 2)`.
- `stop` (95–111): `temptation_cooldown_ticks = 100` (no expiry; counted down by
  `CountDownCooldownTicks`), erase `walk_target` and `look_target`.

Since the sensor refreshes `tempting_player` every 20 ticks, a player who puts the food
away is followed for up to 20 more ticks. No draws but the start's.

#### 7.3.12 `CountDownCooldownTicks(memory)` (78 lines): `Behavior`

P `memory`. Duration 60/60, `timedOut` always false. `canStillUse`: the memory is present
and `> 0`. `tick`: `memory = memory − 1` (a plain `setMemory`, so any expiry is dropped).
`stop`: erase. A cooldown of n set in tick T: started in tick T+1 (it was set after the
start pass of T, unless set by an earlier behaviour in T's start pass) and decremented in
the same tick; it reaches 0 after n decrements and is erased in the tick after. Each
restart costs a level draw.

#### 7.3.13 `AnimalPanic` (352 lines): `Behavior`, 100–120 ticks

Constructors (17–65): `(speed)` = damage tag `PANIC_CAUSES`, position
`LandRandomPos.getPos(mob, 5, 4)` (`lambda$new$0`, `$1`); `(speed, yOffset)` = the same
tag and `AirAndWaterRandomPos.getPos(mob, 5, 4, yOffset, view.x, view.z,
1.5707963705062866)` with `view = mob.getViewVector(0f)` (`lambda$new$2`, `$3`, 317–338);
`(speed, tagFn)` = position `LandRandomPos.getPos(mob, 5, 4)` (`lambda$new$4`). Memories:
R `is_panicking`, R `hurt_by`.

```
checkExtraStartConditions (67–91):
    (hurt_by present and hurt_by.is(tagFn(mob))) or is_panicking present
canStillUse = true                    # it runs its full 100–120 ticks
start (98–113): is_panicking = true; erase walk_target; navigation.stop()
tick (125–149):
    if navigation.isDone():
        p = getPanicPos(mob, level)
        if p != null: walk_target = WalkTarget(p, speed, 0)
stop (115–123): erase is_panicking

getPanicPos(mob, level) (151–175):
    if mob.isOnFire():
        w = lookForWater(level, mob).map(Vec3::atBottomCenterOf)   # Inferred method ref
        if w present: return w
    return positionFn(mob)

lookForWater(level, e) (177–212):
    pos = e.blockPosition()
    if level.getBlockState(pos).getCollisionShape(level, pos) is not empty: return empty
    m = level.findBlocksInBoxByManhattanDistance(pos, 5, 1).filterState(isWater)
    if Mth.ceil(e.getBbWidth()) == 2:
        return m.findFirst((p, s) -> water at p.south(), p.east() and p.south().east())
    return m.findFirst()
```

`isWater` is the fluid in `FluidTags.WATER` (214–220). The visiting order:
`findBlocksInBoxByManhattanDistance(pos, r[, ry])` is `findBlocksIn(BlockPos
.withinBoxByManhattanDistance(pos, r, ry, r))` (LevelReader.txt 376–396), an
`OrderedBlockMatcher` over that iterable; `withinBoxByManhattanDistance` is
`manhattanOrdered(pos, rx, ry, rz, rx + ry + rz)` (BlockPos.txt 781–814), whose iterator
is `BlockPos$3` (lambda 1564–1576), not dumped. **Inferred** from earlier versions'
source: positions by increasing Manhattan distance d = 0 … rx+ry+rz; within one d, x
from −min(rx, d) up, then y from −min(ry, d − |x|) up, then z = d − |x| − |y| (skipped
if above rz) and then its mirror −z; the first match wins (`findFirst`, OrderedBlockMatcher.txt in
n5-javap 92–135).
`DamageTypeTags.PANIC_CAUSES` (`tags/damage_type/panic_causes.json`): the
`panic_environmental_causes` tag (cactus, freeze, hot_floor, sulfur_cube_hot, in_fire,
lava, lightning_bolt, on_fire), arrow, dragon_breath, explosion, fireball, fireworks,
indirect_magic, magic, mob_attack, mob_projectile, player_explosion, sonic_boom, sting,
thrown, trident, unattributed_fireball, wind_charge, wither, wither_skull, and the
`is_player_attack` tag. Draws: the start's level draw (`nextInt(21)`), then each
position's own draws (7.3.3) on every tick where the navigation is done.

#### 7.3.14 `Swim(chance[, fluid = ENTITY_FLOATABLE])` (95 lines): `Behavior`, 60 ticks

No memories. `checkExtraStartConditions` and `canStillUse` (28–51):
`mob.isInFluidDeeperThan(mob.getFluidJumpThreshold(), fluid) || mob.isInLava()`.
`tick` (53–65): `if mob.getRandom().nextFloat() < chance: mob.getJumpControl().jump()`.
So while afloat: one own draw every tick, and a level draw at each start; it times out
after 61 ticks of running and restarts the tick after, so one tick in 62 has no swim draw.
`FluidTags.ENTITY_FLOATABLE` is `#minecraft:water`.

#### 7.3.15 `TryFindLiquid`, `TryFindLand`, `TryFindLandNearLiquid`: one-shots

Each keeps a `MutableLong next` (0) in its closure, per behaviour object.

- **`TryFindLiquid.create(range, speed, fluidTag)`** (TryFindLiquid.txt): A
  `attack_target`, A `walk_target`, R `look_target`. Trigger (`lambda$create$2`,
  57–135): if the fluid at `mob.blockPosition()` is in the tag, false. If `t < next`:
  `next = t + 20 + 2`; true (so the search waits, and each waiting tick re-arms the
  wait). Else: search `level.findBlocksInBoxByManhattanDistance(mob.blockPosition(),
  range)`, excluding positions in the mob's own column (`differsHorizontally`), for
  states that are a `LiquidBlock` with fluid in the tag; visiting in order (`forEachUntil`,
  `lambda$create$5`, 137–167): a position with **air above** is taken and the search
  stops; otherwise the first position not within 1.5 of the mob (`closerToCenterThan`) is
  kept as a fallback while searching on. If one was found: `look_target =
  BlockPosTracker(p)`, `walk_target = WalkTarget(BlockPosTracker(p), speed, 0)`. `next =
  t + 40`; true.
- **`TryFindLand.create(range, speed)`** (TryFindLand.txt): same memories. Trigger
  (81–139): if the fluid at the mob's position is **not** water, false. If `t < next`:
  `next = t + 60`; true. Else search the Manhattan box, not the own column, states whose
  fluid is empty, for the first `canStandOn` (25–48: the state's collision shape for the
  mob's `CollisionContext` is empty and the block below `isFaceSturdy(UP)`); if found,
  `look_target = BlockPosTracker(p)`, `walk_target = WalkTarget(BlockPosTracker(p),
  speed, 1)`. `next = t + 60`; true.
- **`TryFindLandNearLiquid.create(range, speed, fluidTag)`** (TryFindLandNearLiquid.txt):
  same memories. Trigger (57–114): if the fluid at the mob's position is in the tag,
  false. If `t < next`: `next = t + 40`; true. Else the first position in the box, not
  the own column, whose collision shape is empty, the block below has a non-empty
  collision shape, and some horizontal neighbour (north, east, south, west) is air with
  the block below it holding fluid in the tag (140–198); `look_target` and `walk_target
  (speed, 0)` as above. `next = t + 40`; true.

None draws. The visiting order is the Manhattan order of 7.3.13 (nearest first; the
order within one distance **Inferred**, `BlockPos$3` not dumped).

#### 7.3.16 `LongJumpToRandomPos` (595 lines) with `$PossibleJump` and `LongJumpUtil` (296): `Behavior`, 200 ticks

Constructor `(timeBetweenJumps: UniformInt, maxHeight, maxWidth, maxVelocityMultiplier:
float, soundFn[, landingPredicate])` (35–109); the default landing predicate is
`defaultAcceptableLandingSpot` (47–71): the block below is `isSolidRender` and the
position's path type has malus 0. Memories: R `look_target`, A
`long_jump_cooling_down`, A `long_jump_mid_jump`. Duration 200/200. Constants:
`FIND_JUMP_TRIES = 20`, `PREPARE_JUMP_DURATION = 40`, `MIN_PATHFIND_DISTANCE_TO_VALID_JUMP
= 8`, `ALLOWED_ANGLES = [65, 70, 75, 80]` (568–594). State: `jumpCandidates`,
`initialPosition`, `chosenJump`, `findJumpTries`, `prepareJumpStart`.

```
checkExtraStartConditions (111–148):
    ok = mob.onGround() and not inWater and not inLava
         and the block at mob.blockPosition() is not honey_block
    if not ok: long_jump_cooling_down = timeBetweenJumps.sample(level.getRandom()) / 2
    return ok

start (208–270):
    chosenJump = null; findJumpTries = 20; initialPosition = mob.position()
    o = mob.blockPosition()
    jumpCandidates = [PossibleJump(p, Mth.ceil(o.distSqr(p)))
                      for p in BlockPos.betweenClosedStream(o.x - w, o.y - h, o.z - w,
                                                            o.x + w, o.y + h, o.z + w)
                      if p != o]                                   # lambdas 544–566

canStillUse (150–206):
    running = initialPosition present and equal to mob.position() and findJumpTries > 0
              and not mob.isInWater() and (chosenJump != null or jumpCandidates not empty)
    if not running and long_jump_mid_jump absent:
        long_jump_cooling_down = timeBetweenJumps.sample(level.getRandom()) / 2
        erase look_target
    return running

tick (272–339):
    if chosenJump != null:
        if t - prepareJumpStart >= 40:
            mob.setYRot(mob.yBodyRot); mob.setDiscardFriction(true)
            len = chosenJump.length(); boosted = len + (double) mob.getJumpBoostPower()
            mob.setDeltaMovement(chosenJump.scale(boosted / len))
            long_jump_mid_jump = true
            level.playSound(null, mob, soundFn(mob), NEUTRAL, 1.0, 1.0)
    else:
        findJumpTries -= 1; pickCandidate(level, mob, t)

pickCandidate (341–410):
    while jumpCandidates not empty:
        c = WeightedRandom.getRandomItem(level.getRandom(), jumpCandidates, PossibleJump::weight)
        if c present: jumpCandidates.remove(c)              # (getJumpCandidate, 412–430)
        else: continue
        p = c.targetPos
        if p has the mob's own x and z, or not landingPredicate(mob, p): continue
        v = calculateOptimalJumpVector(mob, Vec3.atCenterOf(p))
        if v == null: continue
        look_target = BlockPosTracker(p)
        path = navigation.createPath(p, 0, 8)
        if path == null or not path.canReach():
            chosenJump = v; prepareJumpStart = t; return
        # reachable on foot within the search: not worth a jump; try another

calculateOptimalJumpVector(mob, target) (460–503):
    angles = copy of [65, 70, 75, 80]; Collections.shuffle(angles)   # JDK global random
    maxV = (float)(mob.getAttributeValue(JUMP_STRENGTH) * (double) maxVelocityMultiplier)
    for a in angles:
        v = LongJumpUtil.calculateJumpVectorForAngle(mob, target, maxV, a, true)
        if v present: return v
    return null
```
